chunks.title: Give to Landmark Church | Online Giving & Donations
chunks.text: Support God's work at Landmark Church. Give online, by cash, check, or serve with your gifts. Your generosity fuels ministry and missions locally and globally.

chunks.title: Give to Landmark Church | Online Giving & Donations
chunks.text: Give to What God Is DoingWays To GiveWays To GiveWays To GiveWays to GiveGive Through Time, Talent, and TreasureGive OnlineMake giving easy. Give one-time or set up a recurring gift using Church Center.Give NowGive NowGive NowCashLook for one of our offering drop boxes located around our sanctuary building at any of the doors.CheckMake it out to Landmark Church and drop your check in any of our offering boxes onsite, or mail it to 300 E. 8th Street, Ocean City, NJ 08226.ServingPart of giving is serving with the gifts God gave you. Join a team and put your gifts to use!Find a TeamFind a TeamFind a TeamWhy GiveStewarding Every DollarPreviousPreviousNextNextMinistry of GivingBiblical stewardship invites us to joyfully invest our time, talent, and treasure for God’s purposes. The parable of the talents and Romans 12 remind us that our gifts are intentional and meant to be used faithfully for His glory and the good of the Church.Where We Prioritize FundsWe steward every dollar with intention—supporting our staff and investing in ministries like family life, care, benevolence, missions, and partnerships that help advance the gospel.How Your Giving Makes an ImpactYour generosity fuels life change—helping people grow in their faith, supporting those in need, and extending the reach of the gospel both locally and around the world.FAQsAnswers to popular quesitons regarding giving at Landmark.How is my donation used?Church donations typically support ministry operations, staff, outreach programs, missions, facility upkeep, and community assistance. Many churches provide financial transparency through reports or updates.Do I have to tithe a specific percentage?Many churches teach tithing (traditionally 10%) as a biblical principle, but giving is ultimately a personal decision. It should be done willingly, cheerfully, and according to one’s ability.How can I give to the church?Our church offers several ways to give, including in-person offerings, online giving platforms, mobile apps, mail-in donations, or recurring automated giving.Why is giving important in the church?Giving is an act of worship and gratitude. It’s a simple way we create space for connection, conversation, and community—whether you're catching up with a friend or meeting someone new for the first time.WorshipLearn MoreLearn MoreLearn MoreCloseCloseWorshipEach service kicks off with about 20 minutes of live, contemporary worship led by our team. The music is energetic and immersive—fuller than background music, but not overwhelming—creating a powerful space to engage with God. Lyrics are displayed on large screens so you can easily follow along, whether you're singing out, raising your hands, or simply taking it in. Our heart is to create an atmosphere where worship feels natural, meaningful, and deeply personal.‍Meet & GreetLearn MoreLearn MoreLearn MoreCloseCloseMeet & GreetUsually near the beginning of service we take a brief moment to greet those around us—a simple but meaningful way to spark connection and make everyone feel seen and welcomed. Whether it’s a warm handshake, a smile, or a quick hello, our hope is that you’ll feel like part of the family from the very start.AnnouncementsLearn MoreLearn MoreLearn MoreCloseCloseAnnouncementsSometime during service, one of our team members will take a moment to welcome new guests and present them with a free new guest bag—filled with helpful info and a few gifts to help you get started at Landmark. The messages are designed to help you grow in your relationship with God—offering both encouragement and challenge. We also take time to address relevant topics and cultural issues through the lens of a biblical worldview, helping you navigate life with truth and clarity.If you could describe our speaking style it would be: Passionate / Engaging / Earnest / Practical / ConvictingCurious what a sermon is like? Watch one here.After ServiceLearn MoreLearn MoreLearn MoreCloseCloseAfter ServiceThere’s no rush to leave after service—we’d love for you to stick around! It’s a great time to grab another coffee, connect with others, meet new faces, and chat with our pastors or staff. Whether you have questions, need prayer, or just want to feel more at home, we’re here for you.KidsLandmark Kids is a fun, safe environment where preschool–5th grade children learn the Bible through worship and interactive lessons, growing in faith in an age-appropriate way.Learn About KidsLearn About KidsLearn About KidsPre-Register for Check-InPre-Register for Check-InPre-Register for Check-InYouthLandmark Youth is a welcoming community where students build friendships, grow in faith, and follow Jesus through worship, teaching, and small groups.Learn About YouthLearn About YouthLearn About Youth

chunks.title: Mission & Beliefs | Landmark Church Ocean City, NJ
chunks.text: Discover Landmark Church's biblical mission and core beliefs. A Christ-centered community in Ocean City, NJ committed to living out the Gospel daily.

chunks.title: Mission & Beliefs | Landmark Church Ocean City, NJ
chunks.text: Mission & BeliefsAboutGrounded in a Biblical WorldviewLandmark Church is a Bible-based, Christ-centered community of believers in Ocean City, NJ, committed to living out the Great Commission. We aim to represent Jesus not just on Sundays, but in our everyday lives—at work, at home, and in our community. Our mission is to be a landmark of hope and truth, built on Scripture and shining God’s light to the world around us.We engage real-life issues, cultural conversations, and tough topics with grace and boldness—always grounded in a biblical worldview. Like a city on a hill, we want our lives to reflect God’s love and truth so others are drawn to Him.Our HistoryTracing Our Roots Back to 199119911991Maranatha By The SeaLandmark Church traces its roots back to 1991, when the church was founded as *Maranatha by the Sea*. Throughout the years, the church has experienced several name changes while remaining committed to the same mission: proclaiming the gospel, making disciples, and serving our community.20012001Calvary Chapel Ocean City20112011Coastal Christian Ocean City20232023Rebranded as Landmark Church PresentPresentLandmark Church TodayToday, Landmark Church serves the Ocean City community and beyond, welcoming more than 650 people each week on campus, while hundreds more join us online. With a dedicated staff team and faithful volunteers, ministry takes place both on-site and throughout the community seven days a week.DNAWhat Makes Landmark, Landmark.PreviousPreviousNextNextThe church is the redeemed people of God, centered on the life, death, and resurrection of Jesus.Every program, sermon, hiring, and decision must center on the Gospel as our defining reality.Scripture is the final authority in all matters of faith and practice.All policies, decisions, and teachings must submit to God’s Word, not pragmatism or culture.Church leaders are servant-shepherds who follow the example of Christ.‍Leadership hiring, appointing, and evaluation must prioritize biblical qualifications (character, teaching, and shepherding ability) above management style or competency. Those with professional leadership experience are a gift to the church when their abilities are shaped by biblical servant-leadership.The church exists to make and equip disciples of all nations by Gospel proclamation by the power of the Holy Spirit.Every ministry must align with this mission. Success is measured in faithfulness and fruitfulness in discipleship.The church exists to make and equip disciples of all nations by Gospel proclamation by the power of the Holy Spirit.Every ministry must align with this mission. Success is measured in faithfulness and fruitfulness in discipleship.The church is a covenant family not a consumer-driven organization.Church discipline, staff relationships, and membership (Landmark Covenant), must be guided by biblical accountability and love. ‍The church is called to be holy as God is holy, marked by repentance and restoration.Staff discipline is an act of faithfulness, not failure, when done biblically and redemptively.The church exists to equip all believers to minister, not to entertain or create spectators.All programs and ministries must be designed to develop disciples. In addition to our responsibility to the congregation, staff members themselves must also be equipped and actively discipled. Our ministry philosophy is based on the intentional replication of disciples of Jesus—beginning within the staff and extending to the body.‍The church must steward the faith for the next generation through teaching, modeling, and entrusting.Hiring and vision casting should prioritize the continuity of the faith, not just innovation, trend, or cultural relevance.Faithfulness to Christ includes enduring suffering and carrying the cross.Staff expectations must include perseverance and humility, not entitlement.The church, as one body under the headship of Christ, exists to glorify God, not to elevate leaders, preserve traditions, or pursue numerical success.Decision-making, platform-building, and vision casting must reject self-promotion, brand promotion, and the pursuit of influence for its own sake.Experience It for YourselfThe best way to understand what we believe is to see it lived out—join us this Sunday and be part of a service.Plan your visitPlan your visitPlan your visitLearn What We BelieveLandmark 101Dive deeper into our mission, beliefs, and how you can get connected through Landmark 101.View Upcoming ClassesView Upcoming ClassesView Upcoming Classes

Something went wrong while submitting the form.Contact InformationOffice300 E. 8th Street, Ocean City, NJ 08226HoursMonday8am - 5pmContacthello@thelandmark.churchhello@thelandmark.churchhello@thelandmark.church609-399-4747609-399-4747609-399-4747FAQsLorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.How can I become a Marriage Mentor?We’re always looking for couples who have a desire to invest in and encourage other marriages. Marriage mentors participate in training and are equipped with the tools and resources needed to walk alongside couples well.If you’re interested in becoming a Marriage Mentor, fill out the Marriage Mentor interest form or contact our Care Team to learn about upcoming training opportunities and the process for getting involved.‍How do we get started?Getting started is simple! If you are engaged and interested in Premarital Mentoring, complete the premarital questionnaire form and our team will follow up with you about the next steps.If you are already married and interested in Marriage Coaching or Counseling, complete the marital coaching application form. We’ll connect with you to learn more about what you’re looking for and help determine the best next step for your marriage.‍Who are the marriage mentors and coaches?Our marriage mentors are trained couples from our church who have a heart for helping others build healthy, Christ-centered marriages. They come from a variety of life experiences and are equipped to listen, encourage, ask good questions, and walk alongside couples through the mentoring process.Marriage coaching and counseling is provided by members of our Care Team and other trusted, qualified individuals within our church ministry.‍What is the difference between Premarital Mentoring and Marriage Coaching?Our Premarital Mentoring program is designed for engaged couples who are preparing for marriage. Couples are paired with trained marriage mentors and walk through a guided process that helps them build a strong foundation for their marriage.Marriage Coaching and Counseling is available for couples who are already married. Whether you’re looking to strengthen a healthy marriage, work through a specific challenge, or simply grow together, our team is here to walk alongside you.‍Do you have to be a paid staff member to be an elder and are all the pastors considered elders?The Bible does not require an elder to be a paid staff member, nor does it prohibit financial support for those serving in eldership when necessary (1 Timothy 5:17-18; 1 Corinthians 9:11). At Landmark, both staff and non-staff men may serve as elders provided they meet the biblical qualifications and can fulfill the responsibilities of the office.‍Landmark also recognizes pastors who may have been ordained by other ministries and serve in various pastoral capacities. However, pastoral ordination received elsewhere does not automatically confer governing authority within Landmark Church. Governing eldership at Landmark is determined by the existing elder board through the church's elder evaluation and appointment process.‍Men ordained as pastors by Landmark are recognized as elders according to the qualifications and functions described in Scripture. As a general practice, ordination by Landmark includes installation into the office of elder, having already completed the church's elder evaluation, vetting, and approval process.‍Service on the governing elder board, including voting authority and legal responsibilities, ordinarily accompanies eldership. However, in certain circumstances, the elder board may determine that a different arrangement is appropriate due to unique ministry, legal, or practical considerations.‍Because eldership carries responsibility for the doctrine, direction, and discipline of the church, the final determination of governing eldership rests with the existing plurality of elders. In the case of non-staff elders, they must also have the time and availability necessary to fulfill the oversight responsibilities and meeting requirements established by the elder board.How many elders should make up a board and do they serve for life?The Bible does not give a specific number of elders that should serve a given community nor does it specify term limits. Each church body differs and should exercise wisdom in determining how many elders would be sufficient to effectively lead the church, as well as how long. The team of elders at Landmark collectively oversee the affairs of the church and make these determinations.‍Do you also do Palm Sunday and Good Friday services?Yes, we do! Palm Sunday service is the Sunday before Easter. We also typically cancel our regular Wednesday night service (during the week between Palm Sunday and Easter Sunday) and replace it with a special Good Friday service on the Friday before Easter.What is Easter Sunday like at Landmark?It's the biggest Sunday of the year. Expect worship, the resurrection story, and a community that actually believes it. Plan for about 90 minutes.I haven't been to church in a while. Is this for me?Yes. Christmas Eve at Landmark is for everyone. First-timers, longtime members, skeptics and seekers. Come as you are.Where are you located?300 E. 8th St, Ocean City, NJ 08226. Find service info and directions at thelandmark.church.Do I need to register?No registration required. Just show up! But make sure to allow yourself 20 minutes before service starts to park and find seating.What if I don't see my question listed?If you have a question that isn’t listed above, please reach out to us at finance@thelandmark.church.Should I redirect my regular tithes and contributions to this initiative?We are asking that you prayerfully consider giving to the initiative in addition to, not instead of, your regular tithes and contributions to our general fund.Do you accept other contributions besides cash, check, or credit card payments?Yes we do! Visit ways to give and scroll down for “Other Ways to Give.”Are gifts to the Legacy Initiative tax deductible?Yes, your contributions to this initiative are tax deductible because we are a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization.How can I view or modify my contribution(s)?Follow these steps to view or modify your contributions:Go here and log into your Church Center profileScroll to the bottom and look for “My Giving” and click/tap on itRecurring Donations: If you have a recurring donation set up, navigate to “Recurring Donations” and click or tap the pencil icon to edit that donationDonation History: If you’re looking for donation history you can find that under the “Donation History” tab.Payment Method: Looking to add or change your payment method? Use the “Payment Method” tab.‍How did we come to the conclusion on cost?The cost was derived from a mixture of hard costs (like our mortgage and equipment costs) and renovation estimates from trustworthy advisors within our church.How can I find out more information?We’ll be updating our congregation from time to time with updates along this journey. In the meantime, if you have a specific question, you can reach out to us at finance@thelandmark.church.Can I suggest someone for a future episode?Yes. If you know someone whose story deserves to be heard, reach out at hello@thelandmark.churchWhere can I watch episodes & past events?Every episode is free at thelandmark.church/landmark-stories and on the Landmark Church YouTube channel. New episodes drop regularly — follow @thelandmark.church on Instagram to know when.Do I need to go to Landmark Church to go to a live event?No. Show up. See what it's about.What happens at a live event?A live Landmark Stories event is exactly what it sounds like: a real conversation, in person, with someone whose story is worth showing up for. No big production. No pressure. Just a room full of people and something honest happening in front of them.Is this a church thing?Landmark Stories is produced by Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ. But the conversations stand on their own — you don't need to believe anything to watch. You just have to be willing to listen.Who are the people you interview & host?All kinds. Athletes. Leaders. People who've walked through addiction, loss, identity, career collapse, grief. The common thread isn't their background — it's that something happened they didn't see coming, and it changed them.What is Landmark Stories?It's a long-form video interview & live event series — real conversations with real people about the moments that defined them. Think less panel discussion, more honest one-on-one. We've sat down with NFL players, fire chiefs, worship leaders, and people you might know from down the street in Ocean City. Free to watch at thelandmark.church/landmark-stories.Do I have to attend Landmark Church to join Young Adults?Not at all. Young Adults is open to everyone, whether you've been attending Landmark for years or you've never walked through our doors. Come as you are.What can I expect to get out of Young Adults?That depends on what you put in. Young Adults at Landmark is built around three things: gatherings, D-Groups, and activities. The more you engage, the more it gives back. Real relationships, real growth, real community.What should I bring to a Young Adults gathering?Just bring yourself, a Bible, and an empty stomach. We'll handle the rest.When and where does Young Adults meet?We meet once a month at the Landmark Cafe — 710 Asbury Ave, Ocean City, NJ from 6:30-8:30 PM. What is the age range for Young Adults at Landmark Church?Young Adults at Landmark Church is open to anyone ages 18–29. Do I need to bring anything?We encourage students to bring their Bibles and journals to youth group. If you don’t have a Bible yet or happen to forget yours, don’t worry, we have extras.Do I need to register my child for Youth Group?No registration is required for our weekly youth gatherings—just show up, and we’ll get you checked in! Occasionally, registration will be required for offsite events or camp, and we will clearly communicate when that’s needed.How can I keep up with what’s happening in Landmark Youth?We use a Clearstream text thread to keep parents and students up to date on everything happening in Landmark Youth. Simply text landmarkyouth to 609-566-8450 to join. We encourage both parents and students to sign up so everyone stays informed!What is a Support group?Support groups provide a safe, caring space to walk through life’s challenges with others who understand and can encourage you.What is an Activity group?Activity groups bring people together around shared interests, creating a relaxed environment to build relationships and community.What is a Discipleship Group?A discipleship group is a weekly gathering focused on growing in your faith through Scripture, discussion, and accountability with others.Do I need to go to all three areas when I visit?Not at all—our team will help guide you based on your needs, whether you’re attending a service, checking in kids, or just connecting with others.What is Landmark Cafe?The Landmark Cafe is a space to connect, relax, and build relationships before and after services or throughout the week.What is the Family Life Center used for?The Family Life Center is home to kids, youth, and family-focused environments throughout the week.What happens in the Sanctuary?The Sanctuary is where we gather for worship services, teaching, and church-wide gatherings.What spaces are part of the Landmark campus?Our campus includes the Sanctuary, Family Life Center, and Landmark Café—each designed to support different parts of church life.How can I get connected?You can start by attending, joining a group, or taking Landmark 101.Do I need to sign up before visiting?No, but planning your visit ahead of time can help make your first experience smoother.What should I wear to church?Come as you are—people dress casually and comfortably.What should I expect on a Sunday or Wednesday?You’ll experience worship, biblical teaching, and a welcoming environment for individuals and families.Where is Landmark Church located?You can find directions and campus details on our campus page to help plan your visit.Can I get involved with a partner ministry?Yes—there are opportunities throughout the year to support or participate in outreach efforts.How does Landmark support these partners?Through financial support, prayer, and in some cases, hands-on involvement like missions trips.How do you choose your partners?We partner with trusted ministries that demonstrate strong leadership, biblical alignment, and meaningful impact.What does it mean to be a partner?We partner with ministries that align with our mission to share the gospel and serve people locally and globally.What kinds of classes are offered?Classes vary each session and may include academic, creative, and enrichment opportunities.When does the Co-Op meet?Co-Op runs in seasonal sessions (typically Fall and Spring).Do parents need to be involved?Yes—Co-Op is a shared community, and parents play an active role in helping and supporting classes.What ages can participate in the Co-Op?Our Co-Op serves homeschool families with children across a range of grade levels (details vary by session).Do I need to know a lot about the Bible to join?Not at all—groups are for everyone, no matter where you are in your faith journey.What types of groups are available?We offer discipleship groups, support groups, and activity-based groups for different interests and needs.When do groups meet?Most groups meet during Fall and Spring semesters, with some continuing year-round depending on the group.How do I join a group?You can browse available groups and join one that fits your schedule and stage of life.Can I talk to an elder?Yes—our elders are available to pray, offer guidance, and care for members of our church.How are elders chosen?Elders are selected based on biblical qualifications, character, and a proven track record of leadership and faithfulness.What’s the difference between a pastor and an elder?Pastors typically serve in full-time ministry, while elders provide broader oversight—though both are held to the same biblical qualifications.What do elders do at Landmark Church?Elders provide spiritual oversight, helping guide the church’s direction, doctrine, and care for the congregation.How is my donation used?Church donations typically support ministry operations, staff, outreach programs, missions, facility upkeep, and community assistance. Many churches provide financial transparency through reports or updates.Do I have to tithe a specific percentage?Many churches teach tithing (traditionally 10%) as a biblical principle, but giving is ultimately a personal decision. It should be done willingly, cheerfully, and according to one’s ability.How can I give to the church?Our church offers several ways to give, including in-person offerings, online giving platforms, mobile apps, mail-in donations, or recurring automated giving.Why is giving important in the church?Giving is an act of worship and gratitude. It supports the church’s mission, helps those in need, and allows ministry programs, outreach, and community services to continue.How can I get involved?You can join by attending a meeting or event, signing up for a small group, volunteering, or reaching out to a ministry leader for more details.What kinds of activities are offered?The ministry may include Bible studies, mentorship programs, prayer groups, service projects, retreats, and fellowship events like breakfasts or group outings.Who can participate in the Men’s Ministry?All men are welcome—regardless of age, background, or where they are in their faith journey. It’s a space for growth, accountability, and connection.What is the purpose of the Men’s Ministry?The Men’s Ministry exists to help men grow spiritually, develop strong character, and build authentic relationships while encouraging them through fellowship, to live out their faith in everyday life.How can I get involved?You can get involved by attending events, joining a small group, volunteering for service projects, or contacting a ministry leader for more information.What types of activities does the ministry offer?Activities may include Bible studies, prayer groups, retreats, workshops, community outreach, and social gatherings designed to strengthen faith and friendships.Who can join the Women’s Ministry?All women are welcome, regardless of age, background, or stage in their faith. The ministry is a place for connection, learning, and encouragement.What is the purpose of the Women’s Ministry?The purpose of the Women’s Ministry is to encourage spiritual growth, build meaningful relationships, and support women in their faith journey through fellowship, study, and service.What do I do if my child has allergies?We understand that allergies can be a concern for parents. Each classroom has an iPad with a class roster that includes medical notes. If your child has allergies, a yellow alert icon will appear next to their name to notify leaders.We typically provide simple snacks such as Cheerios and pretzels. Gluten-free options are also available. If your child has additional allergies or dietary restrictions, you are welcome to send a snack with them.‍How do I know what my child is being taught?You can view your child’s curriculum through the Church Center app by selecting Study and then Curriculum. Children in Preschool through 3rd grade also receive a weekly take-home coloring sheet that includes the lesson's Christ connection, weekly Bible passage, and more.‍What safety measures are in place?All volunteers are background-checked and complete a Child Safety Training every two years. The Family Life Center is equipped with security cameras, and has at least two security team members on duty during services.We also follow strict bathroom policies: two adults are always present. For younger children who need assistance, one volunteer helps while another stands at the door. If you do not want us to assist your child in the restroom, just let us know and we can update your child’s profile. ‍What age can my baby start attending Landmark Kids?We recommend waiting until your baby is around 6 months old before dropping them off in the nursery. However, you are welcome to use your discretion and bring them earlier if you feel comfortable.A nursing room is also available upstairs in the main sanctuary for moms to utilize during service. ‍I’m new, what do I need to know?Landmark Kids meets in the Family Life Center (833 West Ave) on Sundays and Wednesdays. While the building is separate from the main sanctuary, it’s just a short walk away.Pre-registration is not required. If you’d like to save time, you can download the Church Center app, select Landmark Church, and enter your family’s information ahead of time, including your child’s grade and any medical notes or allergies. If not, no worries, we’ll have someone on-site to assist you when you arrive.At check-in, your child will receive a name tag with a security number, and you’ll receive a matching tag for pickup. If we need to contact you during service, a Family Life Team member will send you a text. If we don’t hear back, your security number will be displayed on the screen, prompting you to come to the Family Life Center.‍Can I choose which age group or role I serve in?Yes—during the onboarding process, we help determine the best fit based on your gifting, availability, and preference.‍What is a D-Group Leader?A D-Group Leader invests in a smaller group of students through ongoing discipleship, meeting outside regular gatherings for deeper growth and accountability.‍How often do Youth Leaders serve?Leaders typically serve weekly in their assigned environment to build consistency and strong relationships with students.‍Do I need experience to serve in Youth Ministry?No prior experience is required—just a heart for students and a willingness to build relationships and grow as a leader.‍What does a Youth Leader actually do?Youth Leaders build relationships with students, lead small group discussions, encourage participation, and help students grow in their faith.‍What’s the difference between Jr. High and Sr. High Youth?Jr. High (6th–8th grade) meets Wednesday nights in a high-energy, relational environment, while Sr. High (9th–12th) meets Sunday nights with a focus on deeper discipleship and ownership.‍Why should I serve on the Kids Team?To be an instrument through which God’s Word shapes the hearts and minds of the next generation. We have the opportunity every Sunday and Wednesday to make the most of the 90 minutes we have with them and make every minute count whether it be through intentional play and fellowship, worship, lesson time and more. ‍What is our mission on the Landmark Kids team?From nursery to high school, our mission is to disciple students by saturating them in the Word of God and modeling through our actions what it means to be Christlike. Through intentional methods, sound curriculum, and creativity, we seek to educate, equip, and embolden our youth so that they may share the good news of Christ our Savior.How often can I serve?Outreach happens on select days each month, and you can join based on your availability.‍Do I need experience to serve on the Lost + Found team?No—just a willing heart to serve, connect with people, and show kindness.‍Where does outreach typically take place?Outreach typically takes place in Atlantic City and surrounding areas where there are real, practical needs. ‍What do we do during outreach?We provide food, clothing, supplies, and connection while also sharing the hope of Jesus through conversation and prayer. ‍What is Lost + Found?Lost + Found is our outreach ministry focused on serving those who are struggling, lost, or in need in our local community. ‍Is this only for crises?No, care also includes encouragement, prayer, and ongoing support in everyday life.‍How often do I serve?Many roles are flexible and based on needs as they arise.‍Can I serve in specific areas only?Yes, you can choose one or more areas based on your availability and comfort level.‍What does the care team do?The Care Team supports people in our church through prayer, meals, visits, and practical help during life’s needs.Do I need prior experience to serve on the care team?Some of the roles like meals & rides don't require any prior experience, just a willingness to care for others. Other roles like marriage mentors & visitation may require prior experience and training.Is this a good team for new volunteers?Yes, it’s a great place to get your feet wet and start serving!‍When do I serve on the first impressions team?During Sunday and Wednesday gatherings.‍Do I need prior experience to join the first impressions team?No—just a friendly attitude and willingness to serve!‍Can't find what you're looking for?Contact UsContact UsContact Us

chunks.text: Join the Landmark Covenant—a commitment to grow as a disciple through worship, groups, serving, and giving. Learn about membership at Landmark Church.

chunks.title: Church Membership | Landmark Covenant | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Become a Church MemberWhat is Landmark Covenant?Commitment to GrowthWhat Landmark Covenant IsLandmark CovenantA covenant to steward your time, talent, treasure, and trouble for God’s kingdomA call to active participation—through worship, serving, groups, and givingA spiritual agreement between you and Landmark Church to walk in unity, holiness, and accountabilityA reflection of biblical values lived out in communityVoluntary, heartfelt, and grace-filledWhat Landmark Covenant Is NotA traditional church membership with voting rightsA social membership or club-style affiliationA passive or name-only membership statusA contractual agreement with perks, entitlements, or institutional benefitsA list of rules or religious performance expectationsObligatory or tied to pressure or controlAbout the Landmark CovenantThe Landmark Covenant is a commitment to grow as a disciple of Jesus by actively engaging in the life and mission of Landmark Church. Find your place to serve at Landmark Church. Explore volunteer teams in Kids, Youth, Worship, Care, Production, and more. Use your gifts to make an impact.

chunks.title: Serve at Landmark Church | Volunteer Opportunities
chunks.text: What Team Members Are SayingReady to Visit in Person?We’d love to welcome you. Plan your visit and experience Landmark firsthand—from worship to community.Plan Your VisitPlan Your VisitPlan Your VisitGroupsFind Your CommunityDon’t walk alone—join a group where you can find support, build relationships, and grow in your faith.View GroupsView GroupsView GroupsFAQsFind answers to common questions about serving, getting involved, and finding the right place to use your gifts at Landmark Church.How often do Youth Leaders serve?Leaders typically serve weekly in their assigned environment to build consistency and strong relationships with students.‍What does a Youth Leader actually do?Youth Leaders build relationships with students, lead small group discussions, encourage participation, and help students grow in their faith.‍Why should I serve on the Kids Team?To be an instrument through which God’s Word shapes the hearts and minds of the next generation. We have the opportunity every Sunday and Wednesday to make the most of the 90 minutes we have with them and make every minute count whether it be through intentional play and fellowship, worship, lesson time and more. ‍Do I need experience to serve on the Lost + Found team?No—just a willing heart to serve, connect with people, and show kindness.‍What is Lost + Found?Lost + Found is our outreach ministry focused on serving those who are struggling, lost, or in need in our local community. ‍What does the care team do?The Care Team supports people in our church through prayer, meals, visits, and practical help during life’s needs.Do I need prior experience to serve on the care team?Some of the roles like meals & rides don't require any prior experience, just a willingness to care for others. Other roles like marriage mentors & visitation may require prior experience and training.What does the first impressions team do?We welcome guests, assist with seating, and create a positive environment through hospitality (i.e. coffee, donuts, etc), security, and cleaning.‍What roles are available on the creative & photography team?Photography, video, design, and social media.‍What roles are available on the production team?Camera, lighting, sound, computer graphics, and more!Can't find what you're looking for?Contact UsContact UsContact Us

chunks.title: Co-Op | Landmark Church Homeschool Community
chunks.text: Join a Christ-centered homeschool co-op offering supplemental classes, biblical integration, and community support for families in Ocean City, NJ.

chunks.title: Co-Op | Landmark Church Homeschool Community
chunks.text: Co-OpThe MissionProviding homeschooled families with a Christ-centered community that fosters academic, spiritual, and relational growth.FocusWhy Landmark Believes in Co-OpCurious what Co-Op is like? View our parent-uploaded content.View Co-Op ContentView Co-Op ContentView Co-Op ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextHomeschooling is a powerful way for parents to teach their children, but it can feel isolating. Co-Op gives families a place to connect.We believe that education isn’t just academics — it’s discipleship. Co-Op gives students the chance to learn with biblical values in a relational environment.Kids benefit from multiple perspectives: clients, teachers, peers. Co-Op allows them to develop socially and academically in ways that enrich what parents are already doing at home.It aligns with our church’s bigger vision: building community, equipping believers, and cultivating disciples who know how to think critically and walk in faith.How To JoinJoin Co-OpUse this roadmap as a guide to heading toward covenant with us.PreviousPreviousNextNext01Review the Covenant & Statement of FaithMake sure it aligns with your beliefs and how you want your child to grow spiritually.View CovenantView CovenantView Covenant02Fill Out Our Interest FormShare your family information, class interests, and whether you’d like to teach or help.Express InterestExpress InterestExpress Interest03Attend an Orientation (if applicable)Meet the leaders, learn about the classes, and understand expectations.04Commit for the SeasonCo-Op runs in sessions (fall/spring). Make the commitment so we can plan well.Why Co-OpBenefits of Co-OpCommunity & ConnectionKids and parents make friendships, share experiences, encourage one another, and never have to journey alone.Supplemental ClassesWe offer classes that enhance your child’s education—without replacing homeschooling—focusing especially on areas where group settings add value (science labs, arts, etc.).Biblical IntegrationEvery class, every interaction, is grounded in biblical truth. We don’t just teach subjects—we model Christ-like character.Family FlexibilityJoin a like-minded community while continuing to maintain your family’s individual homeschool learning goals.Shared Resources & SupportAccess to co-teaching help, shared curriculum ideas, organized schedules, and fewer burdens on individual families.Get StartedJoin Co-Op TodayJoin a Christ-centered community where your family can grow academically, spiritually, and relationally alongside others.Apply to Join Co-OpApply to Join Co-OpApply to Join Co-OpFAQsFind answers to common questions about our co-op, how it works, and what to expect for your family.What kinds of classes are offered?Classes vary each session and may include academic, creative, and enrichment opportunities.When does the Co-Op meet?Co-Op runs in seasonal sessions (typically Fall and Spring).Do parents need to be involved?Yes—Co-Op is a shared community, and parents play an active role in helping and supporting classes.What ages can participate in the Co-Op?Our Co-Op serves homeschool families with children across a range of grade levels (details vary by session).Can't find what you're looking for?Contact UsContact UsContact Us

chunks.title: Ministry Partners | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Discover the trusted ministries Landmark Church partners with to advance the gospel locally and globally through prayer, support, and service.

chunks.title: Ministry Partners | Landmark Church
chunks.text: PartnersSupport PartnersSupport PartnersSupport PartnersView MissionariesView MissionariesView MissionariesAboutWhat Makes a "Partner"Our Partners are organizations we’re especially invested in—through prayer, finances, and people. These are ministries we trust, align with biblically, and come alongside in a deeper way.With our Partners, we don’t just send support—we send teams, serve together, and build lasting relationships to make disciples locally and around the world.Partners in MinistryWe partner with ministries around the world to advance the gospel, serve communities, and support life-changing work beyond our local church.Jehovah Jireh Children's HomeJehovah Jireh Mustard Seeds is a children's home in the Maboela Village, in Qwa Qwa, South Africa. It's main goals are to provide physical and spiritual support to the children.Learn MoreLearn MoreLearn MoreLandmark Bible CollegeProviding quality biblical and theological training to thousands of people, throughout the nation of India.‍Learn MoreLearn MoreLearn MoreFocusWhy Landmark Believes in PartnershipsPreviousPreviousNextNextWe Multiply Our ImpactWe believe we can do more together than we ever could alone—partnering with trusted ministries allows us to extend the reach of the gospel far beyond our local church.We Fulfill the Great CommissionPartnerships help us actively participate in taking the gospel to the nations by supporting, sending, and strengthening ministries around the world.We Strengthen the Church GloballyBy coming alongside other ministries, we help equip leaders, support communities, and build up the global body of Christ through shared mission and discipleship.We Live Out Biblical UnityScripture calls the Church to function as one body—partnerships reflect that unity as we work together to serve, give, and advance God’s kingdom.MissionsCommitted to Supporting Domestic & International MissionsExplore MissionsExplore MissionsExplore MissionsSupportHelp Support Our Partnerships Through GivingYou can support our Partners in several ways: by giving to Landmark’s Missions Fund, which provides ongoing support; by meeting specific needs we highlight during church gatherings; or by visiting each Partner’s website to learn more and give directly.Support PartnersSupport PartnersSupport PartnersFAQsCommon questions and answers to what partnership looks like at Landmark Church.Can I get involved with a partner ministry?Yes—there are opportunities throughout the year to support or participate in outreach efforts.How does Landmark support these partners?Through financial support, prayer, and in some cases, hands-on involvement like missions trips.How do you choose your partners?We partner with trusted ministries that demonstrate strong leadership, biblical alignment, and meaningful impact.What does it mean to be a partner?We partner with ministries that align with our mission to share the gospel and serve people locally and globally.Can't find what you're looking for?Contact UsContact UsContact Us

chunks.title: Elders | Landmark Church Leadership & Spiritual Oversight
chunks.text: Meet the elders of Landmark Church. Learn about their biblical role in providing spiritual oversight, guidance, and shepherding our congregation.

chunks.title: Elders | Landmark Church Leadership & Spiritual Oversight
chunks.text: EldersEldersMatthew MaherPastorElderEldersMark EmondDirector of OperationsElderEldersJohn ShirkElderEldersNorman JohnsonElderEldersScott JohnsonElderEldersNick JohnsonFamily Life PastorElderWhat Elders DoThe elder’s position is guided by the qualifications as set out in the Scriptures (references below). Simply put, the elders are to be humble servant leaders who oversee and shepherd the congregation. Under God’s authority and His leadership, they are responsible for the final decisions concerning the overall direction, discipline, and doctrine of our church.[1 Timothy 3:1-7, Titus 1: 5-7, Ephesians 4:11-12, 1 Peter 2:25, 1 Peter 5:1-5, Acts 20:17-28, Philippians 1:1, James 5:14, Acts 11:30, 14:23, 15:2-23, 16:4, 21:18, 1 Timothy 5: 17-19]OverviewPastor, Elder, OverseerOther notable titles used interchangeably in Scripture are Pastor (Shepherd), Bishop (Overseer), and Elder. While these titles emphasize different aspects of ministry, they describe the sameoffice of spiritual leadership.‍As demonstrated in Colin Smothers' helpful illustration below, each of these words overlap in various ways with each other.Church LeadershipDistinctions Between Pastor & ElderThis is a vital office for the health of the church. As such, the character qualifications outlined in Scripture are necessary for those who serve in this role (1 Timothy 3:1-7; Titus 1:5-7).‍In the New Testament, the terms pastor (shepherd), elder, and overseer are often usedinterchangeably to describe the same office from different perspectives. A pastor shepherds the flock, an elder emphasizes spiritual maturity and leadership, and an overseer highlights the responsibility of oversight and care. Together, these terms describe the work of spiritual leadership within the local church.‍While the biblical office is the same, responsibilities may differ according to gifting, availability, and ministry assignment. Some elders labor primarily in preaching and teaching, while others focus more heavily on governance, discipleship, counseling, administration, or oversight. Regardless of these distinctions, all elders share responsibility for the spiritual care anddirection of the church.‍PastorTypically serves in a full-time roleLeads day-to-day ministry and operationsFocused on teaching, shepherding, and equippingElderOften serves in a volunteer capacityProvides spiritual oversight and governanceHelps guide the overall direction of the churchLeadership RolesElder ResponsibilitiesAs already mentioned, the elders are responsible for the final decisions concerning the overall direction, discipline, and doctrine of our church. They do that by:PreviousPreviousNextNextPriests In PrayerGoing before God on behalf of the people and going before the people on behalf of God.Stewards Of ResourcesManaging well what God has entrusted to the organization by determining and directing church policy and practice.‍Shepherds Of The SheepOverseeing the flock by feeding, leading, and protecting the church body through duty and doctrine.Counselors Of CareOffering the balm of the Bible to those in need of biblical perspective.‍Prophets Of The BookTeaching and preaching from a biblical worldview; knowing the Word and showing the Word in life and lip.‍Principals Of PrincipleCarrying out church discipline when warranted and protecting the integrity of the church body.Who Picks Elders?Choosing elders begins with praying and seeking God for wisdom and discernment as to who should serve. The office of elder is a high calling and must not be taken lightly by any.PreviousPreviousNextNext01Observe & ServeFirst and foremost, elders are called and appointed by God. While this isharder to determine, it is observed by the individual’s obvious compulsion to serve the body (often as a volunteer and then deacon before nomination of eldership). Eventually they are confirmed by church leadership through observable fruit in ministry, marriage, and family life.‍02NominateUpon nomination, the individual responds to the call through several interviewand vetting processes: including questions about their testimony, their working knowledge of the Bible (doctrine and duty), and their private/family life. This will include a formal interview with his wife and multiple elders.‍03CandidateOnce a man has had his qualifications confirmed by the elders, he may enter aphase of preparation and evaluation for the specific work of eldership. This phase involves intentional mentorship by the current elders, study related to the roles, responsibilities and functions of elders, and participation in elder team meetings. In addition to preparing the candidate, the primary goal is to determine the candidate’s fitness and fit with the team. The time required to complete this phase may vary by individual.‍04ApprovalUpon approval and announcement to the church body, the congregation willhave a 2-week window where they can share any critical information or spiritual concerns they may have about the chosen elder (1 Timothy 5:19). These concerns can be submitted in writing to the elder board for investigation and must be substantiated by credible sources and witnesses.‍05InstallationFollowing the satisfactory completion of all requirements, new elders willbe installed publicly at a worship gathering.[This above-mentioned process is not an induction into a secret society, and thus, the candidate’s character, conversation, and conduct are of public importance. Again, if a congregant is aware of any disqualifying sin or character flaw in an elder candidate, they are urged to make the matter known to the existing elders within the 2-week window so they can investigate the claim]‍FAQsFind answers to common questions about our elders, their role in the church, and how they help lead and shepherd Landmark Church.Do you have to be a paid staff member to be an elder and are all the pastors considered elders?The Bible does not require an elder to be a paid staff member, nor does it prohibit financial support for those serving in eldership when necessary (1 Timothy 5:17-18; 1 Corinthians 9:11). At Landmark, both staff and non-staff men may serve as elders provided they meet the biblical qualifications and can fulfill the responsibilities of the office.‍Landmark also recognizes pastors who may have been ordained by other ministries and serve in various pastoral capacities. However, pastoral ordination received elsewhere does not automatically confer governing authority within Landmark Church. Governing eldership at Landmark is determined by the existing elder board through the church's elder evaluation and appointment process.‍Men ordained as pastors by Landmark are recognized as elders according to the qualifications and functions described in Scripture. As a general practice, ordination by Landmark includes installation into the office of elder, having already completed the church's elder evaluation, vetting, and approval process.‍Service on the governing elder board, including voting authority and legal responsibilities, ordinarily accompanies eldership. However, in certain circumstances, the elder board may determine that a different arrangement is appropriate due to unique ministry, legal, or practical considerations.‍Because eldership carries responsibility for the doctrine, direction, and discipline of the church, the final determination of governing eldership rests with the existing plurality of elders. In the case of non-staff elders, they must also have the time and availability necessary to fulfill the oversight responsibilities and meeting requirements established by the elder board.How many elders should make up a board and do they serve for life?The Bible does not give a specific number of elders that should serve a given community nor does it specify term limits. Each church body differs and should exercise wisdom in determining how many elders would be sufficient to effectively lead the church, as well as how long. The team of elders at Landmark collectively oversee the affairs of the church and make these determinations.‍Can I talk to an elder?Yes—our elders are available to pray, offer guidance, and care for members of our church.How are elders chosen?Elders are selected based on biblical qualifications, character, and a proven track record of leadership and faithfulness.What’s the difference between a pastor and an elder?Pastors typically serve in full-time ministry, while elders provide broader oversight—though both are held to the same biblical qualifications.What do elders do at Landmark Church?Elders provide spiritual oversight, helping guide the church’s direction, doctrine, and care for the congregation.Can't find what you're looking for?Contact UsContact UsContact Us

chunks.title: Marriage Support & Mentoring | The Landmark Church
chunks.text: MarriageBuilding strong, Gospel-centered marriagesBe MentoredBe MentoredBe MentoredBecome A MentorBecome A MentorBecome A MentorFor Married & Engaged CouplesFour unique opportunities to invest in your marriage.PreviousPreviousNextNextPre-Marital CounselingInvest in your marriage before you marry. Premarital counseling guides you and your partner through key topics and questions so you understand your backgrounds and perspectives and begin married life on the right foot.Get counselingGet counselingGet counselingCoaching & MentoringOur marriage coaches and mentors help you and your spouse overcome current challenges and prepare for the future. Investing in coaching strengthens your relationship and equips you to thrive together.Be mentoredBe mentoredBe mentoredDiscipleship Community EventQuarterly gatherings for married couples to fellowship, receive discipleship, and grow together through informative, interactive workshops.Coming SoonMarriage Discipleship GroupsSmall cohorts where you and your spouse will grow together with other couples through biblical teaching, discussion, and mutual support.Marriage TeamMeet Your MentorsShawn & Danielle FlickingerRead BioRead BioRead BioCloseCloseShawn & Danielle FlickingerCelebrating 25 years of marriage, Shawn and Danielle’s journey has been anchored in a shared commitment to God and family. As parents to a beautiful daughter and a heavenly son, they have experienced seasons of challenge and victory that have shaped their faith and strengthened their marriage. These experiences have inspired them to mentor other couples, providing authentic, practical wisdom grounded in Scripture. Their heart is to help couples build marriages that lead to a lasting and meaningful legacy.‍Eric & Kelly SchochRead BioRead BioRead BioCloseCloseEric & Kelly SchochEric and Kelly Schoch have enjoyed more than 25 years of marriage and the blessing of raising their daughter together. Rooted in their faith, they believe in Christ's transformative power to strengthen and renew marriages. Their passion is to help couples experience the joy and purpose of a Christ centered marriage. Eric and Kelly provide practical, Scripture-based guidance to couples at every stage, from those starting with premarital counseling to couples navigating challenging seasons in their marriage. Their commitment to serving others reflects their belief that, with faith and intentionality, marriages can thrive. They mentor and encourage couples to grow closer to God and to one another through shared experiences, biblical wisdom, and practical insights.Wayne & Bonnie MillerRead BioRead BioRead BioCloseCloseWayne & Bonnie MillerWayne and Bonnie Miller have been married for over 40 years and are passionate about helping couples build strong, Christ-centered marriages. Their own journey of marriage, family, careers, and faith has given them a deep appreciation for the importance of commitment, communication, grace, and keeping Christ at the center of a marriage. Bonnie brings a background in nursing and healthcare administration, having spent many years in healthcare leadership with a focus on caring for patients, families, and teams. Wayne spent his career in the RV industry, serving as a Service Manager and working closely with customers and employees. Through their professional experiences, both have developed strong skills in listening, problem-solving, communication, leadership, and working with people from many different backgrounds. Wayne and Bonnie are the proud parents of two grown children, Beveline and Mark. Family has always been an important part of their lives, and they value the lessons that marriage and parenting have taught them about patience, forgiveness, perseverance, and unconditional love. Wayne and Bonnie have been part of Landmark Church for several years as weekenders until moving here full time in 2025. Their faith and desire to serve others have led them to become Marriage Mentors, where they have the privilege of walking alongside couples during both the joyful and challenging seasons of marriage. As Marriage Mentors, Wayne and Bonnie seek to encourage couples through biblical principles, honest conversation, prayer, and practical wisdom. They see themselves as a couple who has experienced the realities of more than four decades together and understands the value of continually growing in Christ and in their relationship with one another. Their heart is to come alongside couples with grace, encouragement, and authenticity—helping them strengthen their relationship, deepen their faith, and build a marriage that honors God and reflects His love.‍Jen HeistRead BioRead BioRead BioCloseCloseJen HeistJennifer Heist is a Life Coach and Marriage Mentor with a heart to encourage, strengthen, and bring hope to those navigating difficult or transitional seasons of life. She is passionate about helping couples communicate more effectively, fostering deeper emotional connection and unity in their relationships. Jennifer holds a Master’s degree in Human Services Counseling with a focus in Life Coaching from Liberty University. She is also certified in SYMBIS (Saving Your Marriage Before It Starts), equipping her to support couples at every stage of their journey. Through both her education and personal life experiences, Jennifer has gained the insight and compassion needed to walk alongside others as they pursue healing, growth, and God’s purpose for their lives.‍Cody & Ceiara PanettaRead BioRead BioRead BioCloseCloseCody & Ceiara PanettaCody and Ceiara are high school sweethearts who have spent the last 17 years building a Christ centered marriage while raising their three children, Brody, Savannah, and Mason. For the past seven years, they have been faithfully planted at Landmark, where their passion for full time ministry has grown. Ceiara is a devoted mother and certified biblical counselor who serves schools, crisis pregnancy centers, and alongside the care team at Landmark Church. Cody serves full time at Landmark and as the Managing Partner of Landmark Cafe. Together, they are passionate about mentoring the next generation and walking alongside couples, with a shared heart to strengthen marriages through biblical truth, unity, and a Christ centered home.‍John & Mary HenryRead BioRead BioRead BioCloseCloseJohn & Mary HenryJohn and Mary have been happily married for over 38 years and love helping other couples build strong, healthy relationships.  They’ve spent 40 years serving with Youth With A Mission, and their life experience - along with their faith - shapes the way they walk alongside others.  As certified SYMBIS marriage mentors, they enjoy guiding engaged and newly married couples through meaningful conversations that strengthen connection and prepare them for a lasting marriage.  They’ve raised three children, love doing life together and are excited to step into a new season as grandparents. ‍Terence & Jen SikoryakRead BioRead BioRead BioCloseCloseTerence & Jen SikoryakTerence and Jennifer Sikoryak are a devoted Christian couple who have been joyfully married for ten years, dedicating their lives to exemplifying a Christ-centered marriage and inspiring others through their faith-filled partnership. As active members of Landmark’s Care Team, Terence serves as a pastor and Jennifer as a committed volunteer, using their experience as life coaches and marriage mentors to guide couples in building spiritually strong, emotionally healthy relationships rooted in biblical principles. Their shared ministry emphasizes the importance of Christian values, personal growth, and brain health, while their love for each other and God remains at the heart of their work. Outside of ministry, they delight in their eight grandchildren, with Jennifer enjoying surfing and serving on the worship team, and Terence hosting his long-running radio show, This One Voice. Together, their united mission is to help others discover God’s purpose for marriage and create a legacy of faith for generations to come.‍Scott & Amy ReefRead BioRead BioRead BioCloseCloseScott & Amy ReefScott and Amy Reef have been joyfully married for over 31 years and are passionate about helping couples build marriages that last a lifetime. As Certified Marriage Coaches and longtime owners of their hometown pharmacy, they understand both the challenges and the beauty of partnership—at home and in life. Together, they’ve raised four children and served in various marriage and family ministries, walking alongside couples through every season. Their journey includes overcoming addiction, deception, and resentment—experiences that have shaped their deep compassion and unwavering faith. Scott and Amy give God all the glory for His faithfulness and grace, and they are devoted to empowering couples to stand resolute in their commitment and to bring life and hope into their marriages.‍The MissionEquipping couples to reflect God's glory and transform future generations.Use Your GiftsBecome a Marriage Mentor or CoachFaith-centered marriage mentoring and coaching to help couples heal, grow, and thrive.Mentoring walks alongside couples long-term. Coaching guides couples through a structured process — bringing clarity, removing obstacles, and building lasting change.Become a MentorBecome a MentorBecome a MentorWhat You'll DoMeet with assigned couples to listen, encourage, and offer biblical guidance.Follow Landmark’s mentoring guidelines and complete session notes so couples stay on track.Support couples through practical steps, prayer, and connection to church resources.FAQsGet answers to some of our most frequently asked questions about marriage ministry.How can I become a Marriage Mentor?We’re always looking for couples who have a desire to invest in and encourage other marriages. Marriage mentors participate in training and are equipped with the tools and resources needed to walk alongside couples well.If you’re interested in becoming a Marriage Mentor, fill out the Marriage Mentor interest form or contact our Care Team to learn about upcoming training opportunities and the process for getting involved.‍How do we get started?Getting started is simple! If you are engaged and interested in Premarital Mentoring, complete the premarital questionnaire form and our team will follow up with you about the next steps.If you are already married and interested in Marriage Coaching or Counseling, complete the marital coaching application form. We’ll connect with you to learn more about what you’re looking for and help determine the best next step for your marriage.‍Who are the marriage mentors and coaches?Our marriage mentors are trained couples from our church who have a heart for helping others build healthy, Christ-centered marriages. They come from a variety of life experiences and are equipped to listen, encourage, ask good questions, and walk alongside couples through the mentoring process.Marriage coaching and counseling is provided by members of our Care Team and other trusted, qualified individuals within our church ministry.‍What is the difference between Premarital Mentoring and Marriage Coaching?Our Premarital Mentoring program is designed for engaged couples who are preparing for marriage. Couples are paired with trained marriage mentors and walk through a guided process that helps them build a strong foundation for their marriage.Marriage Coaching and Counseling is available for couples who are already married. Whether you’re looking to strengthen a healthy marriage, work through a specific challenge, or simply grow together, our team is here to walk alongside you.‍Can't find what you're looking for?Contact UsContact UsContact UsThere Is a Team that CaresIn need of benevolence, meals, help with addiction, or prayer? Our care team will come alongside you to weather the storm.Visit CareVisit CareVisit Care

chunks.text: Privacy PolicyEffective Date: April 11, 2026 Last Revised: April 11, 2026‍1. IntroductionLandmark Church ("Landmark," "we," "us," or "our") operates thelandmark.church (the "Site"). This Privacy Policy explains what information we collect, how we use it, and your rights regarding that information. By using our Site, you agree to the practices described here.‍2. Information We CollectWe collect information in the following ways:Information you provide directly, including when you:Submit a contact, care request, or prayer request formRegister for events or classes (Landmark 101, 201, etc.)Apply for internships or serving teamsRegister your child for Landmark Kids or Youth programsFill out the first-time guest or Co-Op interest formsSign up for our newsletter or email updatesCreate a member profile on our SiteThis information may include your name, email address, phone number, mailing address, and any message or details you voluntarily provide.Information collected automatically, including browser type, IP address, pages visited, and time spent on our Site. This data is collected via cookies and analytics tools.‍3. Third-Party Services We UseOur Site and ministry operations rely on trusted third-party platforms. Each has its own privacy policy:Church Center (Planning Center) — used for event registration, groups, giving, and class sign-ups. planningcenter.com/privacyMemberstack — used for member accounts and access control on our Site.Microsoft Clarity — used for analytics and understanding how visitors use our Site. Microsoft may collect usage data including mouse movements and clicks.Spotify — sermon and podcast audio may be embedded from Spotify. Spotify may collect data per their own policy.Google Fonts & other CDN resources — loaded to support Site typography and performance.We encourage you to review the privacy policies of these third parties.‍4. How We Use Your InformationWe use the information we collect to:Respond to your requests, questions, or care needsRegister you for events, classes, or ministry programsSend service updates, announcements, and newsletters (only if you opt in)Support pastoral care, prayer follow-up, and ministry coordinationImprove the functionality and content of our SiteFulfill child check-in, security, and safety obligations for Landmark Kids and Youth programsWe will never sell your personal information.‍5. Children's PrivacyWe collect limited information about minors (under 18) only as necessary for ministry participation — such as child check-in for Landmark Kids and Youth programs. This information is provided by a parent or guardian and is used solely for ministry and safety purposes. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children without parental consent.‍6. Data SharingWe do not sell, rent, or trade your personal information. We may share information with:Ministry staff and volunteers on a need-to-know basisThird-party service providers listed in Section 3, solely to operate our Site and programsAuthorities if required by law or to protect the safety of individuals‍7. CookiesOur Site uses cookies to remember preferences and gather analytics data. You may disable cookies in your browser settings, though some features of the Site may not function properly as a result.‍8. Data RetentionWe retain your information for as long as needed to fulfill the purposes described in this policy, or as required by applicable law. You may request deletion of your information at any time (see Section 9).‍9. Your RightsYou have the right to:Request access to the personal information we hold about youRequest correction of inaccurate informationRequest deletion of your personal informationOpt out of non-essential communications at any timeTo exercise any of these rights, contact us at hello@thelandmark.church.‍10. External LinksOur Site may contain links to external websites (Church Center, Planning Center, Spotify, etc.). We are not responsible for the privacy practices of those sites and encourage you to review their policies.‍11. Changes to This PolicyWe may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. When we do, we will revise the "Last Revised" date at the top. Continued use of the Site after changes are posted constitutes your acceptance of the updated policy.‍12. Contact UsIf you have questions about this Privacy Policy, please reach out:Landmark Church: 300 E. 8th Street, Ocean City, NJ 08226 📞 609-399-4747✉️ hello@thelandmark.church‍

chunks.title: Charlie Martin | The Landmark Church Team
chunks.text: Charlie MartinRecovery LeadCharlie serves as the Recovery Lead, under the guidance and supervision of Pastor Terence who leads the entire Care Team. He acts as a touch point to those who are, or have loved ones, struggling with addiction, loss of a loved one, or someone just looking for a little extra support in their walk with Christ.Charlie is grateful that, here at Landmark, you can find someone who has, or is currently going, through the same situation as you. It is full of people that just want to serve, and find ways to do it.Having accepted Christ in 2018, after 22 years of battling addiction, in 2019 Charlie came here because of all the opportunities to serve. It was here he met his wife, found wonderful spiritual support groups (Foundational Recovery, GriefShare, Men's Fellowship), and found the peace of God in strenuous circumstances.Charlie finds it important to be willing to meet people where they are, and love them enough to not let them stay there. It often requires saying what is needed, not desired. It demands that individuals deal with the consequences of their choices, and encourage them because they don't have to deal with those consequences on their own. Others have been where you are, so let us connect you with someone who knows where you're at.Outside of church, Charlie enjoys spending time with his children, helping friends with projects, and running.‍Tea SnobListens to FM RadioEncrypts His Journal (Cursive)Meet the TeamFriendly Faces You'll See at LandmarkMeet some of the people at Landmark Church who are here to welcome you, answer questions, and help you feel right at home.Meet the TeamMeet the TeamMeet the TeamPreviousPreviousNextNextOperationsGene WilkinsPastorOperationsEric SchochOperations AssistantWorshipJohn WilsonWorship Leader

She helps handle the week-to-week details—scheduling servant leaders, keeping the FLC stocked, and prepping for future events and trips—trusting that each small effort contributes to the bigger picture of shaping disciples of Jesus. chunks.title: Ethan Hoover | The Landmark Church Team
chunks.text: Ethan HooverCreative DirectorEthan serves as the Creative Director at Landmark Church, leading digital media, content, and communications to help the church communicate clearly and beautifully. A graduate of Regent University with a Bachelor of Science in Business Marketing, he brings both entrepreneurial experience and ministry conviction to his role. Before stepping into full-time ministry, he worked in marketing for organizations in Virginia Beach and Nashville, developing a passion for strategy, storytelling, and building things that last.At his core, Ethan has a heart to resource the Church. He loves helping people grow excited about the Bible—its books, its people, and the unified story it tells—and is passionate about creating tools that make deep biblical learning accessible and engaging. He thrives at the intersection of theology, creativity, and innovation, and is driven by a desire to strengthen the local church for the long haul.Ethan believes all of life belongs to the Lord. Whether serving in vocational ministry or in the marketplace, his aim is the same: to glorify God, steward his gifts faithfully, and support the work of the local church wherever the Lord places him. Above all, he is grateful to be the husband of his wife, Sage, and is committed to loving and leading his family well in every season. chunks.text: Gene WilkinsPastorPG (Gene) has faithfully served the Lord in pastoral ministry for 66 years across multiple communities of faith. He began attending Landmark in 2017 after several years as pastor of Ventnor Community Church and was later invited to join the staff.While still serving in Ventnor, Gene began attending Thursday evening services and later the Saturday Men in Service gatherings. Through those relationships, several of the men helped restore damage to the church facility following Hurricane Sandy. Their care, faithfulness, and Christlike witness deeply impacted him and drew him more fully into the life and ministry of Landmark.Gene especially values the commitment and dedication of Landmark’s leadership and staff. He is grateful for the transparency and integrity of the pastors and elders and treasures the many opportunities he has to share the Word, lead in prayer, and mentor believers of every age.What matters most to him is the joy of serving alongside others in ministry and experiencing the grace that continues to be poured out on his life and family.Outside of church life, Gene enjoys spending time with Suzanne and their family, embracing their role as grandparents and great-grandparents, and encouraging their children as they faithfully walk with the Lord. He also values opportunities to share God’s Word in other communities of faith. chunks.text: Jay ReimerCommunity PastorJay serves Landmark Church in a part-time Community Pastor role, acting as a liaison with the Ocean City Mayor’s Office and City Council, the OC School Board, local ministers, the OC Chamber of Commerce, and other community organizations. His heartbeat is evangelism and discipleship, which makes him especially passionate about participating in Landmark’s many Bible study small groups.Jay lived in Cherry Hill as a child and grew up at Grace Bible Church of Mt. Laurel. chunks.title: Jennifer Emond | The Landmark Church Team
chunks.text: Jennifer EmondAdministration DirectorJennifer serves at Landmark in the areas of finance, administration, and operations; though many affectionately refer to her as the “Ninja” because of her lightning-fast work skills that often happen behind the scenes. She helps ensure that the day-to-day operations run smoothly so that ministry can flourish.In addition to her operational role, she leads Lost + Found Outreach, a ministry dedicated to serving those who are homeless, displaced, or simply in need of love, dignity, and kindness. Her heart for outreach is deeply personal. Having walked through significant challenges in both childhood and adulthood, Jenny sees God’s hand in shaping her story. Those seasons didn’t define her, they refined her. They equipped her with compassion, resilience, and a deep understanding of suffering and addiction. Today, she uses that lived experience to serve others with empathy and authenticity.What she loves most about serving at Landmark is watching people grow, seeing someone who feels forgotten become known, or someone struggling begin to experience hope. She is passionate about Kingdom work that meets both practical and spiritual needs. She believes ministry is not just about programs, but about people; walking with them, loving them well, and reminding them that they matter to God.Jenny also she wears her heart on her sleeve. A tear will often accompany her words when she speaks about the people she loves and serves. Her compassion runs deep, and her outward joy and contagious laugh light up a room.Outside of church life, Jenny treasures time with her family. She loves creating memories with her children and grandchild, traveling to new places, enjoying amazing restaurants, and riding motorcycles with her husband. Whether she’s balancing budgets, leading outreach, or sharing a meal with someone in need, Jenny's life reflects a simple but powerful desire: to serve faithfully, love deeply, and point others to hope.‍LOL! chunks.text: Norman JohnsonElder•ElderNorm joined the Landmark Church family over 20 years ago, having been lead to be part of a growing evangelistic ministry.  Serving as a elder, teacher and home group leader, he is focused on the spiritual growth and strength of the body of Christ. As a financial advisor, Norm recently became a Certified Kingdom Advisor. Coupled with his professional expertise and his passion in ministry to help believers understand what the Bible says about money, he holds classes on how one can better serve the Lord with what they have, weather it’s their time, talent or treasure.  He also facilitates discipleship group in his home.Seeing the church family grow in connection with one other and sharing the message of Jesus’ gift of eternal life is what drives Norm to serve here at Landmark.  His spiritual strength and compassion for others shows in the relationships he builds.Norm and his wife, Marie, have been married for over 45 years, and enjoy spending time with their three children and their spouses, and four grandchildren. He enjoys reading, traveling, coffee at any hour and driving his MGB roadster in the summer months.Coffee AddictAntique British Car EnthusiastStory TellerMeet the TeamFriendly Faces You'll See at LandmarkMeet some of the people at Landmark Church who are here to welcome you, answer questions, and help you feel right at home.Meet the TeamMeet the TeamMeet the TeamPreviousPreviousNextNextEldersJohn ShirkElderCareCharlie MartinRecovery LeadProductionJosh BrockenberryProduction Assistant
