Cafe es un espacio para conectar, relajarse y construir relaciones antes y después de los servicios o durante la semana.¿Para qué se utiliza el Centro de Vida Familiar?El Centro de Vida Familiar es el hogar de ambientes enfocados en niños, jóvenes y familias durante toda la semana.¿Qué sucede en el Santuario?El Santuario es donde nos reunimos para servicios de adoración, enseñanza y reuniones de toda la iglesia.¿Qué espacios son parte del campus Landmark?Nuestro campus incluye el Santuario, el Centro de Vida Familiar y la Cafetería Landmark—cada uno diseñado para apoyar diferentes aspectos de la vida de la iglesia.¿Cómo puedo conectarme?Puedes comenzar asistiendo, uniéndote a un grupo, o tomando Landmark 101.¿Necesito registrarme antes de visitar?No, pero planificar tu visita con anticipación puede ayudar a que tu primera experiencia sea más fluida.¿Qué debo usar para ir a la iglesia?Ven tal como eres—la gente se viste de manera casual y cómoda.¿Qué debo esperar un domingo o miércoles?Experimentarás adoración, enseñanza bíblica y un ambiente acogedor para individuos y familias.¿Dónde está ubicada la Iglesia Landmark?Puedes encontrar indicaciones y detalles del campus en nuestra página del campus para ayudarte a planificar tu visita.¿Cómo me uno a un grupo?Puedes explorar los grupos disponibles y unirte a uno que se adapte a tu horario y etapa de vida.¿Cómo puedo contribuir a la iglesia?Nuestra iglesia ofrece varias formas de contribuir, incluyendo ofrendas presenciales, plataformas de donaciones en línea, aplicaciones móviles, donaciones por correo o donaciones automáticas recurrentes.¿Quién puede participar en el Ministerio de Hombres?Todos los hombres son bienvenidos—sin importar la edad, trasfondo, o dónde se encuentren en su camino de fe. Es un espacio para el crecimiento, la responsabilidad y la conexión.¿Cuál es el propósito del Ministerio de Hombres?El Ministerio de Hombres existe para ayudar a los hombres a crecer espiritualmente, desarrollar un carácter fuerte y construir relaciones auténticas mientras los animan a través de la comunión a vivir su fe en la vida cotidiana.¿Quién puede unirse al Ministerio de Mujeres?Todas las mujeres son bienvenidas, sin importar su edad, trasfondo o etapa en su fe. El ministerio es un lugar para la conexión, el aprendizaje y el apoyo.¿Cuál es el propósito del Ministerio de Mujeres?El propósito del Ministerio de Mujeres es fomentar el crecimiento espiritual, construir relaciones significativas y apoyar a las mujeres en su camino de fe a través de la comunión, el estudio y el servicio.Can't find what you're looking for?Contact UsContact UsContact Us

chunks.title: Landmark Stories | Real Conversations That Change Lives
chunks.text: See More SermonsSee More SermonsSee More SermonsWHAT IS LANDMARK STORIES?A Conversation Series About What Changes PeopleLandmark Stories is a long-form video interview series. We sit down with people — athletes, leaders, a fire chief, a worship leader, people who live right here in Ocean City — and we ask the questions most people avoid. What broke you? What did you almost lose? What did you do when the thing you were counting on fell apart?The answers are different every time. But there's a thread that runs through every single one. Come to a live event and hear it for yourself.See Upcoming EventsSee Upcoming EventsSee Upcoming EventsFAQsDiscover answers to some of our most frequently asked questions about Landmark Stories.Can I suggest someone for a future episode?Yes. If you know someone whose story deserves to be heard, reach out at hello@thelandmark.churchWhere can I watch episodes & past events?Every episode is free at thelandmark.church/landmark-stories and on the Landmark Church YouTube channel. New episodes drop regularly — follow @thelandmark.church on Instagram to know when.Do I need to go to Landmark Church to go to a live event?No. Show up. See what it's about.What happens at a live event?A live Landmark Stories event is exactly what it sounds like: a real conversation, in person, with someone whose story is worth showing up for. No big production. No pressure. Just a room full of people and something honest happening in front of them.Is this a church thing?Landmark Stories is produced by Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ. But the conversations stand on their own — you don't need to believe anything to watch. You just have to be willing to listen.Who are the people you interview & host?All kinds. Athletes. Leaders. People who've walked through addiction, loss, identity, career collapse, grief. The common thread isn't their background — it's that something happened they didn't see coming, and it changed them.What is Landmark Stories?It's a long-form video interview & live event series — real conversations with real people about the moments that defined them. Think less panel discussion, more honest one-on-one. We've sat down with NFL players, fire chiefs, worship leaders, and people you might know from down the street in Ocean City. Free to watch at thelandmark.church/landmark-stories.Can't find what you're looking for?Contact UsContact UsContact Us

chunks.text: Legacy Initiative: For the Church After UsIn 1879, this island was purchased and founded as a Christian seaside resort & meeting place. Our plan is to bring the island back to those roots through eternal investments.Give Toward LegacyGive Toward LegacyGive Toward LegacyWatch The Legacy Initiative Intro VideoWatch The Legacy Initiative Intro VideoWatch The Legacy Initiative Intro VideoThe MissionThis is our vision for the future.‍‍In a world full of isolation & loneliness, we aspire to be a bridge that leads people to Biblical community and relationship.‍‍In a culture of lies & misinformation, we want to be a pillar of Biblical truth to educate the generation of today and the generation to come.‍‍In our unique geographical area of the North East, where hearts are cold and belief in self is much greater than belief in God, we desire to be a place where the love of Christ is evident and the hope of Christ is received.‍‍And in Ocean City and the surrounding towns, we want to lead the charge of helping our community prosper and experience life by caring for the homeless, widowed, orphaned and needy, and being the voice of truth in the public square.This Requires Action‍Not Action from Some, But from AllGod is calling each one of us to pray and consider how we would invest in what needs to be sowed today, so what is reaped down the road has eternal benefit. Want to hear what our Elders said? If you’re looking to give via these other methods, please contact us at finance@thelandmark.church and specify which method you’re interested in using.PreviousPreviousNextNextStocksDonate stock holdings directly to Landmark through our broker. Contact our office to proceed.If you sell appreciated stock and donate the cash proceeds, you may be subject to long term capital gains taxes which can be up to 20% of the appreciated value. If you donate the stock directly to the church, you can avoid that tax altogether and make your gift go further!Donor-Advised FundsDonor-Advised Funds, or DAFs, allow donors to make charitable contributions to a public charity, receive an immediate tax deduction, and then recommend grants to other organizations like Landmark Church.IRA AccountsAre you subject to required minimum distributions from your IRA account? A qualified charitable distribution to Landmark Church can satisfy all or part of the amount of your required minimum distribution from your IRA, helping you to avoid income taxes on an otherwise taxable distribution.Other Non-Cash GiftsWe are also able to accept other non-cash gifts, such as real estate, business interests, personal property, restricted securities, estate gifts, retirement plans, and life insurance.FAQsDiscover answers to some of our most frequently asked Legacy Initiative questions.What if I don't see my question listed?If you have a question that isn’t listed above, please reach out to us at finance@thelandmark.church.Should I redirect my regular tithes and contributions to this initiative?We are asking that you prayerfully consider giving to the initiative in addition to, not instead of, your regular tithes and contributions to our general fund.Do you accept other contributions besides cash, check, or credit card payments?Yes we do! chunks.title: Reid Shields | The Landmark Church Team
chunks.text:
Meet Reid Shields, Ministry Assistant at The Landmark Church. Connect with our team and learn how they serve our community.

Reid ShieldsMinistry AssistantReid serves at Landmark wearing multiple different Ministry hats. He serves with the Lost and Found Outreach Ministry, with Landmark Kids and Landmark Youth, and also serves on the Care Team. He is passionate about connecting with people  one on one and building relationships. Going out on the street and showing the love of Christ through prayer, conversation, and compassion is one of his favorite passions. Reid originally grew up in Boyertown, Pennsylvania and felt called to Ocean City, NJ specifically Landmark Church in 2024. He stepped out in faith to answer the call to work in Ministry and has been at Landmark ever since! Join us for Grief Share  on Nov 03, 2026 at Family Life Center - 835 West Ave. Ocean City, NJ 08226.

Grief Share GriefShare is a friendly, caring group of people who will walk alongside you through the hurt of losing a loved one. Through this 13-week group, you’ll discover what to expect in the days ahead and what’s “normal” in grief. Since there are no neat, orderly stages of grief, you’ll learn helpful ways of coping with grief, in all its unpredictability—and gain solid support each step of the way. Give one-time or set up a recurring gift using Church Center.Give NowGive NowGive NowCashLook for one of our offering drop boxes located around our sanctuary building at any of the doors.CheckMake it out to Landmark Church and drop your check in any of our offering boxes onsite, or mail it to 300 E. 8th Street, Ocean City, NJ 08226.ServingPart of giving is serving with the gifts God gave you. Join a team and put your gifts to use!Find a TeamFind a TeamFind a TeamMore About GivingMore About GivingMore About GivingFAQsFind answers to the post common questions we get here at Landmark.Do I need to go to all three areas when I visit?Not at all—our team will help guide you based on your needs, whether you’re attending a service, checking in kids, or just connecting with others.What is Landmark Cafe?The Landmark Cafe is a space to connect, relax, and build relationships before and after services or throughout the week.What is the Family Life Center used for?The Family Life Center is home to kids, youth, and family-focused environments throughout the week.What happens in the Sanctuary?The Sanctuary is where we gather for worship services, teaching, and church-wide gatherings.What spaces are part of the Landmark campus?Our campus includes the Sanctuary, Family Life Center, and Landmark Café—each designed to support different parts of church life.How can I get connected?You can start by attending, joining a group, or taking Landmark 101.Do I need to sign up before visiting?No, but planning your visit ahead of time can help make your first experience smoother.What should I wear to church?Come as you are—people dress casually and comfortably.What should I expect on a Sunday or Wednesday?You’ll experience worship, biblical teaching, and a welcoming environment for individuals and families.Where is Landmark Church located?You can find directions and campus details on our campus page to help plan your visit.How do I join a group?You can browse available groups and join one that fits your schedule and stage of life.How can I give to the church?Our church offers several ways to give, including in-person offerings, online giving platforms, mobile apps, mail-in donations, or recurring automated giving.Who can participate in the Men’s Ministry?All men are welcome—regardless of age, background, or where they are in their faith journey. It’s a space for growth, accountability, and connection.What is the purpose of the Men’s Ministry?The Men’s Ministry exists to help men grow spiritually, develop strong character, and build authentic relationships while encouraging them through fellowship, to live out their faith in everyday life.Who can join the Women’s Ministry?All women are welcome, regardless of age, background, or stage in their faith. The ministry is a place for connection, learning, and encouragement.What is the purpose of the Women’s Ministry?The purpose of the Women’s Ministry is to encourage spiritual growth, build meaningful relationships, and support women in their faith journey through fellowship, study, and service.Can't find what you're looking for?Contact UsContact UsContact Us

chunks.title: Landmark 101 | Events | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Join us for Landmark 101 on Nov 15, 2026 at Landmark Care Hub.

Landmark 101This class is meant for anyone & everyone to take, no matter how long you've been part of our church. The 101 class will primarily highlight the topic of community/belonging and what that looks like at Landmark Church. It's a basic class that will educate you on who we are, what our mission is, and how you can be part of that. Whether you want to serve, work towards a leadership position, or be further engaged at our church, this is your first step to doing those things! chunks.title: Landmark 201 | Events | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Join us for Landmark 201 on Dec 13, 2026 at Landmark Church  - 300 E 8th St., Ocean City, NJ  08226.

Landmark 201
At Landmark Church, we are looking to develop mature disciples who are committed to their spiritual growth in covenant. This class is designed to explain our covenant, show you how that covenant is practically lived out, and by the end of the class we will give you an opportunity to enter into this covenant between you and the church. Having taken Landmark 101 is a pre-requisite to taking Landmark 201. If you have questions about whether or not you have taken 101, please contact Connor Alvis at calvis@thelandmark.church.

Shalom- Winter Youth RetreatJoin us for a weekend getaway! This trip is designed to foster an environment for both fellowship and spiritual growth, focusing on what it looks like to spend intentional time with our Father.WHO: 9th-12th GradersWHEN: January 22nd-24thWHERE: Harvey Cedars Bible ConferenceCOST: $200 We will leave from Landmark Church on Friday, January 22nd, at 3:45 PM. NOTICE: A deposit of $50 is due at the time of registration. Full payment must be received by January 1st. Payment will be refundable until 3 weeks prior to the retreat.Payment: To avoid Credit Card fees, we will accept payments through check or cash! Please make check payable to:Landmark Church, 300 E. 8th Street, OC, NJ 08226. Mail or drop payment in any onsite offering box. If paying with card, there will be a credit card fee. We will only accept full payments when using a credit card.InfoNoneJanuary 22, 202712:00 amHarvey Cedars Bible Conference - 12 Cedars Ave

chunks.title: Family Life Center | Campus | Landmark Church
chunks.text: ParkingParking at Landmark ChurchWe don’t have a dedicated church parking lot, but you’ll find plenty of street parking nearby on West Avenue, 8th Street, and Asbury Avenue.Metered Parking Info:Meters are in effect from May 1–October 31Sunday mornings: Free parking until 1:00 PMWednesday evenings: Meters are active—please remember to payIf you have trouble finding a spot, plan to arrive a few minutes early to give yourself time to park and walk over.FAQsAnswers to frequently asked questions about this campus location.Do I need to go to all three areas when I visit?Not at all—our team will help guide you based on your needs, whether you’re attending a service, checking in kids, or just connecting with others.What is Landmark Cafe?The Landmark Cafe is a space to connect, relax, and build relationships before and after services or throughout the week.What is the Family Life Center used for?The Family Life Center is home to kids, youth, and family-focused environments throughout the week.What happens in the Sanctuary?The Sanctuary is where we gather for worship services, teaching, and church-wide gatherings.What spaces are part of the Landmark campus?Our campus includes the Sanctuary, Family Life Center, and Landmark Café—each designed to support different parts of church life.How can I get connected?You can start by attending, joining a group, or taking Landmark 101.Do I need to sign up before visiting?No, but planning your visit ahead of time can help make your first experience smoother.What should I wear to church?Come as you are—people dress casually and comfortably.Can’t find what you’re looking for?Contact UsContact UsContact Us

Watch A 3rd Grader Showed More Courage Than the School Board | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher from  with . Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

A 3rd Grader Showed More Courage Than the School Board | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherDecember 28, 2025•3:45SummaryA third-grade girl stood before her school board and asked the adults in the room to protect her.

She described being punched, spit on, and made to feel unsafe while sharing an all-gender restroom with boys. Her request was simple. The response she received was not.

Instead of addressing safety, the adults redirected the conversation to bathroom cleanliness and procedures.

This is not about hygiene.
This is about protecting children.

When a child has the courage to speak up and the adults deflect, that is a moral failure. Jesus warned clearly about causing “little ones” to stumble—and ignoring a child’s cry for protection is not neutral.

Where are the adults?

Watch A Venezuelan’s Warning to Americans Embracing Socialism | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher from Truth Over Trend with . Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

A Venezuelan’s Warning to Americans Embracing Socialism | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherTruth Over TrendApril 14, 2026•8:43SummaryWhat happens when ideas sound good—but reality says otherwise?

In this video, a man who lived through Venezuela’s collapse confronts young Americans embracing socialism. What they believe is sincere—but sincerity doesn’t make it true.

History shows a consistent pattern: economic mismanagement, government overreach, and ultimately suffering for the people. Venezuela, once one of the richest nations in South America, now faces poverty, shortages, and mass migration. 

The warning is simple: ideas have consequences.

This isn’t about politics—it’s about truth over trend.

An Imam Just Proved Charlie Kirk's Final Warning | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherTruth Over TrendMatthew MaherJuly 6, 2026•2:07SummaryPastor Matthew Maher responds to an imam's explanation of Quran 9:29 through the lens of biblical truth and Christian discernment.

The video examines the imam's statements, reflects on one of Charlie Kirk's final public warnings, and contrasts the message of the cross with the ideology of the sword.

Christians are called to love their enemies, pray for those who persecute them, and faithfully proclaim the gospel. But biblical love never requires ignoring dangerous ideas or pretending every worldview is the same.

Truth matters. Ideas have consequences. And every claim should be tested by the Word of God, not the spirit of the age.

"Test all things; hold fast what is good." (1 Thessalonians 5:21)

Antichrist Advancing: Post-Christian, Pre-Islamic - (The Pattern Repeating In The West) | M. MaherJuly 31, 2025•56:30SummaryIs the West falling to Islam—or falling away from Christ?

In this urgent Signs of the Times message, Pastor Matthew Maher exposes how Islam is not just expanding by birthrate or immigration, but by filling the spiritual vacuum left by a post-Christian culture. What happened in Turkey and Europe is now happening in America: demoralize, destabilize, Islamize.

This is not about attacking Muslims. It’s about confronting a counterfeit system that denies Christ and thrives where truth has been cast out. From Dearborn to New York, from soft infiltration to cultural strongholds—this is the pattern repeating in the West.

chunks.title: What The First Horse Started, The Next 3 Finish (Seals 2-4) [#21] | Revelation 6:3-8 | Matthew Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Watch What The First Horse Started, The Next 3 Finish (Seals 2-4) [#21] | Revelation 6:3-8 | Matthew Maher from Revelation with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

What The First Horse Started, The Next 3 Finish (Seals 2-4) [#21] | Revelation 6:3-8 | Matthew MaherRevelationMatthew MaherApril 26, 2026•51:30SummaryThe first horse brought deception. Now the consequences ride.

In this message we open the next three seals of Revelation 6 and follow the red, black, and pale horses as they unleash war, famine, and death on a Christ-rejecting world. This is not random chaos — this is divine consequence. Seal by seal. Horse by horse. In order. In consequence.

What the white horse promised, the red horse removes. What the red horse destroys, the black horse starves. What the black horse starves, the pale horse buries. And following behind the pale horse — Hades.

A world that rejected the fullness of God will be famished without God.

But there is hope. Because the same Lamb opening these seals holds the keys to Death and Hades. And what belongs to Him — no horse can take.

chunks.title: What The First Horse Started, The Next 3 Finish (Seals 2-4) [#21] | Revelation 6:3-8 | Matthew Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
In this sermon:
• The red horse and the removal of peace — Revelation 6:3-4
• The black horse and engineered scarcity — Revelation 6:5-6
• The pale horse, Death, and Hades — Revelation 6:7-8
• The Greek word toxon — bow, poison, and God's covenant rainbow
• Why judgment is sequential, not random
• The only peace that cannot be taken — Romans 5:1, Colossians 1:20
• Christ holds the keys — Revelation 1:18

Scriptures referenced: Revelation 6:3-8 | Revelation 1:18 | Romans 5:1 | Colossians 1:20 | Daniel 9:27 | 1 Thessalonians 5:3 | Ezekiel 14:21 | Revelation 12:3 | John 6:35

Deception opens the door. War walks in. Famine empties the table. And death clears the room. But Christ holds the keys.

chunks.text:
Landmark Church
300 E. 8th Street
Ocean City, NJ 08226Discussion Questions1. The sermon established that the four horses ride in sequence — deception leads to war, war leads to famine, famine leads to death. Where do you see this pattern already operating in the world around you? How does recognizing it as spiritual preparation rather than political instability change how you respond to current events?2. Peace was not lost in seal 2 — it was taken. The sermon drew a distinction between the false peace the world chases and the peace purchased at the cross that cannot be removed. What is the difference between the peace the world offers and the peace of God described in Romans 5:1 and Colossians 1:20? Have you experienced that difference personally?3. The black horse reveals that whoever controls the food controls the people. The sermon connected engineered scarcity to expanding antichrist authority. In what ways are you already dependent on systems outside your control? How does that dependency shape your faith and your sense of security?4. The sermon said — a world that rejected the fullness of God will be famished without God. They refused the bread of life and got famine. They refused the living water and got thirst. The shape of the punishment is the exact shape of what they refused. What does this tell us about the nature of God's judgment? Is it cruel — or is it consequence?5. Christ holds the keys of Death and Hades — Revelation 1:18. The pale horse has power but Christ has the keys. What is the practical difference between knowing about Christ and actually knowing Christ — especially in light of what these four seals describe? What does it mean for your daily life to be on the right side of those keys?ExploreBibleNotesContinue WatchingCurrently PlayingThe Mark of the Lamb vs. The Mark of the Beast | Revelation 14:1-5 [#39] chunks.text: Sermon Notes‍‍• A world at war with God will eventually be given over to the wrath of God.When He opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying, "Come and see." Another horse, fiery red, went out. And it was granted to the one who sat on it to take peace from the earth, and that people should kill one another; and there was given to him a great sword. — Revelation 6:3-4• The only way to have peace with God is to receive the peace of God through the Son of God.When He opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature say, "Come and see." So I looked, and behold, a black horse, and he who sat on it had a pair of scales in his hand. And I heard a voice in the midst of the four living creatures saying, "A quart of wheat for a denarius, and three quarts of barley for a denarius; and do not harm the oil and the wine." — Revelation 6:5-6• A world that rejected the fullness of God will be famished without God.When He opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature saying, "Come and see." So I looked, and behold, a pale horse. And the name of him who sat on it was Death, and Hades followed with him. And power was given to them over a fourth of the earth, to kill with sword, with hunger, with death, and by the beasts of the earth. — Revelation 6:7-8• Jesus Christ has been to Death and Hades and came back holding the keys.• We must not forget—hell breaks loose on earth because the Lamb is breaking the seals in heaven.Additional Scriptures Referenced: Romans 1:18-32 | Daniel 9:27 | Revelation 12:3 | 1 Thessalonians 5:3 | Psalm 103:19 | Romans 5:1 | Colossians 1:20 | Revelation 1:18 | Ezekiel 14:21 | John 6:35View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and GiveGive to support the mission of Landmark and help reach people with the gospel.Ways to GiveWays to GiveWays to GiveSermonsMore Sermons & ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextIn The Church But Not Of The Church: Who Is Jude? Appointed to Power: Divine Favor for Direct Access | Genesis 41:38-43 | Shawn HylandOctober 19, 2025•40:24SummaryIn this timely message, we will explore how God sovereignly uses human government to elevate His people into positions of influence and authority. From Joseph in Egypt to Daniel in Babylon, to Mordecai in Persia, Scripture reveals a consistent pattern: those appointed by kings, emperors, and governors often wield greater impact than the rulers themselves.

These appointed officials—though humanly selected—carry divine favor, possess direct access to the chief executive, and exercise delegated authority to protect, provide for, and advocate on behalf of God’s people.

As New Jersey prepares to elect a new governor this November, we must recognize the spiritual and practical significance of this moment. The winner will appoint dozens of unnamed individuals to govern our families, shape education, and influence religious liberty. Their decisions will either favor or frustrate the people of God.

chunks.title: Appointed to Power: Divine Favor for Direct Access | Genesis 41:38-43 |  Shawn Hyland | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Join us as we examine the biblical record and reflect on the modern implications of executive appointments. This is not just a study of ancient empires—it’s a call to spiritual discernment and civic engagement in our own time.

chunks.text:
Landmark Church
300 E. 8th Street
Ocean City, NJ 08226Discussion QuestionsKing Solomon wrote Proverbs 2900 years ago. In Proverbs 6 he gives some very sound financial advice which is wise in our day. Solomons warns that we should not be surety for another person. What does that mean? Have you ever put yourself in that position?Solomons advises that we avoid laziness by considering the ant. There are at least three things that ants do that would certainly serve us well if we imitated them. Ants are diligent…they don’t have to be told what to do. Ants know how to prepare for the seasons. Ants leave a trail to success. Explain how each of these disciplines relates to our livesSolomon says that Ants store up their food in the summer. That is to prepare for the coming winter. We live in a system of constant and predictable change. If we understand that, we will not be caught unprepared. chunks.text: Sermon NotesProverbs 8:1-3Does not wisdom cry out,And understanding lift up her voice?She takes her stand on the top of the high hill,Beside the way, where the paths meet.She cries out by the gates, at the entry of the city,At the entrance of the doors:Spurgeon“When the ungodly smile upon us their flattery is cruel; when the righteous smite us their faithfulness is kind.”Proverbs 6: Avoid the Five things that will Wreck your Life-Avoid Unwise Financial Entanglements: Proverbs 6:1-5-Avoid Laziness by Choosing Diligence: Proverbs 6:6-11-Avoid the Schemers (Square Rooters): Proverbs 6:12-15-Avoid the 7 Pillars of Wickedness: Proverbs 6:16-19-Avoid Sexual Sin: Proverbs 6:20-35Avoid Unwise Financial EntanglementsProverbs 6:1-5My son, if you become surety for your friend,If you have shaken hands in pledge for a stranger,You are snared by the words of your mouth;You are taken by the words of your mouth.So do this, my son, and deliver yourself;For you have come into the hand of your friend:Go and humble yourself;Plead with your friend.Give no sleep to your eyes,Nor slumber to your eyelids.Deliver yourself like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter,And like a bird from the hand of the fowler.Avoid Laziness by Choosing DiligenceProverbs 6:6-11Go to the ant, you sluggard!Consider her ways and be wise,7 Which, having no captain,Overseer or ruler,8 Provides her supplies in the summer,And gathers her food in the harvest.9 How long will you slumber, O sluggard?When will you rise from your sleep?10 A little sleep, a little slumber,A little folding of the hands to sleep—11 So shall your poverty come on you like a prowler,And your need like an armed man.“The activity of any individual ant seemed to have little impact. Nor was it apparent how a single grain of sand had much to do with the big picture of what was forming.”“Breakthrough results come by a series of good decisions, diligently executed, and accumulated one on top of the other.”“I am resolved never to lose one moment of time, but to improve it, the most profitable way I possibly can.”Matthew 6:19-21“Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moths and vermin destroy, and where thieves break in and steal. Before Revelation (Series Opener): Heaven’s View of History | Revelation 12 | Matthew MaherRevelationMatthew MaherAugust 31, 2025•52:16SummaryWelcome to The Last Revelation: The Countdown to the Kingdom. In this opening message to our Revelation Series, Pastor Matthew Maher takes us to Revelation 12—not to start at the end, but to understand the beginning of the battle. Before Revelation: Heaven’s View of History reveals the spiritual war that shaped the world—from Satan’s rebellion in heaven to the ongoing conflict that impacts our lives today.

This isn’t just prophecy—it’s a panoramic look behind the scenes of history. Discover why Revelation 12 is the theological center of the book, how the dragon (Satan) wages war against God’s people, and why the Lamb’s victory means we can overcome by His blood and our bold testimony.

You’ll see how God protects, preserves, and empowers His people—even when the enemy rages.

300 E. 8th Street
Ocean City, NJ 08226Discussion QuestionsWhy be might beginning a Revelation study in chapter 12 (instead of chapter 1) help us see the “big picture” of spiritual warfare before diving into the details of seals, trumpets, and bowls, etc.?Revelation 12 connects back to Genesis 3:15 (“enmity between the serpent and the woman, and her Seed”). How does this help us understand the continuity of God’s plan from Eden to the end times?The dragon is identified as Satan (Rev. 12:9), yet his influence is seen through earthly kingdoms (Daniel 7). What does this teach us about the relationship between spiritual forces and human governments?John leaps from the birth and ascension of Christ (Rev. 12:5) to Israel’s flight during the Tribulation (Rev. 12:6). What does this prophetic “time gap” reveal about how God sees history compared to how we measure it?Michael and his angels prevail over Satan in heaven (Rev. 12:7–8). What does this tell us about angelic warfare, and how should it shape the way we think about unseen realities affecting earth?Verse 11 says believers overcome by the blood of the Lamb, the word of their testimony, and not loving their lives unto death. Which of these three is most challenging for you personally, and why?Revelation 12 ends with Satan targeting the “offspring” who keep God’s commandments and the testimony of Jesus (v.17). How does this explain both the rise of anti-Israel sentiment and the increase of hostility toward faithful Christians in our world today?ExploreBibleNotesContinue WatchingCurrently PlayingThe Mark of chunks.text: Sermon NotesRevelation is not just the end of the story—it reveals the war that shaped the whole story.Revelation 12:1-2Now a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet, and on her head a garland of twelve stars. Then being with child, she cried out in labor and in pain to give birth.Revelation 12:3-4And another sign appeared in heaven: behold, a great, fiery red dragon having seven heads and ten horns, and seven diadems on his heads. His tail drew a third of the stars of heaven and threw them to the earth. And the dragon stood before the woman who was ready to give birth, to devour her Child as soon as it was born.Revelation Genesis 3 Spoken Word VideoRevelation 12:5She bore a male Child who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron. And her Child was caught up to God and His throne.Revelation 12:6Then the woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, that they should feed her there one thousand two hundred and sixty days.Revelation Zoom-In From Ascension To Tribulation VideoRevelation 12:7-9And war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels fought with the dragon; and the dragon and his angels fought, but they did not prevail, nor was a place found for them in heaven any longer. So the great dragon was cast out, that serpent of old, called the Devil and Satan, who deceives the whole world; he was cast to the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.What happens in heaven impacts what happens on earth — and the God who wins above will keep His people below.Revelation 12:10-12Then I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, “Now salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of His Christ have come, for the accuser of our brethren, who accused them before our God day and night, has been cast down. And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives to the death. Therefore rejoice, O heavens, and you who dwell in them! Woe to the inhabitants of the earth and the sea! For the devil has come down to you, having great wrath, because he knows that he has a short time.Revelation 12:13-16Now when the dragon saw that he had been cast to the earth, he persecuted the woman who gave birth to the male Child. But the woman was given two wings of a great eagle, that she might fly into the wilderness to her place, where she is nourished for a time and times and half a time, from the presence of the serpent. So the serpent spewed water out of his mouth like a flood after the woman, that he might cause her to be carried away by the flood. But the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed up the flood which the dragon had spewed out of his mouth.Satan’s reach is real, but God’s rescue is greater.Revelation 12:17And the dragon was enraged with the woman, and he went to make war with the rest of her offspring, who keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.From Genesis to Revelation: When Satan can’t destroy the covenant root, he attacks the covenant fruit.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and GiveGive to support the mission of Landmark and help reach people with the gospel.Ways to GiveWays to GiveWays to GiveSermonsMore Sermons & ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextTruth Conceived vs. Truth Believed | John 8:1-11 | Nick Johnson | Landmark ChurchTruth Conceived vs. Truth Believed | John 8:1-11 | Nick Johnson | Landmark ChurchTruth Conceived vs. Truth Believed | John 8:1-11 | Nick Johnson | Landmark ChurchThe Spirit Of The Antichrist | Matthew Maher | Sermon Moment | Landmark ChurchThe Spirit Of The Antichrist | Matthew Maher | Sermon Moment | Landmark ChurchThe Spirit Of The Antichrist | Matthew Maher | Sermon Moment | Landmark ChurchEsther - The Background and Backbone of the Book (Chapter 1) | Matthew Maher | Coastal Christian OCEsther - The Background and Backbone of the Book (Chapter 1) | Matthew Maher | Coastal Christian OCEsther - The Background and Backbone of the Book (Chapter 1) | Matthew Maher | Coastal Christian OCPsalm 14: No God, No Good! chunks.title: Avoid The Five Things That Will Wreck Your Life: Part 2 (Proverbs 6) | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Sermon NotesProverbs 13:4The soul of a lazy man desires, and has nothing;But the soul of the diligent shall be made richAvoid the Five things that will Wreck your Life1. Avoid Unwise Financial Entanglements: Proverbs 6:1-52. Avoid Laziness by Choosing Diligence: Proverbs 6:6-113. Avoid the Schemers (Square Rooters): Proverbs 6:12-154. Avoid the 7 Pillars of Wickedness: Proverbs 6:16-195. Avoid Sexual Sin: Proverbs 6:20-35Avoid the Schemers (Square Rooters)Proverbs 6:12-15A worthless person, a wicked man,Walks with a perverse mouth;13 He winks with his eyes,He shuffles his feet,He points with his fingers;14 Perversity is in his heart,He devises evil continually,He sows discord.15 Therefore his calamity shall come suddenly;Suddenly he shall be broken without remedy.“Sowers of Discord” sow the seeds of bitterness, anger, distrust, and hatred into the ground of other people’s hearts. These actions do not come from the spirit of God but birth from hell from the deceiver the devil.Avoid the 7 Pillars of WickednessProverbs 6:16-19These six things the Lord hates,Yes, seven are an abomination to Him:17 A proud look,A lying tongue,Hands that shed innocent blood,18 A heart that devises wicked plans,Feet that are swift in running to evil,19 A false witness who speaks lies,And one who sows discord among brethren.“There is a spiritual force behind the world scene which by means of “the things that are in the world” is seeking to enmesh men in its system.”Avoid Sexual SinProverbs 6:20-35My son, keep your father’s command,And do not forsake the law of your mother.21 Bind them continually upon your heart;Tie them around your neck.22 When you roam, they will lead you;When you sleep, they will keep you;And when you awake, they will speak with you.23 For the commandment is a lamp,And the law a light;Reproofs of instruction are the way of life,24 To keep you from the evil woman,From the flattering tongue of a seductress.25 Do not lust after her beauty in your heart,Nor let her allure you with her eyelids.26 For by means of a harlotA man is reduced to a crust of bread;And an adulteress will prey upon his precious life.Proverbs 6:27-2927 Can a man take fire to his bosom,And his clothes not be burned?28 Can one walk on hot coals,And his feet not be seared?29 So is he who goes in to his neighbor’s wife;Whoever touches her shall not be innocent.Plead with God to take away these desires.Don’t just ask him to keep you from giving into temptation. Ask him to take away any desire for anybody other than your spouse.Feel how revolting and disgusting adultery truly is.Don’t trade permanent pleasures for temporary affairs“Sexual sin and spectacular satisfaction are utterly at odds”….John PiperProverbs 6:30-3530 People do not despise a thiefIf he steals to satisfy himself when he is starving.31 Yet when he is found, he must restore sevenfoldHe may have to give up all the substance of his house.32 Whoever commits adultery with a woman lacks understanding;He who does so destroys his own soul.33 Wounds and dishonor he will get,And his reproach will not be wiped away.34 For jealousy is a husband’s fury;Therefore he will not spare in the day of vengeance.35 He will accept no recompense,Nor will he be appeased though you give many gifts.SevereInevitableUnendingView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerTerence SikoryakCare PastorAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and Watch Built to Stand Together: Striving Side by Side for the Gospel | Philippians 1:27-30| Nick Johnson from  with . Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Built to Stand Together: Striving Side by Side for the Gospel | Philippians 1:27-30| Nick JohnsonFebruary 5, 2026•45:40SummaryThis sermon explores Paul’s call in Philippians 1:27–30 for believers to live in a manner worthy of the gospel by standing firm together in unity and courage. Through vivid biblical teaching and powerful illustrations, we see that perseverance under pressure is not achieved alone but through a church striving side by side in one Spirit and one purpose. Paul’s prayer for ever-growing, Christ-shaped love reveals that unity is both the foundation of spiritual strength and the means God uses to advance the gospel in the midst of suffering. The message challenges personal agendas that fracture the body of Christ and calls believers to sacrificial love that builds one another up. Ultimately, it shows that when the church stands united under pressure, Christ is glorified and the world sees the power of the gospel on display.

Can Men Get Pregnant? When “Trust the Science” Becomes Science Fiction | Truth Over TrendMarch 9, 2026•5:31SummaryDuring a U.S. Senate hearing, Josh Hawley repeatedly asked a medical witness a simple question:

Can men get pregnant?

The exchange happened during a Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee hearing on abortion drugs, where OB-GYN Dr. Nisha Verma was testifying. When pressed for a direct yes-or-no answer, she declined to respond clearly, saying the question was political rather than scientific. 

Hawley pushed back, saying the goal was simply to establish biological reality, noting that science and evidence—not politics—should guide medicine. 

The moment quickly went viral because it revealed something deeper happening in our culture. When basic biological truths become difficult to say out loud, something has shifted.

As Romans 1:22 says: “Professing to be wise, they became fools.”

Men cannot get pregnant. That’s not hate. That’s not politics. That’s biology.

When medicine cannot affirm what is plainly true, science stops being governed by evidence—and starts being governed by ideology.

Candace Owens & Blue’s Clues Christianity: When Discernment Becomes Delusion | Matthew MaherMatthew MaherFebruary 15, 2026•11:07SummaryCandace Owens has turned the aftermath of Charlie Kirk’s murder into something it was never meant to be: a public conspiracy hunt.

Instead of honoring the gravity of the moment, people are chasing “clues,” spinning narratives, and feeding the internet’s obsession with speculation, while the enemy’s oldest strategy is working again: distraction from the Word of God and the Work of God.

In this video, Pastor Matthew Maher addresses the danger of replacing discernment with suspicion, and why Christians must refuse to become addicted to outrage, rumor, and endless rabbit trails.

This is not a game of Clue, nor is it Blue’s Clues. This is real life. And truth is not found in internet theories, it is found in the Word of God.
Enough with the clues. Open your Bible.

chunks.text:
Watch Broken for Battle: Strength Under the Rein | Matthew 5:5-6 | Nick Johnson | Landmark Church from Sermon on the Mount with Nick Johnson. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Broken for Battle: Strength Under the Rein | Matthew 5:5-6 | Nick Johnson | Landmark ChurchSermon on the MountNick JohnsonJuly 2, 2026•38:15SummaryThis sermon continues through the Beatitudes by examining Jesus’ words, “Blessed are the meek” and “Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness.” Using the image of a trained warhorse, it shows that biblical meekness is not weakness, but strength held under the control of God’s Spirit. The sermon then connects that controlled strength to a deep hunger for righteousness — both the longing to be made right with God and the longing to see the world made right under Christ. Ultimately, Jesus promises that this hunger will be satisfied in Him, as He fills His people with His righteousness now and will one day renew the whole earth in righteousness.

Landmark Church
300 E. 8th Street
Ocean City, NJ 08226Discussion Questions1. The sermon describes meekness not as weakness but as "power under control" — like a warhorse trained to hold steady under fire. Where in your own life do you find it hardest to hold back and wait on God rather than seizing control yourself?2. Jesus says the meek "do not grab what God has promised to give, but trust Him to give it in His time." Is there a situation in your life right now where you're tempted to force an outcome rather than wait on God? What makes that kind of trust difficult?3. The message draws a tight connection between hungering to be made righteous and hungering to see righteousness done in the world. How have you experienced that connection personally — does your desire to grow closer to God fuel a deeper concern for justice and the people around you?4. The sermon offers three questions to test whether anger is righteous or sinful: What set it off? Where is it driving? And is it under control? Think of a recent moment when you felt strong anger — how does it hold up against those three questions?5. The promise Jesus gives is "they shall be filled" — not might be, but shall be. How does the certainty of that promise change the way you carry your longings, your frustrations, and your hunger for things to be made right?ExploreBibleNotesContinue WatchingCurrently PlayingYou chunks.text:
Watch Bowed Necks or Stiff Necks? The Response Revealed The Spirit | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher from  with . Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Bowed Necks or Stiff Necks? The Response Revealed The Spirit | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherMay 18, 2026•2:25SummaryIronically, George Floyd and Charlie Kirk shared the same birthday.

And both deaths became national moments centered around the neck.

But the responses could not have been more different.

One response erupted into rage, riots, destruction, and chaos.
The other led millions toward prayer, mourning, vigils, and peaceful remembrance.

Truth Over Trend examines what those very different responses may reveal beneath the surface of culture:
because what flows out of a movement often reveals the spirit behind it.

Jesus said:
“You will know them by their fruits.” — Matthew 7:16

This is not about celebrating anyone’s death.
It’s about discerning the fruit produced in the aftermath.

Very different responses.
Very different spirits.

chunks.text:
Watch Can You Buy Deliverance? | Responding to "Apostle" Kathryn Crick | Truth Over Trend w/ Matthew Maher from Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Can You Buy Deliverance? | Responding to "Apostle" Kathryn Crick | Truth Over Trend w/ Matthew MaherTruth Over TrendMatthew MaherJuly 27, 2026•3:09SummaryCan God's power be unlocked with money?

In this episode of Truth Over Trend, Pastor Matthew Maher responds to a clip from "Apostle" Katherine Crick in which a desperate mother is encouraged to "sow a seed" while her son lies on the ground in need of deliverance.

This isn't a discussion about whether God still heals or delivers. I believe He does. This is about whether Scripture teaches that a financial offering is a "key" to receiving God's power.

Jesus never told people to pay before He healed them. He never attached a price tag to deliverance. He never turned God's power into a transaction. Instead, when the disciples were unable to cast out a demon, Jesus said: "This kind can come out by nothing but prayer and fasting." (Mark 9:29)

Peter also warned the church: "By covetousness they will exploit you with deceptive words..." (2 Peter 2:3)

chunks.title: Can You Buy Deliverance? | Responding to "Apostle" Kathryn Crick | Truth Over Trend w/ Matthew Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
As Christians, we are commanded to test every teaching by the Word of God. The question isn't whether something appears spiritual or supernatural. The question is whether it is biblical.

Truth must always triumph over trend.

Scripture Referenced:
• Mark 9:29 
• 2 Peter 2:3 
• 2 Corinthians 11:13–15 
• Matthew 10:8 

If this video encouraged you to think biblically, consider subscribing and sharing it with someone who values God's truth above cultural trends.

That’s the larger pattern I’ve been warning about in 'Discerning The Devil’s Playbook': different players, same plays. The enemy doesn’t care who carries the lie as long as the lie keeps moving.

In this Truth Over Trend response, Matthew Maher breaks down Charlie’s warning and why Christians need discernment to recognize the worldview beneath the headlines.

Featuring: The "Freedom Edition" of 'Discerning The Devil’s Playbook' expands that warning for the moment we’re living in now.

Christianity Is NOT Socialism: A Biblical Response to Tucker Carlson Segment | Truth Over TrendApril 21, 2026•6:17SummaryA recent conversation on Tucker Carlson’s show raised a bold claim—that Christianity, at its core, is a form of socialism.

It sounds compassionate.
It sounds thoughtful.
But it’s not biblical.

In this video, we break down what Scripture actually says about generosity, ownership, work, and giving—and why the early church was never a model of forced redistribution, but of Spirit-led, voluntary sacrifice.

The difference matters. Because:

Socialism is built on compulsion. Christianity is built on transformation And confusing the two doesn’t elevate the gospel—it distorts it.

Key Scriptures:

Exodus 20:15, 17
Acts 5:4
2 Corinthians 9:7
2 Thessalonians 3:10

Biblical charity is not government policy. It’s the overflow of a changed heart

chunks.title: Christians Called A ‘Cancer’? This Is How Persecution Begins | Truth Over Trend w/ Matthew Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Watch Christians Called A ‘Cancer’? This Is How Persecution Begins | Truth Over Trend w/ Matthew Maher from  with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Christians Called A ‘Cancer’? This Is How Persecution Begins | Truth Over Trend w/ Matthew MaherMatthew MaherFebruary 23, 2026•4:49SummaryWhen Christians are labeled a “cancer,” it’s not just criticism — it’s dehumanization.
In this video, Pastor Matthew Maher responds to rhetoric that paints Christianity as inherently hateful and morally corrupt. Disagreement is one thing. But history shows a dangerous pattern when language shifts from debate to disease metaphors.

First, a group is caricatured. Then, they are assigned words and motives they never spoke. Then, hostility toward them feels justified. That’s how persecution begins — one lie at a time.

Biblical Christianity does not teach hatred. But when lies about Christianity are believed, hatred toward Christians can suddenly feel righteous. Truthful speech gets recast as “hate speech,” not because it is hateful, but because truth itself is now hated.

In an Isaiah 5:20 world — when good is called evil and evil is called good — persecution no longer feels wrong. It feels moral.

This isn’t about politics. It’s about pattern recognition.

chunks.title: Colin Kaepernick: The Danger of Seeing Everything Through Race | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Watch Colin Kaepernick: The Danger of Seeing Everything Through Race | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher from Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Colin Kaepernick: The Danger of Seeing Everything Through Race | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherTruth Over TrendMatthew MaherSeptember 29, 2026•2:50SummaryIn this Truth Over Trend response, Pastor Matthew Maher examines Colin Kaepernick’s view of race, identity, and racism—and the danger of allowing race to become the lens through which we interpret everything.

Kaepernick’s story includes experiences with racism that should be called what they are: wrong. But there is a difference between acknowledging that racism shaped some of your experiences and allowing race to become the lens through which you interpret all of your experiences.

Racism is real. But race is a terrible religion.

The gospel doesn’t pretend ethnicity doesn’t exist, nor does it teach us to ignore our differences. It refuses to let those differences determine our dignity or become our ultimate identity.

Our deepest problem isn’t melanin—it’s sin. And our greatest solution isn’t racial consciousness—it’s Christ.

CNN Didn’t Expect This Answer About ICE | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherFebruary 5, 2026•3:46SummaryIn this powerful commentary, we examine a viral CNN interview involving the former father-in-law of Renee Goode and the growing national conversation surrounding ICE, law enforcement, and cultural division in Minneapolis. While many media outlets attempt to shape narratives through political framing, this unexpected response offers something deeper: biblical clarity.

Rather than blaming the ICE agent or weaponizing grief, the speaker emphasizes a Christian worldview rooted in Scripture. He reminds viewers of the call to love our neighbor while also acknowledging a sobering truth: choices have consequences, and obedience matters.

This video explores how Christian responsibility does not conflict with lawful authority, and why loving others can coexist with respecting order and justice. In a society increasingly rejecting God’s design, tragedy becomes revelatory, exposing what is spiritually broken beneath the surface.

“Death to America” — What This Really Means | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherMarch 16, 2026•5:42SummaryWhat does it mean when a government leads crowds in chanting “Death to America” and “Death to Israel”? This isn’t just geopolitical tension. It reveals something deeper.

Since the Islamic Revolution in 1979, chants like these have been a regular part of regime rallies in Iran. But Scripture reminds us that behind political power there are often spiritual forces at work.

In Daniel 10, the prophet prayed and discovered that the answer to his prayer was delayed because of conflict in the unseen realm.

“The prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me twenty-one days…” — Daniel 10:13

Empires rise and fall on earth, but the Bible teaches that spiritual warfare often operates behind world events. That is why believers must not lose sight of the real battle.

In the middle of a spiritual war, casual Christianity will produce casualties. So we pray — like Daniel prayed. 

Because when nations rage, we must remember: There is a throne above every throne. And prayer is how we step into that throne room.

Watch Does the Bible Really Tell Christians to Handle Snakes? | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher from  with . Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Does the Bible Really Tell Christians to Handle Snakes? | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherSeptember 21, 2026•2:50SummaryWhy do some Christians handle venomous snakes in church—and do they actually have biblical support for it?

Snake-handling churches point to Mark 16:18: “They will take up serpents.” But Acts 28 shows us what that protection actually looked like when a venomous snake unexpectedly fastened onto Paul.

Paul didn’t go looking for the snake. The snake found Paul.

There’s a massive difference between trusting God when danger finds you and deliberately creating danger in the name of faith. Matthew 4 reminds us that biblical faith does not manufacture danger and then demand God’s protection.

That’s not trusting God. That’s testing God.

Put down the snake and pick up the Bible.

chunks.title: Do Mormons Worship A Different God? | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Watch Do Mormons Worship A Different God? | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher from Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Do Mormons Worship A Different God? | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherTruth Over TrendMatthew MaherJune 15, 2026•6:37SummaryMormonism teaches that there is a Heavenly Mother, that men can become gods, women can become goddesses, and that God the Father is part of a divine family structure.

But where are these doctrines found in Scripture?

In this Truth Over Trend response, Pastor Matthew Maher examines one of Mormonism's most distinctive teachings and compare it to the clear teaching of the Bible.

Topics covered:

• The doctrine of a Heavenly Mother
• Can human beings become gods?
• What does Elohim actually mean?
• Joseph Smith and extra-biblical revelation
• Why Christianity begins with Scripture, not speculation

The central question is not whether these teachings are sincere.
The question is whether they are true.

Truth Over Trend:
When God's Word is no longer enough, people will always invent new revelations.
And every new revelation eventually creates a different god.
And a different god always leads to a different gospel.

Facing The Fire: Kelvin Cochran | Landmark Stories | Landmark ChurchOctober 2, 2025•58:08SummaryFormer Atlanta Fire Chief Kelvin Cochran shares his powerful story of faith, conviction, and courage in the face of public persecution. In this Landmark Stories event, Chief Cochran opens up about his journey from humble beginnings in Shreveport, Louisiana, to becoming “America’s Fire Chief,” to the fiery trial that tested his faith when he was fired for living out biblical truth.

Hear how God used the flames of adversity to strengthen his testimony and why his message is so timely for the church today.

📖 Title: Facing The Fire: The Faith That Brought "America's Fire Chief" Through the Flames of Persecution by Kelvin Cochran 

Topics Covered:
 • Cochran’s rise from poverty to national leadership
 • The controversy that cost him his career in Atlanta
 • The lawsuit that shook the nation and ended in victory
 • How his faith sustained him through trials
 • What it means to stand boldly for Christ in today’s culture

Faith That Feeds | John 6:52-59 | Nick Johnson | Landmark ChurchOctober 30, 2025•42:02SummaryThis sermon explores Jesus’ teaching in John 6, tracing the movement from belief to abiding. It shows how many followed Christ for what He provided, but only true disciples remained when His words demanded trust and dependence. Through examples like Richard Jewell’s “trial by media,” it warns against faith built on appearances and calls believers to a faith that endures when perception turns hostile. The message urges listeners to redeem their time by seeking God’s will and feeding daily on the life of Christ. Ultimately, it challenges the church to cultivate abiding faith—steady, tested, and sustained by union with the Bread of Life.

Faithful In The Footnotes | 2 Timothy 4:19-22 | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church2 TimothyMatthew MaherAugust 3, 2025•47:53SummaryAt the end of Paul’s final letter, we find a list of forgotten names—Prisca and Aquila, Onesiphorus, Erastus, Trophimus—seemingly small mentions, but eternally significant. In this powerful message from Landmark Church, Pastor Matthew Maher reminds us that the kingdom remembers what the world forgets and that hidden faithfulness leaves an eternal imprint.
Whether you serve in a pulpit, a classroom, or a city hall, your obedience matters. God sees it, honors it, and uses it. Be encouraged: your life doesn’t have to be loud to be lasting.

chunks.text:
Watch Faithfully Free Until The Finish: A Declaration of Dependence | 2 Timothy 4:6-8 | Matthew Maher from 2 Timothy with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Faithfully Free Until The Finish: A Declaration of Dependence | 2 Timothy 4:6-8 | Matthew Maher2 TimothyMatthew MaherJuly 6, 2025•47:05SummaryAs the world fights to be independent of God, the believer is called to make a declaration of dependence on Christ. In this powerful July 4th weekend message, we look at the words of Paul as he nears the end of his race—not holding back, but pouring out his life for the glory of God.
Just as the 56 signers of the Declaration of Independence risked everything for earthly liberty, Paul gave everything for eternal freedom. This message challenges us to live like Paul—fighting the good fight, keeping the faith, and finishing the race—not with self-preservation, but with a poured-out life of worship. Because when freedom is divorced from faith, it becomes rebellion—but when it bows to Christ, it becomes righteousness.

chunks.text:
Watch First-Degree Premeditated Christianity: Faith On Trial | 2 Timothy 3:12-15 | Matthew Maher from 2 Timothy with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

First-Degree Premeditated Christianity: Faith On Trial | 2 Timothy 3:12-15 | Matthew Maher2 TimothyMatthew MaherJune 8, 2025•40:25SummaryIn an age where truth is twisted and godliness is treated like guilt, what does it mean to live a faith so bold, it could be considered criminal? In this powerful message, Pastor Matthew Maher unpacks 2 Timothy 3:12–15, challenging believers to stand firm in the truth, abide in Scripture, and live lives that reflect the Spirit of Christ—even when the world pushes back.

Persecution may not always come with chains, but it often comes through pressure, isolation, and deception. Are you living a life so surrendered to Jesus that it leaves evidence? If Christianity were outlawed—would there be enough to convict you?

Watch From Doubt to “Yes I Will”: A Worship Leader’s Story | Landmark Stories #6 w/ Judd Harris from  with . Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

From Doubt to “Yes I Will”: A Worship Leader’s Story | Landmark Stories #6 w/ Judd HarrisDecember 18, 2025•50:49SummaryThey say a dead man cannot sing and spiritually that’s true. In this episode of Landmark Stories, Matthew Maher sits down with Judd Harris of Vertical Worship for a conversation about doubt, calling, rejection, and the worship that heals.

Judd shares the moment he walked out of a worship service feeling flat and then heard the Lord speak, “I’m with you.” From writing songs as a teenager to being invited into leadership, from not making the Liberty Worship Collective at first to returning and making it the second time, Judd’s story is a case study in how God uses a small yes to reshape a life.

You will also hear the behind the scenes journey of how Judd joined Vertical Worship, how he ended up singing “Yes I Will,” and why worship is not performance but formation. This is a conversation about beholding Jesus, learning to serve without chasing platforms, and allowing worship to move from a stage into the other ninety five percent of life.

If you are navigating rejection, calling, or spiritual dryness, this episode is for you.
Guest: Judd Harris of Vertical Worship

chunks.text:
Watch From The Great Tribulation To The Great Throne | Revelation 7:9-17 [#25] | Matthew Maher from Revelation with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

From The Great Tribulation To The Great Throne | Revelation 7:9-17 [#25] | Matthew MaherRevelationMatthew MaherMay 31, 2026•49:20SummaryIn Revelation 7, John sees an innumerable multitude from every nation, tribe, people, and tongue standing before the throne and before the Lamb. These are the ones who came out of the Great Tribulation — washed white by the blood of the Lamb, clothed in victory, and shepherded forever in the presence of God.

This message explores:

• The connection between the 144,000 and the great multitude
• “Who is able to stand?” from Revelation 6:17
• The meaning of the white robes and palm branches
• Why redemption in Christ is the only unity that stands the test of time
• “Religion whitewashes. The Lamb washes white.”
• The Lamb who became the Shepherd
• God dwelling with His people again

From the Great Tribulation to the Great Throne, Revelation 7 reminds us that the Lamb loses none of His own.

Revelation 7:9–17

chunks.text: Sermon Notes• The 144,000 were not merely sealed to survive but sealed to serve."In those days ten men from every language of the nations shall grasp the sleeve of a Jewish man, saying, 'Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.'" — Zechariah 8:23After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no one could number, of all nations, tribes, peoples, and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, with palm branches in their hands… — Revelation 7:9• Redemption in Christ is the only DEI that stands the test of time.• They are able to stand before the throne and the Lamb because the Lamb left His throne.And crying out with a loud voice, saying, "Salvation belongs to our God who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!" — Revelation 7:10• Salvation was won by God — which means it was never yours to lose.All the angels stood around the throne and the elders and the four living creatures, and fell on their faces before the throne and worshiped God, saying: "Amen! Blessing and glory and wisdom, Thanksgiving and honor and power and might, Be to our God forever and ever. Amen." — Revelation 7:11-12Then one of the elders answered, saying to me, "Who are these arrayed in white robes, and where did they come from?" And I said to him, "Sir, you know." So he said to me, "These are the ones who come out of the great tribulation, and washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb. — Revelation 7:13-14• Religion whitewashes. The Lamb washes white.Therefore they are before the throne of God, and serve Him day and night in His temple. And He who sits on the throne will dwell among them. They shall neither hunger anymore nor thirst anymore; the sun shall not strike them, nor any heat; for the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne will shepherd them and lead them to living fountains of waters. And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes." — Revelation 7:15-17• What the Serpent distorted in Genesis, the Lamb restores in Revelation.Additional Scriptures Referenced: Isaiah 60:3; Fulfillment or Frustration it’s your Choice | Proverbs 13:12-18 | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark ChurchProverbsTerence SikoryakMarch 1, 2026•44:54SummaryFulfillment and frustration do not come from circumstances, but from whether a man remains under God’s authority or insists on governing himself. The fear of the Lord brings the soul into proper order, where the mind submits to truth, the emotions become quiet, and the will yields in obedience, allowing God’s life to flow unhindered. When a man resists correction and clings to self-rule, he may preserve his independence, but he loses inward life and becomes governed by decay rather than by grace. Therefore, in the time remaining, the decisive question is not what a man achieves outwardly, but whether he has surrendered inwardly—because only the surrendered life can know true fulfillment before God.

chunks.title: Glory in the Setbacks: When God Turns You Back to Move You Forward | Exodus 14:1-25 | Nick Johnson | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Watch Glory in the Setbacks: When God Turns You Back to Move You Forward | Exodus 14:1-25 | Nick Johnson from Topical Sermons with . Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Glory in the Setbacks: When God Turns You Back to Move You Forward | Exodus 14:1-25 | Nick JohnsonTopical SermonsDecember 5, 2025•47:49SummaryThis sermon explores how God sometimes leads His people into unexpected setbacks; moments that feel like going backwards, in order to reveal His glory and strengthen their faith. Drawing from Exodus 14, we see Israel trapped at the Red Sea not by accident, but by divine design, as God positions them where only His power can save. In their fear, God moves the pillar of fire behind them, stands between them and destruction, and displays His glory by breaking the wheels of Egypt’s chariots. The same glory that fought for Israel now strengthens believers from within, as Paul prays in Ephesians 3:14–16. Through personal testimony and Scripture, the message calls us to trust God’s hand in our pain, knowing His glory was at work then, is at work now, and will be revealed fully in the days to come.

Watch God's Wisdom in the Christmas Message: Enjoy the Season But Get the Message | Terence Sikoryak from  with . Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

God's Wisdom in the Christmas Message: Enjoy the Season But Get the Message | Terence SikoryakDecember 21, 2025•33:06SummaryChristmas is not just a sentimental tradition, but a moment of divine wisdom calling us to discern God’s greater redemptive plan. Rooted in John 3:16, it reveals the true meaning of Christmas through four realities: humanity’s danger of perishing, God’s loving design to rescue us through Christ, our duty to respond in faith and surrender, and our destiny of eternal life that begins now. Drawing from Proverbs, it contrasts superficial celebration with wise discernment, urging listeners not to miss what God is revealing in the season. Christmas is shown as the fulfillment of God’s long-planned compassion—new life formed through the womb—calling each person to respond personally to the gospel. Ultimately, the message invites us to enjoy Christmas fully, but to do so with wisdom that leads to life, transformation, and eternity with God.

Watch God's Presence In The Absence | 2 Timothy 4:16-18 | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church from 2 Timothy with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

God's Presence In The Absence | 2 Timothy 4:16-18 | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church2 TimothyMatthew MaherJuly 20, 2025•48:16SummaryWhat do you do when everyone walks away? In this powerful message, Pastor Matthew Maher unpacks 2 Timothy 4:16-18 and explores how Paul responded when he was completely abandoned—but not alone. “At my first defense, no one stood with me,” Paul wrote, “but the Lord stood with me and strengthened me.”
Through heartbreak, isolation, and silence, Paul discovered a deeper awareness of God’s presence and purpose. In this sermon, we’re reminded that when people fail us, God fills the gap. When absence surrounds us, His presence meets us with strength, courage, and hope.

He Said "Love Your Neighbor" Then Called Child Protection "Nasty" | Truth Over Trend w/ Matt MaherMatthew MaherFebruary 26, 2026•3:35SummaryIn this video, Pastor Matthew Maher responds to Governor Andy Beshear who invoked Christian language — “love your neighbor” and the Good Samaritan — while calling a bill that protects children “the nastiest piece of anti-LGBTQ legislation” in his state.

Let’s slow down and deal in reality.

The bill:

• Bans so-called gender-affirming procedures for minors

• Protects girls’ private spaces

• Requires schools to inform parents when their child is experiencing gender dysphoria

Since when is protecting children hate?

When good is called evil and evil is called good, we’re not debating policy — we’re witnessing moral inversion (Isaiah 5:20). Protecting children isn’t cruelty. It’s righteousness.

How Then Should We Respond? | Nick Johnson | Landmark ChurchSeptember 18, 2025•40:38SummaryHow Then Should We Respond?, confronts the reality of persecution and the lies that fuel it. From Tertullian’s defense of early Christians to Jesus’ own trial, we see that truth will always be twisted by a world that hates the light. Yet God uses suffering not to break us but to train us in obedience, preparing us for greater faithfulness. And because our lives are hidden with Christ, even death itself becomes victory, not defeat. The call is simple and urgent: stand firm in truth, endure in hope, and live as those already surrendered to Jesus.

I Died at 17 and Came Back to Share This Story | Jonathan Gonzalez #LandmarkstoriesMarch 20, 2025•59:56SummaryWhat happens when your life flashes before your eyes, and you’re left bleeding to death in the back seat of a car at just 17 years old? This is Jonathan Gonzales’ unimaginable story—an encounter with death that forever changed his life and set him on a path to discovering God’s purpose. In this raw and powerful testimony, Jonathan shares the harrowing details of his near-death experience, the struggles that followed, and how one desperate prayer brought him back to life—physically and spiritually. 

This isn’t just another story. It’s a story of survival, redemption, and the undeniable power of faith. From facing unimaginable pain to overcoming addiction, Jonathan’s journey is proof that no matter how dark life gets, there’s always hope. Could his story be the landmark you need to find your way?

chunks.text: Sermon NotesProverbs 30:18-19There are three things which are too wonderful for me,Four which I do not understand:The way of the eagle in the sky,The way of a snake on a rock,The way of a ship in the middle of the sea,And the way of a man with a maiden.Proverbs 10:1A proverb of Solomon.A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son brings grief to his mother.Proverbs 10: How to bring Honor to Your Home1. Live with Righteousness: (Proverbs 10:2-3)2. Be Diligent and Hardworking: (Proverbs 10:4)3. Live with Integrity: (Proverbs 10:9)4. Be Wise in Speech: (Proverbs 10:11)5. Avoid Dishonesty and Deceit: (Proverbs 10:18)6. Show Generosity: (Proverbs 10:22)1. Live with RighteousnessProverbs 10:2-3“Ill-gotten treasures have no lasting value, but righteousness delivers from death.”Luke 12:16-21Jesus tells a parable:“The land of a rich man was very productive. And he began thinking to himself, saying, ‘What shall I do, since I have no place to store my crops?’ And he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and build larger ones, and I will store all my grain and my goods there. And I will say to myself, “You have many goods stored up for many years to come; relax, eat, drink, and enjoy yourself!”’ But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your soul is demanded of you; and as for all that you have prepared, who will own it now?’ Such is the one who stores up treasure for himself, and is not rich in relation to God.”2. Work DiligentlyProverbs 10:4“Lazy hands make for poverty, but diligent hands bring wealth.”Diligence (charuts) in Proverbs is about more than just effort; it’s about skill, wisdom, and care in one’s work. The person who works and lives with diligence, Charuts brings honor to their family.3. Live with IntegrityProverbs 10:9“Whoever walks in integrity walks securely, but whoever takes crooked paths will be found out.”4. Be Wise in SpeechProverbs 10:11“The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.”5. Avoid Dishonesty and DeceitProverbs 10:18“Whoever conceals hatred with lying lips and spreads slander is a fool.”6. Show GenerosityProverbs 10:22“The blessing of the Lord brings wealth, without painful toil for it.”Laurence Shames: The Hunger for More“Personal disasters ranging from cocaine abuse to sundered marriages to alcoholism to suicide were ascribed not to the stresses of failure, or even the stresses seeking success, but rather the disillusionment that came with success itself”Watchman Nee: The Spiritual ManBelievers who live in the soul incline towards either will or mind or emotion.Those who are disposed towards volition, will walk according to their own delight and refuse the will of God.Those whose propensity is towards mind will order their way according to their own wisdom and neglect to receive with quietness, the guidance of the Holy Spirit and their intuition.While those whose natural disposition is emotional, will seek for pleasures in their feelings.No matter the direction of the inclination, one thing in common to all such people: all live in themselves: all live, and what they naturally possessed before, believing the Lord-with talent, ability, eloquence, cleverness, attractiveness, zealousness, or whatever.In principle soul life is natural strength; and manifestation, its expression is either by stubborn unyielding or by self-conceit or by pleasure-seeking.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerTerence SikoryakCare PastorAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and GiveGive to support the mission of Landmark and help reach people with the gospel.Ways to GiveWays to GiveWays to GiveSermonsMore Sermons & ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextIn The Church But Not Of The Church: Who Is Jude? chunks.text:
Watch Is The Church In The Tribulation (The Rapture Isn't A Secret—Pt 2) [#14] | Matt. 24 | Matthew Maher from Revelation with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Is The Church In The Tribulation (The Rapture Isn't A Secret—Pt 2) [#14] | Matt. 24 | Matthew MaherRevelationMatthew MaherFebruary 8, 2026•54:27SummaryFew doctrines generate more confusion than the rapture — not because Scripture is unclear, but because different passages are often flattened into a single event.

In Part 2 of this teaching, we return to the passages people struggle with most: Matthew 24. The “elect.” The last trumpet. The restrainer. Israel and the Church.

Rather than avoiding these texts, we place them in their proper context and allow Scripture to interpret Scripture.

In this message, we explore:
• Why Matthew 24 describes the Second Coming, not the rapture
• Who the “elect” are — and why context matters
• Why the “last trumpet” is not the same trumpet everywhere
• What must be removed before the Antichrist is revealed
• How salvation continues during the Tribulation
• Why distinguishing Israel and the Church is foundational to biblical prophecy
• Why imminence matters for how believers live today

This doctrine was never meant to divide the Church. It was meant to anchor hope, fuel holiness, and produce urgency.
