chunks.text: Sermon NotesMatthew 24 describes the return of the King, not the removal of the Bride.Matthew 24:31And He will send His angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they will gather together His elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.The last trumpet for the Church is not the last trumpet on earth.2 Thessalonians 2:6-8And now you know what is restraining, that he may be revealed in his own time. For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only He who now restrains will do so until He is taken out of the way. And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord will consume with the breath of His mouth and destroy with the brightness of His coming.You cannot have the Antichrist revealed until the Restrainer is removed.The absence of the Church does not mean the absence of salvation.Daniel 9:24“Seventy weeks are determined for your people and your city…”The Church did not replace Israel, fulfill Israel, or erase Israel.You cannot be watching for Christ if you’re watching for Antichrist.Additional Scriptures Referenced: Matthew 24:15–31; Ephesians 1:4-5; Revelation 7:3, 13:7, 14:12; 1 Corinthians 15:51–52; Revelation 8–11; Deuteronomy 30:4, Isaiah 11:11–12, Ezekiel 34:12; Isaiah 11; Zechariah 12–14; Revelation 19–20; 2 Thessalonians 2:1-8; chunks.title: James Talarico's Prayer Was An Anti-Prayer | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Watch James Talarico's Prayer Was An Anti-Prayer | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher from Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

James Talarico's Prayer Was An Anti-Prayer | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherTruth Over TrendMatthew MaherJune 8, 2026•6:03SummaryBefore you can understand a prayer, you must first answer a simple question: Who is God?

Not what values does He inspire.
Not what causes does He support.
Not what feelings does He evoke.

Who is He?

In a recent prayer delivered by Texas Representative James Talarico, the language sounded compassionate, inclusive, and spiritual. But beneath the language of love was a radically different view of God, truth, and Jesus Christ.

The God of Scripture is not a mystery to be discovered through every religion. He has revealed Himself.

Jesus did not claim to be one teacher among many, one path among many, or one name among many. He claimed to be the way, the truth, and the life.

In this response, we examine:
• The danger of religious pluralism
• Why "all paths lead to God" contradicts Christianity
• The difference between God's love and a cosmic force called love
• How Jesus was reduced from Savior to one spiritual option among many

chunks.title: James Talarico's Prayer Was An Anti-Prayer | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
A God who can be anything to everyone is ultimately nothing at all. The real Jesus is not one name among many. He is the name above every name.

chunks.title: James Talarico Says God Is Non-Binary | A Biblical Response | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Watch James Talarico Says God Is Non-Binary | A Biblical Response | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher from Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

James Talarico Says God Is Non-Binary | A Biblical Response | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherTruth Over TrendMatthew MaherJune 29, 2026•4:49SummaryTexas Representative James Talarico claimed that God is non-binary, appealing to Hebrew grammar, Genesis 1, and the image of God to support his argument.

He also argued that transgender children are perfect exactly as they are and that Christians who disagree are using Scripture to hurt children.

But does the Bible actually teach any of this?

In this response, we examine:

• Does Genesis teach that God is both masculine and feminine?
• Does grammatical gender determine God's identity?
• What does Scripture reveal about the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit?
• What does it mean to be made in the image of God?
• Can compassion exist apart from truth?

Every child bears the image of God. Every child has dignity. Every child deserves compassion. But compassion does not give us permission to rewrite Scripture.

Truth Over Trend:
When you have to redefine God, redefine sin, redefine male and female, and redefine love itself to defend your position, your position is no longer coming from heaven.

Josh Howerton & Satan's Counterfeit to Repentance | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherJanuary 4, 2026•3:28SummaryIn this response video, our pastor engages with comments made by Josh Howerton of Lakepointe Church regarding tolerance, repentance, and the responsibility of faithful shepherds in the church.

Josh makes the striking claim that “tolerance is the satanic counterfeit of repentance,” arguing that biblical love does not mean affirming what God condemns, but lovingly calling people to repentance and alignment with God’s Word. In this discussion, we pause, respond, and affirm where Scripture is clear—especially in light of Jesus’ rebukes of churches that tolerated sin in Revelation.

At Landmark Church, we believe:

Truth and love are never opposed

Repentance is a grace, not an attack

Faithful shepherds protect the sheep, even when it’s unpopular

This video reinforces the importance of biblical clarity over cultural pressure, truth over trend, and the loving responsibility pastors have to guard the flock from teachings that ultimately harm souls.

“Be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain…” — Revelation 3:2

Watch Latin Kings Made Him Feared, God Made Him Free | Melvin Negron | Landmark Stories from  with . Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Latin Kings Made Him Feared, God Made Him Free | Melvin Negron | Landmark StoriesSeptember 10, 2026•69:32SummaryWhat happens when the very thing meant to protect you becomes the thing that almost destroys you?

In this powerful episode of Landmark Stories, Melvin Negron shares his remarkable journey from a childhood marked by abuse and trauma, to becoming part of the Latin Kings, one of America's most feared street gangs, to a life radically transformed by Christ.

Melvin opens up about the pain that shaped his early years, the choices that led him deeper into gang life and prison, the unexpected moment behind bars that changed everything, and the friendship that helped point him toward his faith. He also shares how that transformation led him to found Gangsters Gone Godly and join Hog Mob Ministries, where he now brings hope to the very communities and prisons he once knew from the other side.

This is a story about pain, purpose, and the God who meets us in our darkest moments.

No matter where you are in life, Melvin's testimony is a reminder that God knows where you are, and He knows exactly what you need.

To learn more about Melvin's ministry, visit Hog Mob Ministries: https://hogmob.com/

Legacy Discipleship or Legacy Dysfunction? | 2 Timothy 2:2 | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchAugust 17, 2025•37:35SummaryYou will leave a spiritual legacy — but will it be one of discipleship or dysfunction? In this Youth Sunday message, we look at 2 Timothy 2:2 and the Paul–Timothy model of generational discipleship. Learn why the Gospel wasn’t meant to stop with you but to flow through you, and how your link in the Gospel chain can shape generations to come. Featuring the powerful contrast between Jonathan Edwards’ family legacy and Max Jukes’.

Here's the truth: The faith you keep to yourself dies with you, but the faith you pass on will outlive you.

chunks.text: Sermon NotesMan’s issue is not that he glories in something but that he glories in the wrong thing.Psalm 8:1O Lord, our Lord, how excellent is Your name in all the earth, Who have set Your glory above the heavens!As the world maligns the Name of God, we must magnify the Name of God.Psalm 8:2Out of the mouth of babes and nursing infants You have ordained strength, because of Your enemies, that You may silence the enemy and the avenger.Praise is a stronghold that both conforms us to the Lord and confounds the god of this world.Psalm 8:3-5When I consider Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and the stars, which You have ordained, 4 What is man that You are mindful of him, and the son of man that You visit him? 5 For You have made him a little lower than the angels, and You have crowned him with glory and honor.Since man is the crown of God’s creation, the enemy seeks to defy God by de-crowning man.Psalm 8:6-8You have made him to have dominion over the works of Your hands; You have put all things under his feet, 7 all sheep and oxen—even the beasts of the field, 8 the birds of the air, and the fish of the sea that pass through the paths of the seas.The more we move away from the Designer, the more undone the design becomes.Psalm 8:9O Lord, our Lord, how excellent is Your name in all the earth!View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and GiveGive to support the mission of Landmark and help reach people with the gospel.Ways to GiveWays to GiveWays to GiveSermonsMore Sermons & ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextPsalm 18: The Lord Is My Rock | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchPsalmsMatthew MaherPsalm 18: The Lord Is My Rock | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchPsalm 18: The Lord Is My Rock | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchNow What? Marks of a Transformed Christian | Romans 12:9-21 | Aaron Capito | Landmark ChurchTopical SermonsJuly 23, 2026•29:23SummaryWhat does a transformed Christian actually look like? In Romans 12:9–21, the Apostle Paul shows us that the gospel doesn't just change where we're going—it changes how we're living. This message explores the marks of a life transformed by the mercy of God: genuine love, humility, grace toward others, and overcoming evil with good. This sermon challenges and encourages you to not only bear the name of Christ, but to reflect His character in your everyday life.

Mercy Received, Mercy Given: How God’s Mercy Creates Merciful People | Matthew 5:7 | Nick JohnsonJuly 16, 2026•46:11SummaryIn this message from Matthew 5:7, we consider how easily the constant mercies of God can become so familiar that we stop recognizing them. The holiness of God reveals the true weight of mercy, showing that sin must be answered either in the sinner or in a substitute. Jesus Christ is that perfect substitute—the merciful High Priest who bore the judgment His people deserved and secured mercy through the cross. Because believers have received mercy of such magnitude, they are called to extend mercy within the church and to a world still in need of the gospel. Blessed are the merciful, for they shall receive mercy.

Nazism & Progressivism: Same Snake, Different Skins | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchMay 4, 2025•44:54SummaryTwo ideologies. One ancient lie. Same snake—just different skins. 

In this powerful message, Nazism & Progressivism: Same Snake, Different Skins, Pastor Matthew Maher exposes the spiritual deception lurking beneath two seemingly different ideologies. From totalitarian regimes to modern cultural movements, the enemy recycles the same rebellion against God—just with new language and new packaging. Discover how the spirit of the age mirrors the spirit of the Antichrist, and how believers can stand firm in truth when the world demands compromise.

We are watching it unfold in real time.

At some point, you have to stop and ask: Is this rebellion… or is this blindness?

chunks.text:
Watch Not Just Bread, But Life | John 6:1-15 | Nick Johnson | Landmark Church from  with . Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Not Just Bread, But Life | John 6:1-15 | Nick Johnson | Landmark ChurchAugust 21, 2025•47:20SummaryIn John 6:1–15, Jesus feeds over five thousand people with five loaves and two fish. The crowd saw the miracle but missed its meaning — they wanted bread for the moment instead of the Savior who gives life forever. Like Philip, we often do the math and say it isn’t enough, when the Bread of Life is standing right before us. Jesus doesn’t just feed; He fills. He is more than enough to satisfy now and for eternity.

What Hunter Biden presented as a prayer sounded far more like a description.

James speaks of jealousy, selfish ambition, earthly wisdom, disorder, and even demonic influence. Whether anyone realized it or not, the passage became a mirror.

Because the Word of God has a way of exposing what people often cannot see in themselves.
And sometimes the people most convinced they are exposing others are the ones being exposed themselves.

Out of 31,000+ verses... this was the one.

chunks.text:
Watch Pastor Responds to Druski's Megachurch Skit | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher from  with . Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Pastor Responds to Druski's Megachurch Skit | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherFebruary 2, 2026•6:44SummaryIn this video, we react to and break down a viral satire clip by Druski that exposes the excesses, gimmicks, and manipulation often associated with the prosperity gospel and certain megachurch cultures. Through humor and exaggeration, the video highlights real concerns about pastors who exploit congregations emotionally and spiritually for financial gain.

We discuss themes like prosperity preaching, luxury branding in the pulpit, fundraising pressure tactics, and the misuse of spiritual language to justify wealth, power, and control. While the satire is comedic, the issues it points to are serious and deserve thoughtful biblical discernment.

This conversation is not about mocking God or the Church of Jesus Christ. Instead, it’s about calling out false shepherds, hirelings, and charlatans who fleece the sheep rather than feed them. Scripture calls pastors to humility, faithfulness, and care for souls—not performance, manipulation, or spectacle.

If you care about sound doctrine, biblical leadership, and protecting the church from spiritual abuse, this discussion is for you.

Pastor Reacts To An OG Lesbian | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherJanuary 26, 2026•3:24SummaryIn today’s culture, identity is often built on sexual orientation, gender identity, and personal expression—but what happens when those labels become the foundation of who we are? In this video, we react to a viral clip and respond with biblical truth, pointing to the hope found in Jesus Christ.

This message is not about hate, outrage, or trends—it’s about truth and the life-changing power of the gospel. No matter your background, your past, or your struggles, the Bible offers something culture never can: a new identity rooted in a Person, not a label.

The gospel invitation is clear: Christ calls all to come to the cross.
He doesn’t just affirm what we feel—He transforms who we are.

Truth over trend.
Grace over labels.
Hope for every person.

chunks.text:
Watch Perilous Times Are Here: Cold World, Bold Church | 2 Timothy 3:1-5 | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church from 2 Timothy with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Perilous Times Are Here: Cold World, Bold Church | 2 Timothy 3:1-5 | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church2 TimothyMatthew MaherMay 25, 2025•56:53SummaryPerilous Times Are Here is a prophetic warning and pastoral call to stand firm in an age of deception. Preaching from 2 Timothy 3:1–5, Pastor Matthew Maher exposes the cement-like nature of sin and falsehood in the last days—a world where anarchy rises, apostasy spreads, and apathy numbs the Church. As deception hardens hearts and counterfeit godliness takes root, the only hope is the jackhammer power of God's truth. From spiritual warfare to cultural collapse, this message calls believers to live bold, reflect Christ, and refuse to settle in times that demand we stand.

Ultimately, it urges us to anchor our lives in godly wisdom, practice daily gratitude, and choose the path that leads to enduring fruitfulness.

chunks.text:
Watch Proverbs 15 The Heart, The Path, The Harvest | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark Church from Proverbs with Terence Sikoryak. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Proverbs 15 The Heart, The Path, The Harvest | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark ChurchProverbsTerence SikoryakJune 14, 2026•47:06SummaryMost people don't suddenly arrive at wisdom, peace, or ruin. We move toward them one decision at a time. In this message from Proverbs 15, we explore how the heart shapes our words, our path determines our direction, and our harvest reveals the life we have cultivated. Through the lens of the Kingdom of God, Jesus calls us beyond behavior modification into a transformed heart that brings life, peace, and wisdom to a broken world. In the time remaining, we cannot afford to live accidentally—our future is not an event; it is a direction.

chunks.text: Sermon NotesProverbs 2:2-4Incline your ear to wisdom,apply your heart to understanding;if you cry out for discernment,And lift up your voice for understanding,If you seek her as silver,And search for her as for hidden treasures;Proverbs 9:1-6Wisdom has built her house,She has hewn out her seven pillars;She has slaughtered her meat,She has mixed her wine,She has also furnished her table.She has sent out her maidens,She cries out from the highest places of the city,“Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!”As for him who lacks understanding, she says to him,“Come, eat of my breadAnd drink of the wine I have mixed.Forsake foolishness and live,And go in the way of understanding.Leviticus 10:3And Moses said to Aaron, “This is what the Lord spoke, saying:‘By those who come near MeI must be regarded as holy;And before all the peopleI must be glorified.’Charles Spurgeon“His whole character commands our reverence because it is superlatively holy, and his name is to us a word of awe never to be mentioned flippantly, and never to be quoted without earnest thought and prostration of heart before him.”Psalm 22:3“But thou art holy, O thou that inhabits the praises of Israel”James 3:13-18Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show by good conduct that his works are done in the meekness of wisdom. But if you have bitter envy and self-seeking in your hearts, do not boast and lie against the truth. This wisdom does not descend from above, but is earthly, sensual, demonic. For where envy and self-seeking exist, confusion and every evil thing are there. But the wisdom that is from above is first of all pure, then peace-loving, gentle, willing to yield, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality and sincere. Now the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.1. Peace Loving:2. Gentle:3. Submissive: (Willing to Yield)4. Merciful:5. Fruitful:6. Impartial:7. Sincere:Proverbs 12:18Reckless words pierce like a sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.Proverbs 15:1“A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.”Proverbs 1:5“Let the wise listen and add to their learning, and let the discerning get guidance.”Philippians 2:3-4“Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves, not looking to your own interests but each of you to the interests of the others.”Matthew 9:13“But go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”John 15:4-5“Remain in me, as I also remain in you. No branch can bear fruit by itself; it must remain in the vine. Neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in me. I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit; apart from me you can do nothing.”1. Abiding in Christ2. Exhibiting the fruit of the Spirit3. Doing good works4. Living righteously5. Sharing the gospel6. Leaving an eternal impactProverbs 24:23“These also are sayings of the wise: To show partiality in judging is not good.”Proverbs 10:9“Whoever walks in integrity walks securely, but whoever takes crooked paths will be found out.”The Seven Pillars of Wisdom1. Peace Loving: Where do you find your peace…Do you bring Peace?2. Gentle: do you choose, kindness over harshness, and patience over impatience? Are you a gentle soul?3. Submissive: Willing to Yield4. Merciful: helping the poor, visiting the sick, or serving those in need…That’s mercy in action5. Fruitful: Diligence leads to fruitfulness6. Impartial: do we demonstrate justice, equality, and fairness7. chunks.text: Sermon NotesPsalm 1 is a mirror for man to see his condition and a map for man to see his destination.Psalm 1:1Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stands in the path of sinners, nor sits in the seat of the scornful…Be cautious when listening to anyone who doesn’t listen to God.Where evil is celebrated, good will be persecuted.Psalm 1:2But his delight is in the law of the Lord, and in His law he meditates day and night.What is in our mind determines what we become in time.Psalm 1:3He shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that brings forth its fruit in its season, whose leaf also shall not wither; and whatever he does shall prosper.Where the battle rages the most, there the loyalty of the soldier is proved the best.Psalm 1:4-54 The ungodly are not so, but are like the chaff which the wind drives away. 5 Therefore the ungodly shall not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous.There are only sheep and goats. Sheep know His voice and follow Him at all costs. Goats ignore His voice and rebel against Him which will cost them all.Psalm 1:6For the Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the ungodly shall perish.The godly will always be well and the ungodly will always be ill.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and GiveGive to support the mission of Landmark and help reach people with the gospel.Ways to GiveWays to GiveWays to GiveSermonsMore Sermons & ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextChanging The Unchangeable [Various Scripture] | Chris Einwechter | Landmark ChurchChanging The Unchangeable [Various Scripture] | Chris Einwechter | Landmark ChurchChanging The Unchangeable [Various Scripture] | Chris Einwechter | Landmark ChurchPurging The Church of Thieves [Jeremiah 7:1-15] | Matthew Maher | CCOCPurging The Church of Thieves [Jeremiah 7:1-15] | Matthew Maher | CCOCPurging The Church of Thieves [Jeremiah 7:1-15] | Matthew Maher | CCOCFaithfully Free Until The Finish: A Declaration of Dependence | 2 Timothy 4:6-8 | Matthew Maher2 TimothyMatthew MaherFaithfully Free Until The Finish: A Declaration of Dependence | 2 Timothy 4:6-8 | Matthew MaherFaithfully Free Until The Finish: A Declaration of Dependence | 2 Timothy 4:6-8 | Matthew MaherMaterial Versus Eternal | Sermon Moment | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchMaterial Versus Eternal | Sermon Moment | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchMaterial Versus Eternal | Sermon Moment | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchJeremiah - Proverbs 15 Part 2 | The Path and The Harvest | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark ChurchProverbsTerence SikoryakJuly 12, 2026•44:52SummaryLife doesn't change because we wish it would; it changes because we become different people. Proverbs 15 reminds us that every harvest begins long before the fruit appears—it begins in the condition of the heart, continues on the path of our daily choices, and eventually reveals itself in the life we build. Every conversation, every habit, every response to correction, and every decision is either moving us upward in wisdom or downward into regret. In the time remaining, don't chase more things; become a better person. When your character grows, your path changes, and when your path changes, your harvest inevitably follows.

chunks.text: Sermon NotesBe careful when listening to anyone who doesn’t listen to God.Psalm 11:1-2In the Lord I put my trust; how can you say to my soul, “Flee as a bird to your mountain”? For look! The wicked bend their bow, they make ready their arrow on the string, that they may shoot secretly at the upright in heart.We can flee in fear, or we can fight by faith, but we cannot do both.Psalm 11:3If the foundations are destroyed, what can the righteous do?The righteous ought to remember the Lord’s high and heavenly position over our low and earthly conditions.Psalm 11:4The Lord is in His holy temple, the Lord’s throne is in heaven; His eyes behold, His eyelids test the sons of men.Faith that is not tested cannot be trusted.Psalm 11:5The Lord tests the righteous, but the wicked and the one who loves violence His soul hates.Psalm 11:6Upon the wicked He will rain coals; fire and brimstone and a burning wind shall be the portion of their cup.The echo of Sodom and Gomorrah is not the result of an echo chamber; rather, it’s set forth as a divine reminder.Psalm 11:7For the Lord is righteous, He loves righteousness; chunks.title: Psalm 14: No God, No Good! | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Sermon NotesDietrich Bonhoeffer“Where God is forgotten, there the common good decays.”Psalm 14:1The fool has said in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt, they have done abominable works, there is none who does good.No God, no good. Know God, know good.Those that love darkness will hate the light.Psalm 14:2-3The Lord looks down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there are any who understand, who seek God. They have all turned aside, they have together become corrupt; there is none who does good, no, not one.To remove God from the equation is to multiply corruption.Psalm 14:4Have all the workers of iniquity no knowledge, who eat up my people as they eat bread, and do not call on the Lord?Knowledgelessness is a virus that kills its host.Psalm 14:5There they are in great fear, for God is with the generation of the righteous.Evil fears the gospel, which is why evil vilifies God’s people.Psalm 14:6You shame the counsel of the poor, but the Lord is his refuge.To be faithful to the Word is to be called hateful by the world.Psalm 14:7Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion! When the Lord brings back the captivity of His people, let Jacob rejoice and Israel be glad.Our hope is found in recognizing that the Lamb’s sacrifice paves the way for the Lion’s justice.View Sermon chunks.text: Sermon NotesLiving right in a wrong world will have you deemed wrong by those who think doing wrong is right.Psalm 15:1Lord, who may abide in Your tabernacle? Who may dwell in Your holy hill?We are justified by faith to stand in God’s presence, and then sanctified by truth to stay there.Psalm 15:2He who walks uprightly, and works righteousness, and speaks the truth in his heart…Our work for God should be the overflow of our walk with God; and our walk with God should be the outflow of our worship of God.Psalm 15:3He who does not backbite with his tongue, nor does evil to his neighbor, nor does he take up a reproach against his friend…He who gossips with you will gossip about you.Loving an enemy is about overcoming evil, not overlooking evil.Psalm 15:4In whose eyes a vile person is despised, but he honors those who fear the Lord; He who swears to his own hurt and does not change…Integrity is consistent and constant and does not compromise even at personal consequence.Psalm 15:5He who does not put out his money at usury, nor does he take a bribeagainst the innocent.Psalm 15:5He who does these things shall never be moved.A heart right with God remains immovable in a world full of wrong.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and GiveGive to support the mission of Landmark and help reach people with the gospel.Ways to GiveWays to GiveWays to GiveSermonsMore Sermons & ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextThe Coordinates Of Christmas (Why Bethlehem?) chunks.title: Psalm 10: When Man Forgets God | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Sermon NotesC.S. Lewis“There are only two kinds of people in the end: those who say to God, “Thy will be done,” and those to whom God says, in the end, “Thy will be done.” All that are in Hell, choose it. Without that self-choice there could be no Hell. No soul that seriously and constantly desires joy will ever miss it. Those who seek find. Those who knock it is opened.”Psalm 10:1-4Why do You stand afar off, O Lord? Why do You hide in times of trouble? The wicked in his pride persecutes the poor; let them be caught in the plots which they have devised. For the wicked boasts of his heart’s desire; he blesses the greedy and renounces the Lord. The wicked in his proud countenance does not seek God; God is in none of his thoughts.When man does not think about God, man in a way thinks he is God.Psalm 10:5-7His ways are always prospering; Your judgments are far above, out of his sight; as for all his enemies, he sneers at them. He has said in his heart, “I shall not be moved; I shall never be in adversity.” His mouth is full of cursing and deceit and oppression; under his tongue is trouble and iniquity.There are two sources behind the declaration, “I shall not be moved.” But only one—the one in Christ—will not be moved.Psalm 10:8-11He sits in the lurking places of the villages; in the secret places he murders the innocent; his eyes are secretly fixed on the helpless. He lies in wait secretly, as a lion in his den; he lies in wait to catch the poor; he catches the poor when he draws him into his net. So he crouches, he lies low, that the helpless may fall by his strength. He has said in his heart, “God has forgotten; He hides His face; He will never see.”One of the greatest lies about God is that He is ignorant, and He is impotent.Psalm 10:12-13Arise, O Lord! O God, lift up Your hand! Do not forget the humble. Why do the wicked renounce God? He has said in his heart, “You will not require an account.”Where we turn in times of crisis is an indication of who we think Christ is.Psalm 10:14-15But You have seen, for You observe trouble and grief, to repay it by Your hand. The helpless commits himself to You; You are the helper of the fatherless. Break the arm of the wicked and the evil man; seek out his wickedness until You find none.Death, darkness, and decay will have their day.Psalm 10:16-18The Lord is King forever and ever; the nations have perished out of His land. Lord, You have heard the desire of the humble; You will prepare their heart; You will cause Your ear to hear, to do justice to the fatherless and the oppressed, that the man of the earth may oppress no more.There is no time from the beginning of time where the Lord has not sat sovereign over time.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the chunks.title: Psalm 17: When Enemies Surround | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Sermon NotesPsalm 17:1-2Hear a just cause, O Lord, attend to my cry; give ear to my prayer which is not from deceitful lips. Let my vindication come from Your presence; let Your eyes look on the things that are upright.We cannot go wrong when we know the Lord is always right.Psalm 17:3-4You have tested my heart; You have visited me in the night; You have tried me and have found nothing; I have purposed that my mouth shall not transgress. Concerning the works of men, by the word of Your lips, I have kept away from the paths of the destroyer.We ought to be more concerned about being righteous than being right.Psalm 17:5Uphold my steps in Your paths, that my footsteps may not slip.Psalm 17:6-9I have called upon You, for You will hear me, O God; Incline Your ear to me, and hear my speech. Show Your marvelous lovingkindness by Your right hand, O You who save those who trust in You from those who rise up against them. Keep me as the apple of Your eye; hide me under the shadow of Your wings, From the wicked who oppress me, from my deadly enemies who surround me.Psalm 17:10-12They have closed up their fat hearts; with their mouths they speak proudly. They have now surrounded us in our steps; they have set their eyes, crouching down to the earth, As a lion is eager to tear his prey, and like a young lion lurking in secret places.God’s protection around us does not erase the reality of the opposition against us.Psalm 17:13-14Arise, O Lord, confront him, cast him down; deliver my life from the wicked with Your sword, With Your hand from men, O Lord, from men of the world who have their portion in this life, and whose belly You fill with Your hidden treasure. They are satisfied with children, and leave the rest of their possession for their babes.God fills us according to the appetite of our hearts.Psalm 17:15As for me, I will see Your face in righteousness; I shall be satisfied when I awake in Your likeness.The person who knows Christ is everything needs nothing.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and GiveGive to support the mission of Landmark and help reach people with the gospel.Ways to GiveWays to GiveWays to GiveSermonsMore Sermons & ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextPsalm 32: Hiding From God or Hidden In God? chunks.title: Psalm 19: The Perfect Word For An Imperfect World | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Sermon NotesPsalm 19:1-4aThe heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament shows His handiwork. Day unto day utters speech, and night unto night reveals knowledge. There is no speech nor language where their voice is not heard. Their line has gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world.The heavens are God’s handiwork, but humans are the work of God’s hands.To deny God’s creative genius is to become genuinely foolish.Psalm 19:4b-6In them He has set a tabernacle for the sun, Which is like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, and rejoices like a strong man to run its race. Its rising is from one end of heaven, and its circuit to the other end; and there is nothing hidden from its heat.The Son doesn’t cease to exist just because man doesn’t see Him.Psalm 19:7-8The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul; The testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple; The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart; the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes…Psalm 19:9The fear of the Lord is clean, enduring forever; the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether.Psalm 19:10More to be desired are they than gold, yea, than much fine gold; sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb.Gold and God’s Word:Man will go to the ends of the earth to mine for one, yet often pays no mind to the other.Psalm 19:11Moreover by them Your servant is warned, and in keeping them there is great reward.Psalm 19:12-13Who can understand his errors? Cleanse me from secret faults. Keep back Your servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me. Then I shall be blameless, and I shall be innocent of great transgression.God puts us in a fix for the faults He sees to fix the faults we can’t see.Blameless doesn’t mean you won’t make mistakes; it means your mistakes won’t make you.Psalm 19:14Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in Your sight, O Lord, my strength and my Redeemer.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and GiveGive to support the mission of Landmark and help reach people with the gospel.Ways to GiveWays to GiveWays to GiveSermonsMore Sermons & ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextI John 2 Review to Renew : Matthew MaherI John 2 Review to Renew : Matthew MaherI John 2 Review to Renew : Matthew MaherSigns of the Times | Lawlessness & The Lens of Delusion: Is ICE The Gestapo? | Romans 13 | M. chunks.title: Psalm 18: The Lord Is My Rock | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Sermon NotesPsalm 18:1-3I will love You, O Lord, my strength. 2 The Lord is my rock and my fortress and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust; my shield and the horn of my salvation, my stronghold. 3 I will call upon the Lord, who is worthy to be praised; so shall I be saved from my enemies.I am secure where I am as who I am because of the truth of where He is and who He is.Psalm 18:4-6The pangs of death surrounded me, and the floods of ungodliness made me afraid. 5 The sorrows of Sheol surrounded me; the snares of death confronted me. 6 In my distress I called upon the Lord, and cried out to my God; He heard my voice from His temple, and my cry came before Him, even to His ears.The fear of death and the floods of ungodliness may overwhelm, but God’s faithfulness is over them.Psalm 18:7-15Then the earth shook and trembled; the foundations of the hills also quaked and were shaken, because He was angry. 8 Smoke went up from His nostrils, and devouring fire from His mouth; coals were kindled by it. 9 He bowed the heavens also, and came down with darkness under His feet. 10 And He rode upon a cherub, and flew; He flew upon the wings of the wind. 11 He made darkness His secret place; His canopy around Him was dark waters and thick clouds of the skies. 12 From the brightness before Him, His thick clouds passed with hailstones and coals of fire. 13 The Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High uttered His voice, hailstones and coals of fire. 14 He sent out His arrows and scattered the foe, lightnings in abundance, and He vanquished them. 15 Then the channels of the sea were seen, the foundations of the world were uncovered at Your rebuke, O Lord, at the blast of the breath of Your nostrils.Psalm 18:16-19He sent from above, He took me; He drew me out of many waters. 17 He delivered me from my strong enemy, from those who hated me, for they were too strong for me. 18 They confronted me in the day of my calamity, but the Lord was my support. 19 He also brought me out into a broad place; He delivered me because He delighted in me.The God who rescues also restores.Psalm 18:20-24The Lord rewarded me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands He has recompensed me. 21 For I have kept the ways of the Lord, and have not wickedly departed from my God. 22 For all His judgments were before me, And I did not put away His statutes from me. 23 I was also blameless before Him, and I kept myself from my iniquity. 24 Therefore the Lord has recompensed me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands in His sight.God make us righteous and then righteousness makes us godly.Psalm 18:25-27With the merciful You will show Yourself merciful; with a blameless man You will show Yourself blameless; 26 with the pure You will show Yourself pure; and with the devious You will show Yourself shrewd. 27 For You will save the humble people, but will bring down haughty looks.Those who are humble will be exalted; and those who exalt themselves will be humiliated.Psalm 18:28-30For You will light my lamp; The Lord my God will enlighten my darkness. 29 For by You I can run against a troop, by my God I can leap over a wall. 30 As for God, His way is perfect; the word of the Lord is proven; He is a shield to all who trust in Him.Psalm 18:31-36For who is God, except the Lord? And who is a rock, except our God? 32 It is God who arms me with strength, and makes my way perfect. 33 He makes my feet like the feet of deer, and sets me on my high places. 34 He teaches my hands to make war, so that my arms can bend a bow of bronze. 35 You have also given me the shield of Your salvation; Your right hand has held me up, Your gentleness has made me great. 36 You enlarged my path under me, so my feet did not slip.Man’s greatness is made by God’s gentleness.Psalm 18:37-42I have pursued my enemies and overtaken them; Neither did I turn back again till they were destroyed. 38 I have wounded them, so that they could not rise; they have fallen under my feet. 39 For You have armed me with strength for the battle; You have subdued under me those who rose up against me. 40 You have also given me the necks of my enemies, so that I destroyed those who hated me. 41 They cried out, but there was none to save; even to the Lord, but He did not answer them. 42 Then I beat them as fine as the dust before the wind; I cast them out like dirt in the streets.The battle may be long to us, but the battle belongs to the Lord.Psalm 18:43-49You have delivered me from the strivings of the people; You have made me the head of the nations; A people I have not known shall serve me. 44 As soon as they hear of me they obey me; the foreigners submit to me. 45 The foreigners fade away, and come frightened from their hideouts. 46 The Lord lives! Blessed be my Rock! Let the God of my salvation be exalted. 47 It is God who avenges me, and subdues the peoples under me; 48 He delivers me from my enemies. You also lift me up above those who rise against me; You have delivered me from the violent man. 49 Therefore I will give thanks to You, O Lord, among the Gentiles, and sing praises to Your name.Psalm 18:50Great deliverance He gives to His king, and shows mercy to His anointed, to David and his descendants forevermore.(Psalm 18:1-6) His Death– “The pangs of death encompassed me…”(Psalm 18:7-18) His Resurrection– “He sent from above, He took me; He drew me out of many waters. He delivered me from my strong enemy.”(Psalm 18:19-27) His Ascension– “Therefore the LORD has recompensed me according to my righteousness.”(Psalm 18:28-42) His Church– “For You have armed me with strength for the battle; You have subdued under me those who rose up against me.”(Psalm 18:43-50) His Kingdom– “You have made me the head of the nations…”View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon chunks.text: Sermon NotesPsalm 20:1-3May the Lord answer you in the day of trouble; may the name of the God of Jacob defend you; May He send you help from the sanctuary, and strengthen you out of Zion; May He remember all your offerings, and accept your burnt sacrifice. SelahTrouble may touch you, but trusting the Lord through it will transform you.Psalm 20:4-6May He grant you according to your heart’s desire, and fulfill all your purpose. We will rejoice in your salvation, and in the name of our God we will set up our banners! May the Lord fulfill all your petitions. Now I know that the Lord saves His anointed; He will answer him from His holy heaven with the saving strength of His right hand.He will do what we ask because what we ask is from the desire to do what He wills.He will do what He wills.Psalm 20:7-8Some trust in chariots, and some in horses; but we will remember the name of the Lord our God. They have bowed down and fallen; but we have risen and stand upright.Human resources come to a hopeless end. Heaven’s resources come with endless hope.Psalm 20:9Save, Lord! May the King answer us when we call.The Lord not only answers when we call, but the Lord is the Answer when we call.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and GiveGive to support the mission of Landmark and help reach people with the gospel.Ways to GiveWays to GiveWays to GiveSermonsMore Sermons & ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextBreaking News: The Gospel Is Unchained! chunks.title: Psalm 2: Why Do The Nations Rage? (Psalm 2:1-12) | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Sermon NotesPsalm 2:1-3Why do the nations rage, and the people plot a vain thing? 2 The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the Lord and against His Anointed, saying, 3 “Let us break Their bonds in pieces and cast away Their cords from us.”Man’s rule apart from God’s rules will always be unruly.OBYGN STUDENT VIDEOThe bonds of the Bible are intolerable to the heart of the rebel.Psalm 2:4-6He who sits in the heavens shall laugh; the Lord shall hold them in derision. 5 Then He shall speak to them in His wrath, and distress them in His deep displeasure: 6 “Yet I have set My King on My holy hill of Zion.”The insurrection of hell cannot overthrow the installation of heaven.UNRWA Students VIDEOPsalm 2:7-9“I will declare the decree: The Lord has said to Me, ‘You are My Son, today I have begotten You. 8 Ask of Me, and I will give You the nations for Your inheritance, and the ends of the earth for Your possession. 9 You shall break them with a rod of iron; You shall dash them to pieces like a potter’s vessel.’ ”Jesus rules the universe by decree not democracy.We can be broken before Christ or we will be broken by Christ.Psalm 2:10-12Now therefore, be wise, O kings; be instructed, you judges of the earth. 11 Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice with trembling. 12 Kiss the Son, lest He be angry, and you perish in the way, when His wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed are all those who put their trust in Him.There is no refuge from Christ; there is only refuge in Christ.Additional Scriptures Referenced: Acts 17:24-31; Luke 23:12; Acts 4:25; Psalm 49:20; Proverbs 1:25-27; chunks.title: Psalm 16: Trusting God In The Dark | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Sermon NotesWhen with God, the lessons we learn are deeper in the dark than in the pretentious light.Psalm 16:1Preserve me, O God, for in You I put my trust.God preserves us so that we may be agents of preservation for Him.Psalm 16:2-3O my soul, you have said to the Lord, “You are my Lord, my goodness is nothing apart from You.” As for the saints who are on the earth, “They are the excellent ones, in whom is all my delight.”Our worth is in His worthiness.Psalm 16:4Their sorrows shall be multiplied who hasten after another god; their drink offerings of blood I will not offer, nor take up their names on my lips.The soul knows no sorrow that the Savior can’t heal.Psalm 16:5-6O Lord, You are the portion of my inheritance and my cup; You maintain my lot. The lines have fallen to me in pleasant places; yes, I have a good inheritance.Psalm 16:7-8I will bless the Lord who has given me counsel; my heart also instructs me in the night seasons. I have set the Lord always before me; because He is at my right hand I shall not be moved.We can follow our heart in the night seasons only when our heart is rooted in the Word, both in and out of season.Psalm 16:9-10Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoices; my flesh also will rest in hope. For You will not leave my soul in Sheol, nor will You allow Your Holy One to see corruption.Psalm 16:11You will show me the path of life; in Your presence is fullness of joy; at Your right hand are pleasures forevermore.Life in Christ is not without pain and problems. chunks.title: Psalm 21: "Make Me!": Prayer or Protest? | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Sermon NotesPsalm 21:1-2The king shall have joy in Your strength, O Lord; and in Your salvation how greatly shall he rejoice! You have given him his heart’s desire, and have not withheld the request of his lips. SelahPeople do not see prayers answered because they do not believe prayer is the answer.Psalm 21:3-4For You meet him with the blessings of goodness; You set a crown of pure gold upon his head. He asked life from You, and You gave it to him—Length of days forever and ever.So whether we get what we want or we don’t want what we get, let us rest in knowing God’s got it.Psalm 21:5-7His glory is great in Your salvation; honor and majesty You have placed upon him. For You have made him most blessed forever; You have made him exceedingly glad with Your presence. For the king trusts in the Lord, and through the mercy of the Most High he shall not be moved.The Lord will not make much of Himself through people who think too much of themselves.Psalm 21:8-10Your hand will find all Your enemies; Your right hand will find those who hate You. You shall make them as a fiery oven in the time of Your anger; the Lord shall swallow them up in His wrath, and the fire shall devour them. Their offspring You shall destroy from the earth, and their descendants from among the sons of men.Those who hate God’s grace will get His wrath.Psalm 21:11-12For they intended evil against You; they devised a plot which they are not able to perform. Therefore You will make them turn their back; You will make ready Your arrows on Your string toward their faces.In the end, there are those who say “make me” as a prayer and those who say “make me” as a protest. God will empower one and devour the other.Psalm 21:13Be exalted, O Lord, in Your own strength! We will sing and praise Your power.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and For the faithful disappear from among the sons of men.True Christianity will never perish because Christ cannot perish.Psalm 12:2They speak idly everyone with his neighbor; with flattering lips and a double heart they speak.If you live by people’s praise, you will die by their criticism.Psalm 12:3-4May the Lord cut off all flattering lips, and the tongue that speaks proud things, who have said, “With our tongue we will prevail; our lips are our own; who is lord over us?”There is a time to hold your tongue and there is a time when your tongue holds you.Psalm 12:5“For the oppression of the poor, for the sighing of the needy, now I will arise,” says the Lord; “I will set him in the safety for which he yearns.”When the Lord arises, every king and kingdom will bow down, and every lie and liar will be torn down.Psalm 12:6The words of the Lord are pure words, like silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times.Psalm 12:7You shall keep them, O Lord, You shall preserve them from this generation forever.The Lord keeps His Word. Thus, the Lord keeps those who keep His Word.Psalm 12:8The wicked prowl on every side, when vileness is exalted among the sons of men.When filth is the norm, faith needs to be firm.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and GiveGive to support the mission of Landmark and help reach people with the gospel.Ways to GiveWays to GiveWays to GiveSermonsMore Sermons & ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextPsalm 42: Preaching To A Downcast Soul | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchPsalmsMatthew MaherPsalm 42: Preaching To A Downcast Soul | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchPsalm 42: Preaching To A Downcast Soul | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchThe Sound of Gratitude: Turning Testimony into Impact | Jonathan Gonzalez | Landmark ChurchThe Sound of Gratitude: Turning Testimony into Impact | Jonathan Gonzalez | Landmark ChurchThe Sound of Gratitude: Turning Testimony into Impact | Jonathan Gonzalez | Landmark ChurchThe Dismantling of the Family Foundation | Matthew Maher | Coastal Christian Ocean CityThe Dismantling of the Family Foundation | Matthew Maher | Coastal Christian Ocean CityThe Dismantling of the Family Foundation | Matthew Maher | Coastal Christian Ocean CityThe Thorns: The Place Of Suffering | Good Friday 2025 | Landmark ChurchThe Thorns: The Place Of Suffering | Good Friday 2025 | Landmark ChurchThe Thorns: The Place Of Suffering | Good Friday 2025 | Landmark ChurchA Native Knows The Language | Matthew MaherA Native Knows The Language | Matthew MaherA Native Knows The Language | Matthew MaherPAY ATTENTION CHRISTIAN | Sermon JamPAY ATTENTION CHRISTIAN | Sermon JamPAY ATTENTION CHRISTIAN | Sermon JamOur TeamMeet the People Behind the MessageDiscover the pastors and leaders who faithfully share God’s Word and serve our church.Meet the TeamMeet the TeamMeet the Team

chunks.text: Sermon NotesPsalm 22:21bYou have answered Me.No matter how roughly life has handled you, never forget Whose hands ultimately hold you.Psalm 22:22-23I will declare Your name to My brethren; in the midst of the assembly I will praise You. You who fear the Lord, praise Him! All you descendants of Jacob, glorify Him, and fear Him, all you offspring of Israel!Testimony is the language of the redeemed.Psalm 22:24-25For He has not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted; nor has He hidden His face from Him; But when He cried to Him, He heard. My praise shall be of You in the great assembly; I will pay My vows before those who fear Him.It’s often through affliction that He teaches us so much about His affection.Psalm 22:26-27The poor shall eat and be satisfied; those who seek Him will praise the Lord. Let your heart live forever! All the ends of the world shall remember and turn to the Lord, and all the families of the nations shall worship before You.Psalm 22:28For the kingdom is the Lord’s, and He rules over the nations.Psalm 22:29-31All the prosperous of the earth shall eat and worship; all those who go down to the dust shall bow before Him, even he who cannot keep himself alive.A posterity shall serve Him. It will be recounted of the Lord to the next generation, they will come and declare His righteousness to a people who will be born, that He has done this.Because “it is finished” in Jesus, it has chunks.title: Psalm 25: The Grit To Wait, The Grace To Walk | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Sermon NotesIt takes grit to wait on the Lord—and grace to walk in His ways.Psalm 25:1-3To You, O Lord, I lift up my soul. O my God, I trust in You; let me not be ashamed; let not my enemies triumph over me. Indeed, let no one who waits on You be ashamed; let those be ashamed who deal treacherously without cause.Shame may be brought, but we will not be brought to shame.Psalm 25:4-7Show me Your ways, O Lord; teach me Your paths. Lead me in Your truth and teach me, for You are the God of my salvation; on You I wait all the day. Remember, O Lord, Your tender mercies and Your lovingkindnesses, for they are from of old. Do not remember the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions; according to Your mercy remember me, for Your goodness’ sake, O Lord.When God remembers His mercies, He forgets our mistakes.Psalm 25:8-11Good and upright is the Lord; therefore He teaches sinners in the way. The humble He guides in justice, and the humble He teaches His way. All the paths of the Lord are mercy and truth, to such as keep His covenant and His testimonies. For Your name’s sake, O Lord, pardon my iniquity, for it is great.The world says, “This path is horrible.” But the Word says, “This path is holy.”Psalm 25:12-15Who is the man that fears the Lord? Him shall He teach in the way He chooses. He himself shall dwell in prosperity, and his descendants shall inherit the earth. The secret of the Lord is with those who fear Him, and He will show them His covenant. My eyes are ever toward the Lord, for He shall pluck my feet out of the net.Those who stand under covenant are those who understand what it means to be confident.Psalm 25:16-21Turn Yourself to me, and have mercy on me, for I am desolate and afflicted. The troubles of my heart have enlarged; bring me out of my distresses! Look on my affliction and my pain, and forgive all my sins. Consider my enemies, for they are many; and they hate me with cruel hatred. Keep my soul, and deliver me; let me not be ashamed, for I put my trust in You. Let integrity and uprightness preserve me, for I wait for You.The troubles of life may be consistent, but God’s faithfulness is our constant.Psalm 25:22Redeem Israel, O God, out of all their troubles!Redemption is never just for me—it’s always meant to ripple out to we.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and GiveGive to support the mission of Landmark and help reach people with the gospel.Ways to GiveWays to GiveWays to GiveSermonsMore Sermons & ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextMens Gathering | September 2025Mens Gathering | September 2025Mens Gathering | September 2025Making Unity a Reality 2 | Matthew MaherMaking Unity a Reality 2 | Matthew MaherMaking Unity a Reality 2 | Matthew MaherThree Days In Holy Week [Palm Sunday] | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark ChurchThree Days In Holy Week [Palm Sunday] | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark ChurchThree Days In Holy Week [Palm Sunday] | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark ChurchIn the Lord Part | Matthew MaherIn the Lord Part | Matthew MaherIn the Lord Part | Matthew MaherBuilt to Stand Together: Striving Side by Side for the Gospel | Philippians 1:27-30| Nick JohnsonBuilt to Stand Together: Striving Side by Side for the Gospel | Philippians 1:27-30| Nick JohnsonBuilt to Stand Together: Striving Side by Side for the Gospel | Philippians 1:27-30| Nick JohnsonThe Tension Between Two Truths 2 | Matthew MaherThe Tension Between Two Truths 2 | Matthew MaherThe Tension Between Two Truths 2 | Matthew MaherOur TeamMeet the People Behind the MessageDiscover the pastors and leaders who faithfully share God’s Word and serve our church.Meet the TeamMeet the TeamMeet the Team

chunks.title: Psalm 22: The Clues & Cues From The Cross | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Sermon NotesPsalm 22:1-2My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me? Why are You so far from helping Me, and from the words of My groaning? O My God, I cry in the daytime, but You do not hear; and in the night season, and am not silent.When God feels distant, remember His faithfulness is never absent.Psalm 22:3-5But You are holy, enthroned in the praises of Israel. Our fathers trusted in You; They trusted, and You delivered them. They cried to You, and were delivered; They trusted in You, and were not ashamed.Psalm 22:6-8But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised by the people. All those who see Me ridicule Me; they shoot out the lip, they shake the head, saying, “He trusted in the Lord, let Him rescue Him; let Him deliver Him, since He delights in Him!”We may be mocked by men, but let every Christian remember that they are marked by God.Jesus experienced separation so we could experience reconciliation.Psalm 22:9-11But You are He who took Me out of the womb; You made Me trust while on My mother’s breasts. I was cast upon You from birth. From My mother’s womb You have been My God. Be not far from Me, for trouble is near; for there is none to help.The One who knit you together inside the womb will not abandon you outside the womb.Psalm 22:12-15Many bulls have surrounded Me; strong bulls of Bashan have encircled Me. They gape at Me with their mouths, like a raging and roaring lion. I am poured out like water, and all My bones are out of joint; my heart is like wax; it has melted within Me. My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and My tongue clings to My jaws; You have brought Me to the dust of death.If the earthly rulers had known who He was, they wouldn’t have crucified Him—but if He hadn’t been crucified, we wouldn’t know who He is.If the demonic rulers had known what it was, they wouldn’t have crucified Him—but if He hadn’t been crucified, we wouldn’t know what it is.Psalm 22:16-18For dogs have surrounded Me; the congregation of the wicked has enclosed Me. They pierced My hands and My feet; I can count all My bones. They look and stare at Me. They divide My garments among them, and for My clothing they cast lots.Psalm 22:19-21But You, O Lord, do not be far from Me; O My Strength, hasten to help Me! Deliver Me from the sword, my precious life from the power of the dog. Save Me from the lion’s mouth and from the horns of the wild oxen! You have answered Me.The best way to manage our sorrow is to know the Man of Sorrows.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and GiveGive to support the mission of Landmark and help reach people with the gospel.Ways to GiveWays to GiveWays to GiveSermonsMore Sermons & ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextFirst John 1 Review to Renew | Matthew MaherFirst John 1 Review to Renew | Matthew MaherFirst John 1 Review to Renew | Matthew MaherIsrael's Itinerary (Part 3): *Here Comes The Church [Daniel 9:26-27] | Matthew Maher | CCOCIsrael's Itinerary (Part 3): *Here Comes The Church [Daniel 9:26-27] | Matthew Maher | CCOCIsrael's Itinerary (Part 3): *Here Comes The Church [Daniel 9:26-27] | Matthew Maher | CCOCPsalm 47: King By Right, Not By Vote | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchPsalm 47: King By Right, Not By Vote | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchPsalm 47: King By Right, Not By Vote | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchThe Age of Wisdom: 70 Years Is Not A Long Time | Proverbs 16:31 | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark ChurchProverbsTerence SikoryakThe Age of Wisdom: 70 Years Is Not A Long Time | Proverbs 16:31 | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark ChurchThe Age of Wisdom: 70 Years Is Not A Long Time | Proverbs 16:31 | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark ChurchHolding Court (Part 2) (Esther 6-7) | Matthew Maher | Coastal Christian Ocean CityHolding Court (Part 2) (Esther 6-7) | Matthew Maher | Coastal Christian Ocean CityHolding Court (Part 2) (Esther 6-7) | Matthew Maher | Coastal Christian Ocean CityThe Spirit of Lunacy (Matthew 17) | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark ChurchThe Spirit of Lunacy (Matthew 17) | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark ChurchThe Spirit of Lunacy (Matthew 17) | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark ChurchOur TeamMeet the People Behind the MessageDiscover the pastors and leaders who faithfully share God’s Word and serve our church.Meet the TeamMeet the TeamMeet the Team

chunks.text: Sermon NotesPsalm 23 isn’t just poetic — it’s potent. These words are not just for memory but for intimacy.Psalm 23:1The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.To be near the Shepherd is to not only hear His voice, but to adhere to His voice.Psalm 23:1The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.Trusting in the Lord doesn’t mean everything will happen the way you want, but that you will not be “in want” no matter what happens.Psalm 23:2He makes me to lie down in green pastures…The grass isn’t greener on the other side. The grass is greener where the Lord resides.Psalm 23:2He leads me beside the still waters.Psalm 23:3He restores my soul; He leads me in the paths of righteousness for His name’s sake.Psalm 23:3He restores my soul; He leads me in the paths of righteousness for His name’s sake.Righteous paths may be hard to travel, but they’re always easy to trust.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon Psalm 26: Integrity Stands & Perversity Slips | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchPsalmsMatthew MaherJune 5, 2025•38:42SummaryIntegrity Stands & Perversity Slips is a timely call to walk uprightly in a world bent on corruption. Preaching from Psalm 26, Pastor Matthew Maher unpacks David’s bold appeal for God to examine his heart and vindicate his walk. This message draws a clear contrast between the faithful who walk in truth and the wicked who walk in schemes. While others scheme, bribe, and deceive—the one who walks in integrity stands on solid ground. In a culture full of compromise, this sermon urges believers to pursue spiritual stability, moral clarity, and wholehearted devotion to the God who sees the heart and rewards the righteous.

will bless the Lord.Spiritual stability doesn’t come from willpower, but from standing in God’s will and power.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / For He has founded it upon the seas, and established it upon the waters.If God made it, He owns it. If He owns it, He rules it. If He rules it, then it must follow His rules.Psalm 24:3Who may ascend into the hill of the Lord? Or who may stand in His holy place?You don’t climb to become king of the hill—you get clean to approach the King on the Hill.Psalm 24:4He who has clean hands and a pure heart, Who has not lifted up his soul to an idol, nor sworn deceitfully.Jesus is the only way God paved, the only truth God gave, and the only life God saved.Psalm 24:5-6He shall receive blessing from the Lord, and righteousness from the God of his salvation. This is Jacob, the generation of those who seek Him, Who seek Your face. SelahThe Gospel is seeker sensitive, not that it changes to reach people but that it reaches people it changes.Psalm 24:7-8Lift up your heads, O you gates! And be lifted up, you everlasting doors! And the King of glory shall come in. Who is this King of glory? The Lord strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle.Psalm 24:9-10Lift up your heads, O you gates! Lift up, you everlasting doors! And the King of glory shall come in. Who is this King of glory? The Lord of hosts, He is the King of glory. chunks.text: Sermon NotesIn Psalm 29, creation doesn’t just react to the weather—it responds to its Creator.Psalm 29:1-2Give unto the Lord, O you mighty ones, Give unto the Lord glory and strength. Give unto the Lord the glory due to His name; Worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness.The Lord doesn’t need our worship; we need to worship the Lord.Psalm 29:3-5The voice of the Lord is over the waters; The God of glory thunders; The Lord is over many waters. The voice of the Lord is powerful; The voice of the Lord is full of majesty. The voice of the Lord breaks the cedars, Yes, the Lord splinters the cedars of Lebanon.God’s voice is not just still and small—it’s also the power that stills it all.Psalm 29:6-9He makes them also skip like a calf, Lebanon and Sirion like a young wild ox. The voice of the Lord divides the flames of fire. The voice of the Lord shakes the wilderness; The Lord shakes the Wilderness of Kadesh. The voice of the Lord makes the deer give birth, And strips the forests bare; And in His temple everyone says, “Glory!”Psalm 29:10The Lord sat enthroned at the Flood, and the Lord sits as King forever.Psalm 29:11The Lord will give strength to His people; The Lord will bless His people with peace.The voice of the Lord both commands the storm and calms the soul.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and GiveGive to support the mission of Landmark and help reach people with the gospel.Ways to GiveWays to GiveWays to GiveSermonsMore Sermons & ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextUPDATE: Israel Declares War | The Pain, Problem, Prophecy, and Peace of What’s Happening | M. Psalm 28: You Cannot Slip Through The Rock | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchPsalmsMatthew MaherAugust 14, 2025•32:04SummaryIn a world quick to settle for comfort over character, Psalm 28 calls us back to desperate dependence on God. In this heartfelt message, Pastor Matthew Maher unpacks David’s cry to the Lord his Rock, showing how honesty before God is better than outward peace that hides inward corruption.
From desperation to trust, from personal prayer to public praise, this psalm traces the bridge that takes us from crying out to singing out. Learn how to cling to the Rock who will not slip, how trust becomes the turning point from fear to faith, and why spiritual leaders must be intercessors before they are influencers.

chunks.text: Sermon NotesPsalm 28:1-2To You I will cry, O Lord my Rock: Do not be silent to me, lest, if You are silent to me, I become like those who go down to the pit. Hear the voice of my supplications when I cry to You, when I lift up my hands toward Your holy sanctuary.When we lose our desperation, we lose our dependence.You cannot slip through a Rock.Psalm 28:3-5Do not take me away with the wicked and with the workers of iniquity, who speak peace to their neighbors, but evil is in their hearts. Give them according to their deeds, and according to the wickedness of their endeavors; give them according to the work of their hands; render to them what they deserve. Because they do not regard the works of the Lord, nor the operation of His hands, He shall destroy them and not build them up.It is better to be desperate and honest than comfortable and corrupt.Psalm 28:6-7Blessed be the Lord, because He has heard the voice of my supplications! The Lord is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in Him, and I am helped; therefore my heart greatly rejoices, and with my song I will praise Him.Trust is the bridge that takes us from desperation to declaration.Psalm 28:8The Lord is their strength, and He is the saving refuge of His anointed.Personal testimony strengthens public faith.Psalm 28:9Save Your people, and bless Your inheritance; Shepherd them also, and bear them up forever.Spiritual leaders must be intercessors before they are influencers.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and GiveGive to support the mission of Landmark and help reach people with the gospel.Ways to GiveWays to GiveWays to GiveSermonsMore Sermons & ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextLifting Up Government: Prime Prayers For Prime Ministers (1 Timothy 2:1-4) | Matthew Maher1 TimothyMatthew MaherLifting Up Government: Prime Prayers For Prime Ministers (1 Timothy 2:1-4) | Matthew MaherLifting Up Government: Prime Prayers For Prime Ministers (1 Timothy 2:1-4) | Matthew MaherShe Called Her Cancer a GIFT. chunks.text: Sermon NotesPsalm 30:1-3I will extol You, O Lord, for You have lifted me up, and have not let my foes rejoice over me. O Lord my God, I cried out to You, and You healed me. O Lord, You brought my soul up from the grave; You have kept me alive, that I should not go down to the pit.God is not who we think He is. God is who He says He is.Psalm 30:4-5Sing praise to the Lord, you saints of His, and give thanks at the remembrance of His holy name. For His anger is but for a moment, His favor is for life; Weeping may endure for a night, but joy comes in the morning.Seasons of midnight sorrow always yield to morning mercy.Psalm 30:6-7Now in my prosperity I said, “I shall never be moved.” Lord, by Your favor You have made my mountain stand strong; You hid Your face, and I was troubled.When we elevate self, we eclipse the Son.Psalm 30:8-10I cried out to You, O Lord; And to the Lord I made supplication: “What profit is there in my blood, When I go down to the pit? Will the dust praise You? Will it declare Your truth? Hear, O Lord, and have mercy on me; Lord, be my helper!”Desperation strips away pretense, and the most honest prayers rise in the most intense times.Psalm 30:11-12You have turned for me my mourning into dancing; You have put off my sackcloth and clothed me with gladness, to the end that my glory may sing praise to You and not be silent. O Lord my God, I will give thanks to You forever.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the chunks.text: Sermon NotesA Psalm of David when he fled from Absalom his son.Part of the fall is that things fall apart.Part of redemption is that what falls apart still plays a part in the beautification of being set apart.Psalm 3:1-2Lord, how they have increased who trouble me! Many are they who rise up against me. 2 Many are they who say of me, “There is no help for him in God.” SelahMany are they and many are they who say whatever they want to say, but only God has the final say.The music may be interrupted by a pause, but the pause is still an intricate part of the music.Psalm 3:3-4But You, O Lord, are a shield for me, my glory and the One who lifts up my head. 4 I cried to the Lord with my voice, and He heard me from His holy hill. SelahWhen the enemy comes in like a flood, it is the shield of faith that serves as a fortress.Psalm 3:5-6I lay down and slept; I awoke, for the Lord sustained me. 6 I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people who have set themselves against me all around.God’s peace is a pillow. With it, we rest. Without it, we rust.When you know God stands with you, it doesn’t matter who stands against you.Psalm 3:7-8Arise, O Lord; Save me, O my God! For You have struck all my enemies on the cheekbone; You have broken the teeth of the ungodly. 8 Salvation belongs to the Lord. Your blessing is upon Your people. SelahDavid turned an assault into a Psalm. He turned a wrong into a song. In this powerful message, Pastor Matthew unpacks David’s raw yet resolute prayer, showing how courage and brokenness can exist in the same heart when God is our light, salvation, and strength.
From fear to faith, from enemies to intimacy, from waiting to worship—this psalm walks us through every season of the soul. Learn how to anchor your confidence in God's presence, not your circumstances, and discover the rule of faith: that the Lord rules over all.

chunks.title: Psalm 27: The Rule of Faith: God Rules | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Sermon NotesFaith isn’t blind—it’s bold. It doesn’t avoid trouble; it aligns with truth.Psalm 27:1-3The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The Lord is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid? When the wicked came against me to eat up my flesh, my enemies and foes, they stumbled and fell. Though an army may encamp against me, my heart shall not fear; though war may rise against me, in this I will be confident.The rule of fear is that fear wants to rule. But fear cannot rule when you follow the rule of faith.Psalm 27:4-5One thing I have desired of the Lord, that will I seek: that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the Lord, and to inquire in His temple. For in the time of trouble He shall hide me in His pavilion; In the secret place of His tabernacle He shall hide me; He shall set me high upon a rock.Our greatest pursuit shouldn’t be for rescue; it should be for relationship.Psalm 27:6And now my head shall be lifted up above my enemies all around me; therefore I will offer sacrifices of joy in His tabernacle; I will sing, yes, I will sing praises to the Lord.Worship is a weapon and a witness.Psalm 27:7-10Hear, O Lord, when I cry with my voice! Have mercy also upon me, and answer me. When You said, “Seek My face,” my heart said to You, “Your face, Lord, I will seek.” Do not hide Your face from me; do not turn Your servant away in anger; You have been my help; do not leave me nor forsake me, O God of my salvation. When my father and my mother forsake me, then the Lord will take care of me.Even when the closest of relationships pull away, God is always there to pull us through.Psalm 27:11-12Teach me Your way, O Lord, and lead me in a smooth path, because of my enemies. Do not deliver me to the will of my adversaries; for false witnesses have risen against me, and such as breathe out violence.The Lord’s path isn’t always easy, but it is always steady.Psalm 27:13-14I would have lost heart, unless I had believed that I would see the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living. Wait on the Lord; be of good courage, and He shall strengthen your heart; wait, I say, on the Lord!Waiting on the Lord isn’t about God being tardy—it’s about Him being timely.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerMatthew MaherPastor / ElderAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and GiveGive to support the mission of Landmark and help reach people with the gospel.Ways to GiveWays to GiveWays to GiveSermonsMore Sermons & ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextWorthy of Praise, Always and In All Ways [Jude 24-25] | Matthew Maher | Coastal Christian Ocean CityWorthy of Praise, Always and In All Ways [Jude 24-25] | Matthew Maher | Coastal Christian Ocean CityWorthy of Praise, Always and In All Ways [Jude 24-25] | Matthew Maher | Coastal Christian Ocean CityPsalm 20: The Answer In The Day of Trouble | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchPsalmsMatthew MaherPsalm 20: The Answer In The Day of Trouble | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchPsalm 20: The Answer In The Day of Trouble | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchThe Genesis & Revelation Of Antisemitism (Revelation 12) | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchThe Genesis & Revelation Of Antisemitism (Revelation 12) | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchThe Genesis & Revelation Of Antisemitism (Revelation 12) | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchWorking Hard Or Hardly Working? chunks.text: Sermon NotesPsalm 23:4Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil; For You are with me…“I will not fear because the Shepherd is near.”When the Son is before you, the shadow is behind you.Psalm 23:4Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.If God allows pain to touch your life, it’s because He wants you to use it to touch His life.Psalm 23:5You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies…The table is not the absence of enemies — it’s the presence of the Shepherd.Psalm 23:5You anoint my head with oil…Spiritual maturity isn’t measured by you getting more of the Holy Spirit, but rather the Holy Spirit getting more of you.Psalm 23:5My cup runs over.Psalm 23:6Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life; chunks.text:
Watch Psalm 32: Hiding From God or Hidden In God? | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church from Psalms with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Psalm 32: Hiding From God or Hidden In God? | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchPsalmsMatthew MaherNovember 13, 2025•53:43SummaryIn this message, “Hiding From God or Hidden In God?” Pastor Matthew Maher walks through Psalm 32 — a psalm of confession, cleansing, and the kind of joy that only forgiveness can bring.

From David’s silence and shame to his freedom and song, this psalm reveals the difference between concealing sin and confessing sin — between hiding from God and finding refuge in God.

When we stop covering what we’ve done, God starts covering who we are. And the life that was once weighed down with guilt becomes surrounded by mercy and filled with praise.

Because blessing doesn’t begin when we behave — blessing begins when we are forgiven.
