chunks.text:
Watch The Two Witnesses of the Tribulation | Revelation 11:3-14 [#32] | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church from Revelation with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

The Two Witnesses of the Tribulation | Revelation 11:3-14 [#32] | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchRevelationMatthew MaherAugust 2, 2026•59:03SummaryWho are the Two Witnesses of Revelation 11, and why does God send them during the darkest days in human history?

In this message, we examine one of the Bible's most fascinating prophetic passages—Revelation 11:3–14. While many debates surround the identity of the Two Witnesses, the greater question is why God sends them. Their ministry reminds us that even in the midst of judgment, God continues to extend mercy, proclaim truth, and call people to repentance.

We'll explore:
• The identity and purpose of the Two Witnesses
• The significance of the olive trees and lampstands from Zechariah 4
• The parallels between the Two Witnesses, Moses, and Elijah
• Why God empowers them with miraculous signs
• The rise of the Beast and Satan's counterfeit kingdom
• Why the world celebrates their deaths
• Their resurrection, ascension, and God's ultimate vindication
• What this passage teaches us about God's sovereignty, mercy, and final judgment

chunks.title: The Two Witnesses of the Tribulation | Revelation 11:3-14 [#32] | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Above all, Revelation 11 reminds us that God never leaves Himself without a witness. Though the world may reject His truth, God's purposes cannot be stopped, His witnesses cannot be silenced before their work is finished, and His Word will always prevail.

The War In Heaven: Satan's Future Expulsion | Revelation 12:7–12 [#35] | Matthew MaherRevelationMatthew MaherSeptember 6, 2026•54:16SummaryWar breaks out in heaven. Michael and his angels battle the Dragon, Satan is cast down to the earth, and heaven erupts in praise. But what exactly is happening—and if Satan was defeated at the cross, why does he still have access to accuse God's people?

In Revelation 12:7–12, Pastor Matthew Maher traces Satan's role as the deceiver, slanderer, and accuser, explains why his expulsion from heaven marks a major turning point in the Tribulation, and shows how God's people overcome—not through their own strength, but “by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony.”

The war is real, but the outcome is not in question. The cross settled Satan's fate. Revelation shows his judgment being carried out.

Scripture: Revelation 12:7–12
Series: The Last Revelation: The Countdown to the Kingdom

chunks.text:
Watch The War For Israel: Hated by Hell, Held by Heaven | Revelation 12:13–17 [#36] | Matthew Maher from Revelation with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

The War For Israel: Hated by Hell, Held by Heaven | Revelation 12:13–17 [#36] | Matthew MaherRevelationMatthew MaherSeptember 20, 2026•49:25SummaryRevelation 12 closes with the Dragon turning his fury toward Israel. Cast down from heaven and knowing his time is short, Satan persecutes the woman—but every attack is met by the providence and preservation of God. The Dragon may determine to pursue, but God has already determined how He will deliver, where He will preserve, what He will provide, and how long the season will last.

In this message, Pastor Matthew Maher explores the prophetic significance of Israel’s flight into the wilderness, the possible geographical clues surrounding her place of refuge, the final three-and-a-half years of the Tribulation, and the flood unleashed by the serpent. Through it all, Revelation 12 reveals a God whose providence goes before every circumstance: He prepares the place before His people ever reach the place.

chunks.title: The War For Israel: Hated by Hell, Held by Heaven | Revelation 12:13–17 [#36] | Matthew Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
The chapter ends with an enraged Dragon turning his warfare toward those who keep the commandments of God and hold the testimony of Jesus Christ. From Genesis to Revelation, the pattern remains: when Satan cannot destroy the covenant root, he attacks the covenant fruit. Yet Revelation 12 leaves no doubt about the outcome. The Dragon’s fury is fierce, but it cannot frustrate the purposes of God.

Whatever is chosen by heaven will be hated by hell—but it will be held by the hand of the Almighty.

chunks.title: The War Behind the World: The Dragon, Woman, and Child | Revelation 12:1-6 [#34] | Matthew Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Watch The War Behind the World: The Dragon, Woman, and Child | Revelation 12:1-6 [#34] | Matthew Maher from Revelation with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

The War Behind the World: The Dragon, Woman, and Child | Revelation 12:1-6 [#34] | Matthew MaherRevelationMatthew MaherAugust 30, 2026•53:37SummaryWhat if the events we see unfolding on earth are only part of the story?

Revelation 12 pulls back the curtain and gives us "heaven’s perspective on history," revealing an ancient spiritual war that stretches from Genesis to the Great Tribulation. Behind the kingdoms, conflict, and chaos stands the dragon—Satan—waging war against the woman, Israel, and her promised Seed, Jesus Christ.

Yet every attempt of the enemy ultimately serves the sovereign purposes of God. Satan could not stop Christ at His birth, and through His death came the very victory Satan sought to prevent.

In this message from Revelation 12:1–6, Pastor Matthew Maher traces the war behind the world—from the promise of the Seed, to the cross, to the throne, and finally to Israel’s flight into the wilderness for 1,260 days.

The enemy moves through history, but God rules over history.

Watch as we uncover the battle that shaped the world before time, the battle raging throughout time, and the battle that will climax at the end of time.

chunks.title: The “W” Means WOMEN: The WNBA Can’t Answer a Simple Question | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Watch The “W” Means WOMEN: The WNBA Can’t Answer a Simple Question | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher from Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

The “W” Means WOMEN: The WNBA Can’t Answer a Simple Question | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherTruth Over TrendMatthew MaherAugust 17, 2026•3:05SummaryA WNBA coach was asked a straightforward question: Should biological males be allowed to compete in the Women’s National Basketball Association?

Her answer? She wasn’t “educated enough” scientifically to say.
But the entire existence of women’s sports is based on the biological distinction between men and women. If biology doesn’t matter, why does the WNBA exist?

In this Truth Over Trend response, Matthew Maher examines the contradiction behind that answer and the growing reluctance to acknowledge one of the most basic realities of human biology.
Nobody is saying women can’t compete with men. The question is whether men should compete in the women’s category.

Scripture makes the foundation clear: “Male and female He created them.” — Genesis 1:27

What God designs, God defines.

We don’t need a deeper, more layered conversation to understand what God has made plain. And here’s the irony: in the name of being inclusive, we can become abusive to the very women the “W” is supposed to represent.

The Wound from Within | Matthew 5:10 | The Sermon On The Mount | Nick Johnson | Landmark ChurchSeptember 3, 2026•40:03SummarySome of the deepest wounds a believer feels do not come from the outside world. They come from inside the family of faith. In this closing message on the Beatitudes, we follow the thread of betrayal from Cain, to Peter in the courtyard, to Paul under attack from a church he helped build, and we ask how a Christian survives that kind of hurt without growing bitter or silent. Jesus does not promise us a life without it. He promises something better: that the kingdom of heaven already belongs to those who are persecuted for righteousness' sake. Come and be reminded that the wound does not get the last word.

There Is Power In The Thorn | 2 Corinthians 12:7-10 | Nick Johnson | Landmark ChurchTopical SermonsNick JohnsonApril 9, 2026•38:44SummaryThis sermon explores 2 Corinthians 12:7–10 by reframing weakness as the very means through which Christ’s power is displayed. It argues that Paul’s “thorn” is not a single issue but the ongoing hardships of his ministry, given by God to keep him humble and dependent. Through suffering, Paul learns that God’s grace is not removal of difficulty but sustaining presence and power within it. As a result, Paul moves from pleading for relief to boasting in weakness, recognizing it as the platform for Christ’s work in him. The sermon calls believers to trust God in their own “thorns,” seeing them not as obstacles but as instruments through which God accomplishes His purposes.

A plaque publicly thanking Governor Tim Walz for allowing the spread of Satanism inside the State Capitol building has raised serious questions about leadership, morality, and spiritual authority in government.

As Scripture warns, what is allowed into positions of power does not remain silent or symbolic—it takes residence. When darkness is invited in, it does not whisper; it occupies. This video calls out the spiritual implications of governance, the responsibility of leadership, and the urgent need for the Church to wake up before it’s too late.

Trust God's Sovereignty | Proverbs 16:1-9 | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark ChurchProverbsTerence SikoryakAugust 16, 2026•40:57SummaryProverbs 16 reminds us that wise living begins by trusting God's sovereignty while embracing our own responsibility. We are called to prepare diligently, examine our motives honestly, and cultivate the character of Christ, knowing that God directs the outcome even when life doesn't unfold according to our plans. True success is not measured by accomplishments or possessions, but by becoming the kind of person who pleases God and leaves behind a legacy of faithfulness. In the time remaining, our calling is simple: plan wisely, live humbly, and trust God with every step.

Truth Conceived vs. Truth Believed | John 8:1-11 | Nick Johnson | Landmark ChurchMarch 5, 2026•44:59SummaryIn John 8:1–11, we witness the collision between human self-appointed authority and divine truth. Religious leaders attempt to trap Jesus with the Law, but the embodiment of Truth turns a legal dispute into a confrontation of the conscience. As accusations fall silent and stones drop to the ground, we see that when Truth stands in the room, autonomy crumbles and hearts are exposed. Yet the same Word who judges also shows mercy, freeing the guilty and calling them into new obedience. This sermon invites us to consider whether we will stand over against Christ in self-righteous confidence—or sit at His feet, receive His grace, and walk in the light.

chunks.text:
Watch Truth They Won't Tolerate | 2 Timothy 4:1-5 |  Matthew Maher | Landmark Church from 2 Timothy with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Truth They Won't Tolerate | 2 Timothy 4:1-5 | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church2 TimothyMatthew MaherJune 22, 2025•53:19SummaryIn a culture quick to cancel and slow to repent, what happens when truth is no longer tolerated? In this timely and powerful message, Pastor Matthew Maher walks through 2 Timothy 4:1–5, echoing Paul’s eternal charge to preach the Word—clearly, courageously, and compassionately. When people choose affirmation over transformation and trade sound doctrine for soft lies, Christ’s call remains: stand firm, speak truth, and stay faithful.

This isn’t about being popular—it’s about being obedient. God's Word isn’t a suggestion to consider but a sword to carry. Whether the crowd applauds or opposes, we are called to proclaim what He has said—without edits or apologies. Because in the end, the question isn’t “Did they accept it?”—but “Were we faithful to deliver it?”

Will you stand for truth in a world that won’t tolerate it?

chunks.text:
Watch Victor Marx Asked Candace Owens One Question… And Her Non-Answer Said Everything | Truth Over Trend from Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Victor Marx Asked Candace Owens One Question… And Her Non-Answer Said Everything | Truth Over TrendTruth Over TrendMatthew MaherMay 26, 2026•4:29SummaryCandace Owens spent the interview aggressively scrutinizing Victor Marx’s trauma, military background, spiritual warfare beliefs, relationship with Charlie Kirk, and even his mental state. But the most revealing moment in the interview was not Victor’s answer. It was Candace’s non-answer.

When Victor asked one simple foundational question — “Do you believe the Bible to be the inerrant Word of God?” 

Candace could not plainly answer whether Scripture itself is the final authority. And that mattered. Because biblical discernment does not begin with platforms or personalities. It begins with authority. 

What is your final authority? God’s Word? Or yourself?

This Truth Over Trend response examines:

• “Poisoning the well” and manipulative framing
• The difference between discernment and arrogance
• Why authority matters in spiritual conversations
• How refusing to stand under Scripture eventually leads to standing above it
“That question and her non-answer was the tell; that exchange was the receipt.”

Walk in God's Wisdom: Three Great Truths to Live Wisely Pt 2 | Proverbs 16 10-24 | Terence SikoryakProverbsTerence SikoryakSeptember 13, 2026•38:22SummaryProverbs 16 reminds us that wisdom isn’t simply something we know—it is revealed in the choices we make every day. We choose justice by using our influence wisely, treating people with the same honest standard, and building the character necessary to carry whatever God entrusts to us. We choose humility by pursuing wisdom over wealth, staying on the right road, and remaining willing to say, “I could be wrong—what am I missing?” And we choose our words carefully, because what comes out of our mouths reveals what is happening in our hearts, and our words always leave something behind. In the time remaining, I want to use my influence wisely, walk the right road, stay humble—and leave people stronger because I was here.

chunks.text: Sermon NotesProverbs 24:3-4By wisdom a house is built,And by understanding it is established;And by knowledge the rooms are filledWith all precious and pleasant riches.3D Printer HomeProverbs 12:17He who speaks truth declares righteousness,But a false witness, deceit.Winston ChurchillThe truth is incontrovertible. Malice may attack it, ignorance may deride it, but in the end, there it is.Proverbs 12:18There is one who speaks like the piercings of a sword,But the tongue of the wise promotes health.Proverbs 12:19The truthful lip shall be established forever,But a lying tongue is but for a moment.Proverbs 12:20-22Deceit is in the heart of those who devise evil,But counselors of peace have joy.No grave trouble will overtake the righteous,But the wicked shall be filled with evil.Lying lips are an abomination to the LORD,But those who deal truthfully are His delight.Paul House: Old Testament Theology“God’s Blessings never leave the righteous, but they sometimes unfold in the midst of stressful and distressing circumstances.”Proverbs 12:23A prudent man conceals knowledge,But the heart of fools proclaims foolishnessProverbs 12:24The hand of the diligent will rule,But the lazy man will be put to forced labor.Proverbs 12:25Anxiety in the heart of man causes depression,But a good word makes it glad.Proverbs 12:26The righteous should choose his friends carefully,For the way of the wicked leads them astray.Proverbs 12:27The lazy man does not roast what he took in hunting,But diligence is man’s precious possessionProverbs 12:28In the way of righteousness is life,And in its pathway there is no death.View Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteView Sermon NoteMeet the SpeakerTerence SikoryakCare PastorAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerAbout the SpeakerJoin the Mission and GiveGive to support the mission of Landmark and help reach people with the gospel.Ways to GiveWays to GiveWays to GiveSermonsMore Sermons & ContentPreviousPreviousNextNextPsalm 39: Don't Waste Your Breath | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchPsalmsMatthew MaherPsalm 39: Don't Waste Your Breath | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchPsalm 39: Don't Waste Your Breath | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchThe Fix Is In! chunks.title: What’s with the Palms? A Misunderstood Victory | Palm Sunday | Nick Johnson | Landmark Church | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Watch What’s with the Palms? A Misunderstood Victory | Palm Sunday | Nick Johnson | Landmark Church from Topical Sermons with Nick Johnson. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

What’s with the Palms? A Misunderstood Victory | Palm Sunday | Nick Johnson | Landmark ChurchTopical SermonsNick JohnsonMarch 30, 2026•32:58SummaryThis sermon explores the meaning behind the palm branches waved on Palm Sunday and why the crowd misunderstood the kind of victory Jesus came to accomplish. While the people expected political deliverance, Christ came to secure a far greater victory over sin, death, and the wrath of God through His life, death, and resurrection. By examining the historical, biblical, and symbolic significance of the palms, we see that true victory was only possible through the incarnation—God entering into our condition to redeem us. The message calls us to see Jesus clearly, trust Him fully, and live lives rooted in His righteousness. Ultimately, Palm Sunday is not just a celebration of a moment, but a preview of the final victory that will be fully realized in the presence of God.

chunks.text:
Watch What Tyler Robinson’s Defense Actually Says: Charlie Kirk Case | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher from  with . Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

What Tyler Robinson’s Defense Actually Says: Charlie Kirk Case | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherAugust 31, 2026•4:20SummaryThere are plenty of theories online about the Charlie Kirk case. But before reacting to TikToks, posts, podcasts, and speculation, there’s a much better place to start: the actual court record.

In this Truth Over Trend response, Matthew Maher examines Tyler Robinson’s defense filing and what his attorneys are actually arguing.

The defense challenges whether the State established what was necessary at this stage, but it also argues in the alternative against the aggravating circumstance being pursued in connection with the death penalty.

That distinction matters.

Instead of beginning with distrust and calling it discernment, read the filing. Examine the arguments. Follow the evidence.

As Christians, we shouldn’t be afraid of questions, but we should also be willing to examine the answers.

Distrust ≠ discernment.

“The first one to plead his cause seems right, until his neighbor comes and examines him.” — Proverbs 18:17

chunks.title: What Is Being Terminated? The Question They Won’t Answer | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Watch What Is Being Terminated? The Question They Won’t Answer | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher from  with . Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

What Is Being Terminated? The Question They Won’t Answer | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherMarch 23, 2026•3:07SummarySometimes the most revealing moments aren’t found in what’s said—but in what’s avoided.

During discussion of House Bill 1957, a simple question was asked: What is being terminated in a pregnancy?
No clear answer came. Just deflection. Vague language. Political talking points. But truth doesn’t need to hide behind ambiguity.

A pregnancy doesn’t terminate a concept, a right, or an inconvenience—it terminates a life. The baby’s body is not the mother’s body. That’s not opinion. That’s biology.

And when something is so difficult to name, it’s often because the truth is too heavy to confront. “If you can’t name what you’re ending, you shouldn’t be allowed to end it.”

Scripture brings clarity where culture brings confusion: “Before I formed you in the womb I knew you.” — Jeremiah 1:5

It's not "my body, my choice." It's "My body, His choice." Because life begins with Him, is sustained by Him, and exists for Him.

When Babel Goes Digital: The Tech Revolution That Leads to Revelation | M. Maher | Landmark ChurchSigns Of The TimesMatthew MaherNovember 27, 2025•45:55SummaryThe first Tower of Babel was built with bricks—this one is being built with bandwidth. In this prophetic message, Pastor Matthew Maher reveals how modern technology, global connectivity, and artificial intelligence are rebuilding the digital Babel and preparing the world for the Beast System of Revelation 13.

Learn how:

• Babel provides the blueprint for global control
• Technology is reassembling what God once scattered
• Digital currency, biometric ID, and surveillance set up Rev. 13:16–17
• AI and global media make an “image that speaks” (Rev. 13:15) possible
• Convenience becomes conformity, efficiency becomes enslavement, and security becomes surrender
• The Church must stay rooted in Scripture, not the algorithm
• In a world driven by AI, believers must be led by eternal intelligence

We are the first generation where Revelation doesn’t sound symbolic—it sounds systemized.

Watch When False Apostles Look Anointed: A Warning About Kathryn Krick | Truth Over Trend w/ Matthew Maher from Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

When False Apostles Look Anointed: A Warning About Kathryn Krick | Truth Over Trend w/ Matthew MaherTruth Over TrendMatthew MaherAugust 3, 2026•5:41SummaryWhen false teachers come, they don't usually arrive looking dangerous—they arrive looking anointed.

In this video, Matthew Maher introduces and responds to a well-documented compilation highlighting concerning teachings and practices associated with Kathryn Krick.

Before watching, remember Paul's warning:

"For such are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into apostles of Christ. And no wonder! For Satan himself transforms himself into an angel of light." —2 Corinthians 11:13–14

The question isn't whether something appears spiritual. The question is whether it is biblical.

God calls every believer to exercise discernment by testing every teaching against His Word—not against personalities, platforms, emotions, or experiences.

As you watch, ask yourself:

Does this align with Scripture?
Does it exalt Christ?
Does it reflect the character of God?

Truth is never determined by popularity. Truth is determined by God's Word.

When Killers Become Causes: America’s Growing Moral Inversion | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherTruth Over TrendMatthew MaherSeptember 14, 2026•3:23SummarySomething deeply disturbing is happening in our culture.

From Luigi Mangione and Karmelo Anthony to Lindsay Clancy and Tyler Robinson, we’re watching a cultural instinct to turn people associated with the taking of human life into celebrities, symbols, and causes.

The cases are not legally identical. But the cultural reaction reveals something deeper: when sympathy for the accused becomes greater than our grief for the dead, we don’t merely have a crime problem, we have a conscience problem.

Scripture warned that perilous times would come—when people would become “brutal, despisers of good” (2 Timothy 3:1–3), and when people would not only practice unrighteousness but “approve of those who practice them” (Romans 1:32).

When killers become causes and victims become forgotten footnotes, evil no longer has to hide. It can operate in broad daylight and still find an audience.

When Hell Answers to Heaven (The Fifth Trumpet | First Woe) | Revelation 9:1-12 [#28] | M. MaherRevelationMatthew MaherJune 28, 2026•50:15SummaryAs the fifth trumpet sounds, Revelation moves into a new phase of judgment known as the first woe. A fallen star is given the key to the bottomless pit, smoke rises from the abyss, and a terrifying army of demonic locusts emerges to torment those who do not belong to God.

These are not ordinary locusts. They have crowns like gold, faces like men, hair like women, teeth like lions, breastplates of iron, and tails like scorpions. Their king bears a chilling name: Abaddon in Hebrew and Apollyon in Greek—both meaning "Destroyer."

Yet beneath the horror of this passage lies a powerful truth: hell does not operate independently of heaven. The fallen star is given a key. The locusts are given authority. Their torment is limited to five months. Even in judgment, God remains completely sovereign.

In this message, we explore:

chunks.title: When Hell Answers to Heaven (The Fifth Trumpet | First Woe) | Revelation 9:1-12 [#28] | M.  Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
The Fifth Trumpet Judgment (Revelation 9:1-12)
The identity of the fallen star
The meaning of the bottomless pit (abyss)
The terrifying locust army
Abaddon/Apollyon: the king called Destroyer
Why these judgments are called "woes"
God's sovereignty over hell and judgment
The contrast between the kingdom of darkness and the kingdom of Christ

Revelation 9 reminds us that every kingdom reflects its king. The kingdom of the Destroyer produces destruction. The kingdom of Christ produces life.

chunks.title: When Man Refuses To Answer To Heaven (Sixth Trumpet | Second Woe) | Rev. 9:13-21 [#29] | Matt Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Watch When Man Refuses To Answer To Heaven (Sixth Trumpet | Second Woe) | Rev. 9:13-21 [#29] | Matt Maher from Revelation with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

When Man Refuses To Answer To Heaven (Sixth Trumpet | Second Woe) | Rev. 9:13-21 [#29] | Matt MaherRevelationMatthew MaherJuly 5, 2026•60:09SummaryThe first woe revealed what happens when hell answers to heaven.

The second woe reveals what happens when man refuses to answer to heaven.

As the sixth trumpet sounds, four bound angels are released from the Euphrates, a massive demonic army is unleashed, and one-third of mankind is killed. Yet the greatest tragedy of Revelation 9 isn't the judgment itself—it is humanity's refusal to repent.

Just as the first woe reminded us that even hell answers to heaven, the second woe reminds us that the greatest danger isn't God's unwillingness to save—it's man's unwillingness to repent.

In this message, we explore:

chunks.title: When Man Refuses To Answer To Heaven (Sixth Trumpet | Second Woe) | Rev. 9:13-21 [#29] | Matt Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
• The significance of the Sixth Trumpet and the Second Woe
• The identity of the four bound angels
• Why the Euphrates River has always been associated with God's judgment
• The terrifying 200-million-man army
• What the serpent imagery reveals about Satan's deception
• Why idolatry is the root of every other sin
• The difference between an evidence problem and a heart problem
• Why only the Holy Spirit can bring true repentance

Revelation 9 isn't ultimately about demons, horsemen, or supernatural warfare.

It's about the condition of the human heart.

Hell answers to heaven. The question is...

Will we?

chunks.text: Sermon Notes• The point isn't to be mesmerized by demonology but to marvel at God's sovereignty.Then the sixth angel sounded: And I heard a voice from the four horns of the golden altar which is before God, saying to the sixth angel who had the trumpet, "Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates." — Revelation 9:13-14• To continually reject God's mercy is to eventually receive God's wrath.So the four angels, who had been prepared for the hour and day and month and year, were released to kill a third of mankind. Now the number of the army of the horsemen was two hundred million; I heard the number of them. — Revelation 9:15-16And thus I saw the horses in the vision: those who sat on them had breastplates of fiery red, hyacinth blue, and sulfur yellow; and the heads of the horses were like the heads of lions; and out of their mouths came fire, smoke, and brimstone. — Revelation 9:17By these three plagues a third of mankind was killed—by the fire and the smoke and the brimstone which came out of their mouth. For their power is in their mouth and in their tails; for their tails are like serpents, having heads; and with them they do harm. — Revelation 9:18-19• Sin begins with deception, but it always ends in destruction.But the rest of mankind, who were not killed by these plagues, did not repent of the works of their hands, that they should not worship demons, and idols of gold, silver, brass, stone, and wood, which can neither see nor hear nor walk. And they did not repent of their murders or their sorceries or their sexual immorality or their thefts. — Revelation 9:20-21• The root problem of the unrepentant is not a lack of evidence but a hardened heart."And this is the condemnation, that the light has come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil." — John 3:19• False worship always produces false living.• A culture that rejects the Author of life eventually authorizes death.Additional Scriptures Referenced: Exodus 30:10; chunks.title: When Heaven Stops To Listen (The Seventh Seal) | Revelation 8:1-5 [#26] | Matthew Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Watch When Heaven Stops To Listen (The Seventh Seal) | Revelation 8:1-5 [#26] | Matthew Maher from Revelation with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

When Heaven Stops To Listen (The Seventh Seal) | Revelation 8:1-5 [#26] | Matthew MaherRevelationMatthew MaherJune 7, 2026•45:23SummaryWhat happens when Heaven falls silent?

In Revelation 8, the Lamb opens the seventh seal, and for the first time in the book, the songs stop, the worship pauses, and Heaven grows silent. Why? What is so significant that even the hosts of Heaven stand in awe?

In this message, we explore the profound silence of Revelation 8, the seven angels and seven trumpets, and the powerful connection between the prayers of the saints and the judgments of God. From the bowls of incense in Revelation 5 to the cry of the martyrs in Revelation 6, and finally to the fire cast upon the earth in Revelation 8, we discover that God never forgets the prayers of His people.

Why is there silence in Heaven for thirty minutes?
What do the seven trumpets represent?
How are the prayers of the saints connected to God's unfolding plan?
What can believers learn when God seems silent?

One of the great lessons of Revelation 8 is this:
Just because Heaven is silent doesn't mean Heaven is inactive.
Sometimes we only see the dots. God sees the whole picture.

When The Word Consumes You (The Mystery of God) | Revelation 10:1-11 [#30] | Matthew MaherRevelationMatthew MaherJuly 19, 2026•49:16SummaryRevelation 10 pauses the trumpet judgments and pulls back the curtain on the unfolding mystery of God. From Genesis to Revelation, God's promises, covenants, redemption, the church, Israel, and the coming Kingdom are not disconnected stories—they are pieces of one divine plan moving toward fulfillment in Jesus Christ.

John is then commanded to take the little book and eat it. It is sweet in his mouth but bitter in his stomach—a powerful picture of the prophetic Word of God. Scripture comforts us, confronts us, and sometimes costs us. The Word must get into us before it can faithfully come out of us.

Don't just consume the Word. Let it consume you—and then carry it to the world.

Revelation 10:1–11

chunks.text:
Watch When Tragedy Becomes Trendy: A Generation Numb To Violence | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher from Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

When Tragedy Becomes Trendy: A Generation Numb To Violence | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherTruth Over TrendMatthew MaherMay 11, 2026•2:01SummaryA viral video of girls lip-syncing the final moments before Charlie Kirk’s murder reveals something far deeper happening beneath the surface of our culture.

This isn’t just about one inappropriate video.

It’s about a generation increasingly discipled by algorithms instead of truth… where tragedy becomes content, reverence is replaced with reactions, and viral moments are chased at the expense of virtue.

Jesus warned:
“Because lawlessness will abound, the love of many will grow cold.” (Matthew 24:12)

Pastor Matthew Maher examines how constant exposure to darkness and violence can desensitize hearts, numb consciences, and reshape culture in dangerous ways.

The answer is not to simply keep scrolling.

It’s to stop.
Reflect.
Repent.

And ask God for a return to truth, reverence, conviction, and the fear of the Lord.

Watch WHERE WAS THE EVIDENCE? | Tyler Robinson's Preliminary Hearing | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher from Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

WHERE WAS THE EVIDENCE? | Tyler Robinson's Preliminary Hearing | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherTruth Over TrendMatthew MaherJuly 20, 2026•3:06SummaryWHERE WAS THE EVIDENCE?

After months of viral claims surrounding the Tyler Robinson case, the preliminary hearing provided five days of sworn testimony, forensic evidence, witness testimony, and courtroom proceedings.

In this episode of Truth Over Trend, Pastor Matthew Maher examines the contrast between the extraordinary claims circulating online and the evidence presented in court. This video is not about criticizing someone's constitutional rights or deciding guilt or innocence. Instead, it asks a broader question:

When extraordinary claims are made, where is the evidence to support them?

As Christians, we are called to love truth, exercise discernment, and remain humble enough to follow the evidence wherever it leads.

Love the truth more than your opinions. Love Christ more than your tribe.

If this video challenged you, please like, subscribe, and share it with someone who values truth over narratives.

Watch Who Are The 144,000? (The Mark of the Lamb) | Revelation 7:1-8 [#24] | Matthew Maher from Revelation with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Who Are The 144,000? (The Mark of the Lamb) | Revelation 7:1-8 [#24] | Matthew MaherRevelationMatthew MaherMay 24, 2026•53:13SummaryWhat is the seal of God? Who are the 144,000 in Revelation 7?
Are they symbolic… or literal Israelites preserved during the Tribulation?

In this message, we walk verse-by-verse through Revelation 7:1–8 and uncover the biblical thread of the remnant running from Genesis to Revelation. Before judgment intensifies, heaven pauses the timeline to reveal a powerful truth: God knows those who are His.

In this teaching:
• The interlude of Revelation 7 explained
• The four winds and withheld judgment
• The sealing of the 144,000
• The Old Testament connection to Ezekiel 9
• The “remnant thread” throughout Scripture
• The Seal of God vs. the Mark of the Beast
• Satan as the great counterfeiter
• Why Revelation ultimately comes down to one question: Who do you belong to?

“Who is able to stand?” Those who belong to Jesus.

chunks.title: When Heaven Hears the Martyrs’ Cry (The Fifth Seal) [#22] | Revelation 6:9–11 | Matthew Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Watch When Heaven Hears the Martyrs’ Cry (The Fifth Seal) [#22] | Revelation 6:9–11 | Matthew Maher from Revelation with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

When Heaven Hears the Martyrs’ Cry (The Fifth Seal) [#22] | Revelation 6:9–11 | Matthew MaherRevelationMatthew MaherMay 3, 2026•54:55SummaryWhat happens when faith costs everything?

In the fifth seal of Revelation, the scene shifts from chaos on earth to a courtroom in heaven. The four horsemen have ridden—deception, war, famine, and death—and now we see the result: souls under the altar, crying out for justice.

This message explores Revelation 6:9–11 and answers one of the most human questions in Scripture: “How long, O Lord?”

These are not cries of doubt—they are cries of faith rooted in the character of God. He is holy. He is true. And His justice is not absent—it is appointed.

Even in the darkest period of human history, the gospel is still advancing. The world may produce martyrs, but the Lamb is producing worshippers.

God’s justice may be delayed—but it will not be denied.

chunks.title: Why Dada Can't Be Mama: When Culture Rewrites Design | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher | Sermons | Landmark Church
chunks.text:
Watch Why Dada Can't Be Mama: When Culture Rewrites Design | Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher from Truth Over Trend with Matthew Maher. Verse-by-verse biblical teaching from Landmark Church in Ocean City, NJ.

Why Dada Can't Be Mama: When Culture Rewrites Design | Truth Over Trend with Matthew MaherTruth Over TrendMatthew MaherApril 27, 2026•2:16SummaryIn a viral video, a child keeps saying “Mama”…
but is told there is no mama—only “Dada” or “Pop.”

This isn’t just a moment. It’s a message.

You can train language, but you can’t erase design.
And when a culture begins to redefine family and marriage, it doesn’t stop there—it starts to reshape how we value children themselves.

Even more telling? The comments.
Jokes about “throwing the baby away” followed by laughter.

This video isn’t about attacking people.
It’s about defending truth and God's created order.

God’s design isn’t restrictive—it’s protective.
And every child deserves what God intended from the beginning.

Where Is The Lamb? The Story From Genesis To Revelation | Easter 2026 | Landmark Church | Matt MaherTopical SermonsMatthew MaherApril 5, 2026•32:32SummaryFrom the beginning, the Bible has been asking one question:
“Where is the Lamb?” (Genesis 22:7)

From Abraham… to Passover… to the cross—every sacrifice was pointing to Jesus.

“Behold! The Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!” (John 1:29)

He didn’t just come to teach—He came to be the sacrifice. Not just to die for you… but instead of you.

And how do we know it worked?

There is no body in the grave. He is risen.

“Worthy is the Lamb who was slain!” (Revelation 5:12)

The Lamb you were looking for is the Lamb who was looking for you.

chunks.text: RechurchedRechurched podcast is meant to inspire conscience and instigate conviction, so people may know God and show God. In a day and age where the Church has been commercialized, the Christian secularized, and the cross sanitized, it’s time to return to a biblical faith that knows our life is to be crucified. The Apostle Paul said, “For I have determined not to know anything among you except Jesus Christ and Him crucified” (I Corinthians 2:2). Rechurched builds upon the time-tested and true brick and mortar of the Bible by calling the nominal Christian back to their faith’s foundation. Too many people are just going to church but have never experienced the transforming power of being the Church. So join us as we not only start the conversation about the identity crisis, but we end the conversation where Christ is, period.Thank you! Your submission has been received!Oops! chunks.title: Gene Wilkins | Pastor | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Gene WilkinsPG (Gene) has faithfully served the Lord in pastoral ministry for 66 years across multiple communities of faith. He began attending Landmark in 2017 after several years as pastor of Ventnor Community Church and was later invited to join the staff.While still serving in Ventnor, Gene began attending Thursday evening services and later the Saturday Men in Service gatherings. Through those relationships, several of the men helped restore damage to the church facility following Hurricane Sandy. Their care, faithfulness, and Christlike witness deeply impacted him and drew him more fully into the life and ministry of Landmark.Gene especially values the commitment and dedication of Landmark’s leadership and staff. He is grateful for the transparency and integrity of the pastors and elders and treasures the many opportunities he has to share the Word, lead in prayer, and mentor believers of every age.What matters most to him is the joy of serving alongside others in ministry and experiencing the grace that continues to be poured out on his life and family.Outside of church life, Gene enjoys spending time with Suzanne and their family, embracing their role as grandparents and great-grandparents, and encouraging their children as they faithfully walk with the Lord. He also values opportunities to share God’s Word in other communities of faith. chunks.text: Matthew MaherPastor•ElderVisit WebsiteVisit WebsiteVisit WebsiteSend them an emailSend them an emailSend them an emailView TikTokView TikTokView TikTokVisit InstagramVisit InstagramVisit InstagramVisit FacebookVisit FacebookVisit FacebookVisit XVisit XVisit XMatthew Maher serves as a pastor at Landmark Church in Ocean City, New Jersey, where he is passionate about helping people see the world through the lens of Scripture and live with conviction in a culture of confusion. He oversees teaching, discipleship, and ministry initiatives that equip believers to stand firm in God’s Word while staying anchored in the hope of Christ.Matthew’s heart for ministry has been shaped by a unique journey—from playing professional soccer early in life to later experiencing firsthand the transforming power of God’s grace. His story is one of redemption, calling, and a deep desire to see others encounter the same life-changing freedom found in Jesus.He is also the author of several books, hosts the Rechurched podcast, and leads the Truth Over Trend platform, which exists to help Christians navigate today’s world with wisdom, discernment, and bold faith.Above all, Matthew loves preaching God’s Word, shepherding people toward spiritual maturity, and reminding the Church that we are living in urgent days—but with an unshakable Savior.Matthew lives in Egg Harbor Township, New Jersey with his wife Sarah and their children, Willow, Ezekiel, and Malachi. chunks.title: Nick Johnson | Family Life Minister | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Nick JohnsonFamily Life Pastor•ElderNick Johnson serves as the Family Life Pastor at Landmark Church, where he oversees the core areas of education, discipleship, and curriculum development. His role centers on equipping families and strengthening the church’s discipleship pathways, ensuring that what is taught and practiced aligns clearly with the mission of spiritual growth. In addition to administrative oversight, Nick also has the privilege of preaching from time to time, discipling individuals and families, and stepping in wherever there is a need.Discipleship and teaching are at the heart of his ministry. He is deeply passionate about helping people grow in their understanding of Scripture and mature both spiritually and emotionally. One of the things he appreciates most about Landmark is its collaborative culture. The consistent support and guidance from leadership and staff create an environment where ministry is not done alone but together, fostering unity and shared growth.Nick has been on staff for over three years and, along with his wife Kelly, has been part of the Landmark family for five years. They are grateful to call this church home. Nick and Kelly have five children—four boys and one girl: Dylan, Ryan, Sean, Ronan, and Maisy. Nick was recently ordained on July 19, 2026 as a pastor. Outside of ministry, Nick enjoys spending time with his family, gardening, and reading. chunks.text: Terence SikoryakTerence is the Pastor of the Care team. On the Care team we get to meet people at certain intersections of their lives.  We shepherd souls and see the Gospel at work in real time.Sting has a song "Fragile". It reminds us of how fragile we are and no one is immune from pain. In the Time Remaining we are charged with shepherding souls through those times of pain and loss. Terence enjoys reading and doing his radio show which he has been hosting since 1996. He also enjoys the beach and watching his wife Jennifer surf. chunks.title: Ethan Hoover | Creative Director | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Ethan HooverEthan serves as the Creative Director at Landmark Church, leading digital media, content, and communications to help the church communicate clearly and beautifully. A graduate of Regent University with a Bachelor of Science in Business Marketing, he brings both entrepreneurial experience and ministry conviction to his role. Before stepping into full-time ministry, he worked in marketing for organizations in Virginia Beach and Nashville, developing a passion for strategy, storytelling, and building things that last.At his core, Ethan has a heart to resource the Church. He loves helping people grow excited about the Bible—its books, its people, and the unified story it tells—and is passionate about creating tools that make deep biblical learning accessible and engaging. He thrives at the intersection of theology, creativity, and innovation, and is driven by a desire to strengthen the local church for the long haul.Ethan believes all of life belongs to the Lord. Whether serving in vocational ministry or in the marketplace, his aim is the same: to glorify God, steward his gifts faithfully, and support the work of the local church wherever the Lord places him. Above all, he is grateful to be the husband of his wife, Sage, and is committed to loving and leading his family well in every season. chunks.title: Appointed to Power: Divine Favor for Direct Access | Genesis 41:38-43 |  Shawn Hyland | Landmark Church
chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastAppointed to Power: Divine Favor for Direct Access | Genesis 41:38-43 | Shawn HylandShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsAppointed to Power: Divine Favor for Direct Access | Genesis 41:38-43 | Shawn HylandIn this timely message, we will explore how God sovereignly uses human government to elevate His people into positions of influence and authority. From Joseph in Egypt to Daniel in Babylon, to Mordecai in Persia, Scripture reveals a consistent pattern: those appointed by kings, emperors, and governors often wield greater impact than the rulers themselves. These appointed officials—though humanly selected—carry divine favor, possess direct access to the chief executive, and exercise delegated authority to protect, provide for, and advocate on behalf of God’s people. As New Jersey prepares to elect a new governor this November, we must recognize the spiritual and practical significance of this moment. The winner will appoint dozens of unnamed individuals to govern our families, shape education, and influence religious liberty. Their decisions will either favor or frustrate the people of God. Join us as we examine the biblical record and reflect on the modern implications of executive appointments. This is not just a study of ancient empires—it’s a call to spiritual discernment and civic engagement in our own time. chunks.title: Built to Stand Together: Striving Side by Side for the Gospel | Philippians 1:27-30| Nick Johnson | Landmark Church
chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastBuilt to Stand Together: Striving Side by Side for the Gospel | Philippians 1:27-30| Nick JohnsonShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsBuilt to Stand Together: Striving Side by Side for the Gospel | Philippians 1:27-30| Nick JohnsonThis sermon explores Paul’s call in Philippians 1:27–30 for believers to live in a manner worthy of the gospel by standing firm together in unity and courage. Through vivid biblical teaching and powerful illustrations, we see that perseverance under pressure is not achieved alone but through a church striving side by side in one Spirit and one purpose. Paul’s prayer for ever-growing, Christ-shaped love reveals that unity is both the foundation of spiritual strength and the means God uses to advance the gospel in the midst of suffering. The message challenges personal agendas that fracture the body of Christ and calls believers to sacrificial love that builds one another up. Ultimately, it shows that when the church stands united under pressure, Christ is glorified and the world sees the power of the gospel on display. chunks.title: After The Lie Comes The Loss (Seals 2-4: The Red, Black, & Pale Horse) | Revelation 6:3-8 | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church
chunks.text: The first horse brought deception. Now the consequences ride.  In this message we open the next three seals of Revelation 6 and follow the red, black, and pale

chunks.title: After The Lie Comes The Loss (Seals 2-4: The Red, Black, & Pale Horse) | Revelation 6:3-8 | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church
chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastAfter The Lie Comes The Loss (Seals 2-4: The Red, Black, & Pale Horse) | Revelation 6:3-8 | Matthew MaherShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsAfter The Lie Comes The Loss (Seals 2-4: The Red, Black, & Pale Horse) | Revelation 6:3-8 | Matthew MaherThe first horse brought deception. Now the consequences ride. In this message we open the next three seals of Revelation 6 and follow the red, black, and pale horses as they unleash war, famine, and death on a Christ-rejecting world. This is not random chaos — this is divine consequence. Seal by seal. Horse by horse. In order. In consequence. What the white horse promised, the red horse removes. What the red horse destroys, the black horse starves. What the black horse starves, the pale horse buries. And following behind the pale horse — Hades. A world that rejected the fullness of God will be famished without God. But there is hope. Because the same Lamb opening these seals holds the keys to Death and Hades. And what belongs to Him — no horse can take. In this sermon: • The red horse and the removal of peace — Revelation 6:3-4 • The black horse and engineered scarcity — Revelation 6:5-6 • The pale horse, Death, and Hades — Revelation 6:7-8 • The Greek word toxon — bow, poison, and God's covenant rainbow • Why judgment is sequential, not random • The only peace that cannot be taken — Romans 5:1, Colossians 1:20 • Christ holds the keys — Revelation 1:18 Scriptures referenced: Revelation 6:3-8 | Revelation 1:18 | Romans 5:1 | Colossians 1:20 | Daniel 9:27 | 1 Thessalonians 5:3 | Ezekiel 14:21 | Revelation 12:3 | John 6:35 Deception opens the door. War walks in. Famine empties the table. And death clears the room. But Christ holds the keys. In this message we open the next three seals of Revelation 6 and follow the red, black, and pale horses as they unleash war, famine, and death on a Christ-rejecting world. This is not random chaos — this is divine consequence. Seal by seal. Horse by horse. In order. In consequence. What the white horse promised, the red horse removes. chunks.title: Faithfully Free Until The Finish: A Declaration of Dependence | 2 Timothy 4:6-8 | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church
chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastFaithfully Free Until The Finish: A Declaration of Dependence | 2 Timothy 4:6-8 | Matthew MaherShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsFaithfully Free Until The Finish: A Declaration of Dependence | 2 Timothy 4:6-8 | Matthew MaherAs the world fights to be independent of God, the believer is called to make a declaration of dependence on Christ. In this powerful July 4th weekend message, we look at the words of Paul as he nears the end of his race—not holding back, but pouring out his life for the glory of God. Just as the 56 signers of the Declaration of Independence risked everything for earthly liberty, Paul gave everything for eternal freedom. This message challenges us to live like Paul—fighting the good fight, keeping the faith, and finishing the race—not with self-preservation, but with a poured-out life of worship. Because when freedom is divorced from faith, it becomes rebellion—but when it bows to Christ, it becomes righteousness. Be sure to subscribe to the Landmark Church YouTube Channel and wherever you access podcasts to stay updated on all upcoming sermons. Because when freedom is divorced from faith, it becomes rebellion—but when it bows to Christ, it becomes righteousness. These are the ones who came out of the Great Tribulation — washed white by the blood of the Lamb, clothed in victory, and shepherded forever in the presence of God. chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastFaith That Feeds | John 6:52-59 | Nick JohnsonShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsFaith That Feeds | John 6:52-59 | Nick JohnsonThis sermon explores Jesus’ teaching in John 6, tracing the movement from belief to abiding. It shows how many followed Christ for what He provided, but only true disciples remained when His words demanded trust and dependence. Through examples like Richard Jewell’s “trial by media,” it warns against faith built on appearances and calls believers to a faith that endures when perception turns hostile. The message urges listeners to redeem their time by seeking God’s will and feeding daily on the life of Christ. Ultimately, it challenges the church to cultivate abiding faith—steady, tested, and sustained by union with the Bread of Life. chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastFulfillment or Frustration it’s your Choice | Proverbs 13:12-18 | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark ChurchShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsFulfillment or Frustration it’s your Choice | Proverbs 13:12-18 | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark ChurchFulfillment and frustration do not come from circumstances, but from whether a man remains under God’s authority or insists on governing himself. The fear of the Lord brings the soul into proper order, where the mind submits to truth, the emotions become quiet, and the will yields in obedience, allowing God’s life to flow unhindered. When a man resists correction and clings to self-rule, he may preserve his independence, but he loses inward life and becomes governed by decay rather than by grace. Therefore, in the time remaining, the decisive question is not what a man achieves outwardly, but whether he has surrendered inwardly—because only the surrendered life can know true fulfillment before God. chunks.title: God's Wisdom in the Christmas Message: Enjoy the Season But Get the Message | Terence Sikoryak | Landmark Church
chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastGod's Wisdom in the Christmas Message: Enjoy the Season But Get the Message | Terence SikoryakShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsGod's Wisdom in the Christmas Message: Enjoy the Season But Get the Message | Terence SikoryakChristmas is not just a sentimental tradition, but a moment of divine wisdom calling us to discern God’s greater redemptive plan. Rooted in John 3:16, it reveals the true meaning of Christmas through four realities: humanity’s danger of perishing, God’s loving design to rescue us through Christ, our duty to respond in faith and surrender, and our destiny of eternal life that begins now. Drawing from Proverbs, it contrasts superficial celebration with wise discernment, urging listeners not to miss what God is revealing in the season. Christmas is shown as the fulfillment of God’s long-planned compassion—new life formed through the womb—calling each person to respond personally to the gospel. Ultimately, the message invites us to enjoy Christmas fully, but to do so with wisdom that leads to life, transformation, and eternity with God. chunks.text: This sermon explores how God sometimes leads His people into unexpected setbacks; moments that feel like going backwards, in order to reveal His glory and stren

chunks.title: Glory in the Setbacks: When God Turns You Back to Move You Forward | Exodus 14:1-25 | Nick Johnson | Landmark Church
chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastGlory in the Setbacks: When God Turns You Back to Move You Forward | Exodus 14:1-25 | Nick JohnsonShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsGlory in the Setbacks: When God Turns You Back to Move You Forward | Exodus 14:1-25 | Nick JohnsonThis sermon explores how God sometimes leads His people into unexpected setbacks; moments that feel like going backwards, in order to reveal His glory and strengthen their faith. Drawing from Exodus 14, we see Israel trapped at the Red Sea not by accident, but by divine design, as God positions them where only His power can save. In their fear, God moves the pillar of fire behind them, stands between them and destruction, and displays His glory by breaking the wheels of Egypt’s chariots. The same glory that fought for Israel now strengthens believers from within, as Paul prays in Ephesians 3:14–16. Through personal testimony and Scripture, the message calls us to trust God’s hand in our pain, knowing His glory was at work then, is at work now, and will be revealed fully in the days to come. chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastHow Then Should We Respond? | Nick Johnson | Landmark ChurchShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsHow Then Should We Respond? | Nick Johnson | Landmark ChurchHow Then Should We Respond?, confronts the reality of persecution and the lies that fuel it. From Tertullian’s defense of early Christians to Jesus’ own trial, we see that truth will always be twisted by a world that hates the light. Yet God uses suffering not to break us but to train us in obedience, preparing us for greater faithfulness. And because our lives are hidden with Christ, even death itself becomes victory, not defeat. The call is simple and urgent: stand firm in truth, endure in hope, and live as those already surrendered to Jesus. chunks.text: Few doctrines generate more confusion than the rapture — not because Scripture is unclear, but because different passages are often flattened into a single even

chunks.title: Is The Church In The Tribulation (The Rapture Isn't A Secret - Part 2) | Matthew 24 | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church
chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastIs The Church In The Tribulation (The Rapture Isn't A Secret - Part 2) | Matthew 24 | Matthew MaherShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsIs The Church In The Tribulation (The Rapture Isn't A Secret - Part 2) | Matthew 24 | Matthew MaherFew doctrines generate more confusion than the rapture — not because Scripture is unclear, but because different passages are often flattened into a single event. In Part 2 of this teaching, we return to the passages people struggle with most: Matthew 24. The “elect.” The last trumpet. The restrainer. Israel and the Church. Rather than avoiding these texts, we place them in their proper context and allow Scripture to interpret Scripture. In this message, we explore: • Why Matthew 24 describes the Second Coming, not the rapture • Who the “elect” are — and why context matters • Why the “last trumpet” is not the same trumpet everywhere • What must be removed before the Antichrist is revealed • How salvation continues during the Tribulation • Why distinguishing Israel and the Church is foundational to biblical prophecy • Why imminence matters for how believers live today This doctrine was never meant to divide the Church. It was meant to anchor hope, fuel holiness, and produce urgency. Key Scriptures: Matthew 24, 1 Corinthians 15, 1 Thessalonians 4–5, 2 Thessalonians 2, Daniel 9 Be sure to subscribe to the Landmark Church YouTube Channel and wherever you access podcasts to stay updated on all upcoming sermons. Learn why the Gospel wasn’t meant to stop with you but to flow through you, and how your link in the Gospel chain can shape generations to come. The holiness of God reveals the true weight of mercy, showing that sin must be answered either in the sinner or in a substitute. Jesus Christ is that perfect substitute—the merciful High Priest who bore the judgment His people deserved and secured mercy through the cross. Because believers have received mercy of such magnitude, they are called to extend mercy within the church and to a world still in need of the gospel. chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastProverbs 13: Choices That Shape Our Lives | Terence SikoryakShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsProverbs 13: Choices That Shape Our Lives | Terence SikoryakDrawing connections to modern culture—including the lure of wealth, the commodification of creativity, and the dangers of pride—the message emphasizes that wisdom protects while foolishness inevitably collapses. By examining themes such as diligence, contentment, counsel, and the law of sowing and reaping, the sermon calls listeners to pursue inner character rather than outward success. Ultimately, it urges us to anchor our lives in godly wisdom, practice daily gratitude, and choose the path that leads to enduring fruitfulness. We move toward them one decision at a time. In this message from Proverbs 15, we explore how the heart shapes our words, our path determines our direction, and our harvest reveals the life we have cultivated. Through the lens of the Kingdom of God, Jesus calls us beyond behavior modification into a transformed heart that brings life, peace, and wisdom to a broken world. In the time remaining, we cannot afford to live accidentally—our future is not an event; it is a direction. chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastProverbs 15 pt. 2 | The Path and The Harvest | Terence SikoryakShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsProverbs 15 pt. 2 | The Path and The Harvest | Terence SikoryakLife doesn't change because we wish it would; it changes because we become different people. Proverbs 15 reminds us that every harvest begins long before the fruit appears—it begins in the condition of the heart, continues on the path of our daily choices, and eventually reveals itself in the life we build. Every conversation, every habit, every response to correction, and every decision is either moving us upward in wisdom or downward into regret. In the time remaining, don't chase more things; become a better person. When your character grows, your path changes, and when your path changes, your harvest inevitably follows. chunks.title: Psalm 26: Integrity Stands & Perversity Slips | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church
chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastPsalm 26: Integrity Stands & Perversity Slips | Matthew MaherShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsPsalm 26: Integrity Stands & Perversity Slips | Matthew MaherIntegrity Stands & Perversity Slips is a timely call to walk uprightly in a world bent on corruption. Preaching from Psalm 26, Pastor Matthew Maher unpacks David’s bold appeal for God to examine his heart and vindicate his walk. This message draws a clear contrast between the faithful who walk in truth and the wicked who walk in schemes. While others scheme, bribe, and deceive—the one who walks in integrity stands on solid ground. In a culture full of compromise, this sermon urges believers to pursue spiritual stability, moral clarity, and wholehearted devotion to the God who sees the heart and rewards the righteous. chunks.title: Psalm 34: Not Safe, But Secure | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church
chunks.text: Psalm 34 was written by David after one of the most humiliating moments of his life—when he fled for his life and pretended madness before King Achish in Gath.

chunks.title: Psalm 34: Not Safe, But Secure | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church
chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastPsalm 34: Not Safe, But Secure | Matthew MaherShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsPsalm 34: Not Safe, But Secure | Matthew MaherPsalm 34 was written by David after one of the most humiliating moments of his life—when he fled for his life and pretended madness before King Achish in Gath. What followed was not bitterness or silence, but praise. This psalm shows us how public worship can be born from private crisis, and how deliverance does not always mean escape, but redemption. In this message, we walk through Psalm 34 as both wisdom and testimony, tracing David’s journey from fear to praise, from desperation to invitation, and from affliction to assurance. We discover that praise is not driven by feelings, but by focus; not shaped by circumstances, but by perspective. God delivers us not only from enemies, but from fear itself—and He draws especially near to the brokenhearted. Psalm 34 also points us forward to Christ. David writes that God guards all the bones of the righteous, foreshadowing Jesus’ crucifixion, where not one of His bones was broken. Unbroken bones reveal unbroken promises. Righteousness does not exempt us from suffering, but it guarantees redemption through it. This psalm ends where the Gospel begins: rescue by redemption. Trusting the Lord does not remove tribulation, but it does remove condemnation. Or Is It? | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsPsalm 37: Evil Is Winning... Or Is It? | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchPsalm 37 answers one of the oldest questions believers wrestle with: Why do the wicked seem to prosper while the righteous struggle? In this teaching, we walk through David’s wisdom as he contrasts two completely different ways of living: the way of the wicked and the way of the righteous. The wicked may appear powerful, wealthy, and successful for a moment, but their influence is temporary. The righteous, though often overlooked or opposed, are upheld by the Lord and ultimately inherit what God has promised. David shows us that God’s economy operates differently than the world’s. What the world measures by riches, power, and control, God measures by righteousness, trust, and faithfulness. If you’ve ever been discouraged by the apparent success of evil or wondered how believers should respond when injustice seems to prevail, Psalm 37 gives a clear answer: Do not fret. Trust the Lord. The end of the righteous is peace. “The salvation of the righteous is from the LORD; He is their strength in the time of trouble.” — Psalm 37:39 Be sure to subscribe to the Landmark Church YouTube Channel and wherever you access podcasts to stay updated on all upcoming sermons. chunks.title: Psalm 39: Don't Waste Your Breath | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church | Landmark Church
chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastPsalm 39: Don't Waste Your Breath | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsPsalm 39: Don't Waste Your Breath | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchThere are moments in life when you know you shouldn’t speak, but everything in you wants to. So you hold it in. You bite your tongue. You try to stay composed in a world that’s loud, wrong, and watching. But what you suppress doesn’t disappear—it builds. And before long, what started as restraint becomes pressure, and what was meant to guard your mouth begins to consume your heart. In Psalm 39, David takes us from a muzzled mouth to a burning soul, and ultimately to eternal perspective. This message unpacks the tension we all feel: Speaking too quickly… Suppressing too long… And reveals the solution: Before we speak to others, we must learn to speak to God. David’s turning point comes when he shifts from reacting to people to realigning before God: “And now, Lord, what do I wait for? My hope is in You.” (Psalm 39:7) Hope is not found in fixing problems—it’s found in fixing your eyes on God’s promises. This sermon will challenge you to: Stop wasting your breath on unnecessary battles Stop carrying what was never yours to carry Start bringing everything to God Because life is a breath and your hope must be bigger than your breath. In Psalm 40, David testifies of crying out to God from the miry clay — and discovering that the same God who hears us in the pit is able to lift us onto the rock. What began with waiting eventually turned into worship, proclamation, and renewed dependence upon the Lord. Psalm 42 is one of the most honest passages in all of Scripture. The psalmist thirsts for God, battles despair, wrestles with difficult questions, and yet refuses to let go of hope. In this message, we discover that faith and discouragement can occupy the same heart at the same time, and we learn how to preach truth to a downcast soul. Whether you're walking through grief, spiritual dryness, disappointment, or simply a season where God feels far away, Psalm 42 reminds us that our hope is not found in changing circumstances, but in an unchanging God. In this message: The difference between listening to yourself and preaching to yourself Why our tears can make terrible theologians What "deep calls unto deep" really means Trusting God's heart when you cannot trace His hand Finding hope in the midst of adversity Key Verse: "Why are you cast down, O my soul? chunks.title: Psalm 43: When God Feels Far Away | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church | Landmark Church
chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastPsalm 43: When God Feels Far Away | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsPsalm 43: When God Feels Far Away | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchHave you ever felt like God was distant? Like your prayers were unanswered, your circumstances were overwhelming, or your soul was simply exhausted? Psalm 43 reminds us that faith is not the absence of difficult questions—it is bringing those questions to the right Person. In this message, we'll discover: Why the psalmist asks God to "plead his cause" against an ungodly culture. How God's light and truth provide direction when life feels confusing. Why David's greatest desire wasn't relief—but God Himself. How Jesus fulfills the altar and becomes our only hope. Why the most important sermon you'll ever hear may be the one you preach to your own soul. If you're walking through discouragement, spiritual dryness, or wondering where God is, this psalm will remind you that your feelings are not your final authority. God's truth is. Key Takeaways: • Ask Him your questions—but remember: He is the answer. • Don't ask God to merely change your conditions; ask Him to change your direction. • God isn't your emergency exit or your last resort—He is your exceeding joy. • When your soul is discouraged, preach God's promises to your heart. chunks.title: Psalm 36: When The Fear of God Is Gone | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church | Landmark Church
chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastPsalm 36: When The Fear of God Is Gone | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsPsalm 36: When The Fear of God Is Gone | Matthew Maher | Landmark ChurchIn Psalm 36, David exposes what happens when there is no fear of God before our eyes. Sin doesn’t accuse—it affirms. The wicked flatter themselves, minimize evil, and drift into a lifestyle of deception and arrogance. But then the psalm makes a stunning theological pivot: from the darkness of man to the heights of God. God’s mercy reaches to the heavens, His righteousness stands like the mountains, and His people find refuge under the shadow of His wings. This message is a call to recover a big view of God, a proper hatred of sin, and a deep trust in the Lord’s justice. You don’t have to fight for vengeance—pride will take the wicked “there,” and God will deal with them far better than we ever could. What does it mean to have a "pure" heart, and how can sinful people possess one? We trace how God gives us a new heart, why we still battle sin even after receiving it, and what genuine peacemaking looks like when it refuses to settle for surface-level quiet. The message closes with a searching question for every listener: not whether you have a father, but which one you resemble right now. Come and see how the face you will one day behold and the name you will one day bear are already being shaped by the Master you serve today. chunks.title: Revelation 6–18 Overview: Heaven’s Order, Earth’s Collapse | The Final Seven Years | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church
chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastRevelation 6–18 Overview: Heaven’s Order, Earth’s Collapse | The Final Seven Years | Matthew MaherShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsRevelation 6–18 Overview: Heaven’s Order, Earth’s Collapse | The Final Seven Years | Matthew MaherWhat looks like chaos on earth is actually controlled judgment from heaven. In this message, we walk through Revelation 6–18, the most intense seven-year period in human history—the Great Tribulation. This is not random destruction or symbolic confusion. It is a structured, escalating unveiling of God’s judgment, released by the Lamb who once took judgment for the world. From the seals to the trumpets to the bowls, we see how judgment unfolds, intensifies, and ultimately leads to the collapse of a Christ-rejecting world system. But behind it all is a deeper reality—a spiritual war that has been raging since before time. Revelation 12 reveals the war. Revelation 13 reveals the beast. Revelation 14 reminds us—the Lamb wins. This is not just prophecy… it’s trajectory. chunks.title: Signs of the Times | Lawlessness & The Lens of Delusion: Is ICE The Gestapo? | Matthew Maher | Landmark Church
chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastSigns of the Times | Lawlessness & The Lens of Delusion: Is ICE The Gestapo? | Matthew MaherShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsSigns of the Times | Lawlessness & The Lens of Delusion: Is ICE The Gestapo? | Matthew MaherWith every passing week, new headlines surface—but beneath the noise, a deeper pattern is being revealed. Lawlessness is defended. Authority is vilified. Moral categories are inverted. And many are increasingly confident in beliefs that Scripture warned us about long ago. In this Signs of the Times message, Pastor Matthew walks verse by verse through Romans 13:1–5, exposing what the Bible teaches about God-ordained authority, law and order, conscience, and restraint. This sermon is not about a political party or a single incident—it is about spiritual discernment in an age of moral confusion. The provocative question “Is ICE the Gestapo?” is not posed as a historical claim, but as a diagnostic lens—revealing how cultural rhetoric, media narratives, and ideological conditioning shape how people define good and evil. Drawing from Isaiah 5:20, Romans 1, Matthew 24, and key Old Testament warnings, this message confronts the inversion of truth happening in real time. You’ll also hear: • Why lawlessness is more than chaos—it’s moral relativity • How dehumanizing rhetoric conditions people to excuse violence • Why restraint is a biblical mercy, not tyranny • The role of the Church in times of confusion • Why the Book of Revelation matters now This message calls believers to clarity—not outrage. chunks.text: PodcastPodcastPodcastSickness of the Heart | Nick JohnsonShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsSickness of the Heart | Nick JohnsonThis sermon explores the biblical call to vigilance by framing sin as both an internal sickness that must be treated and an enemy that must be confronted. Drawing from Proverbs 4 and the language of Scripture, it clarifies where the battle with sin is truly fought, within the heart, not merely against external influences like the world or Satan. The message challenges common patterns of blame-shifting and emphasizes the believer’s responsibility to actively put sin to death while resting in Christ’s finished work. Grounded in the resurrection of Jesus, the sermon shows how victory over sin empowers watchful, disciplined, and hope-filled obedience. Ultimately, it calls believers to guard their hearts with confidence, knowing that life and healing flow from Christ’s triumph. MaherShareButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextButton TextLandmark SermonsSigns of the Times: Shaken Foundations: May 17, 1776 - 250 Years Later | Hebrews 12:25-28 | M. MaherAmerica was born in a moment of shaking. On May 17, 1776, before independence was declared, the Continental Congress called the nation to humiliation, fasting, repentance, and prayer — asking God to establish America upon “a solid and lasting foundation.” Now, 250 years later, we again find ourselves in a time of shaking: political shaking | moral shaking | cultural shaking | spiritual shaking. Hebrews 12 reminds us that God allows shaking so that what cannot be shaken may remain. When the foundations are destroyed, what can the righteous do? Like Nehemiah — rebuild the wall. Like Ezekiel — stand watch on the wall. Like Esther — intercede in the gap of the wall. Like Daniel — discern the writing on the wall. This Signs of the Times message explores America’s foundations, the dangers of false foundations, and the unshakable Kingdom of Christ.
