chunks.title: Landmark Church
chunks.text: Skip to main contentWatch LiveWatch LiveLiveDashboardDashboardDashboardenEnglish (United States)SpanishSearchMenuSeptember 20, 2026Q&AsWhat Does The Bible Say About____?VariousAbout the SeriesThis week was not a regular series lesson. It was a student Q&A night: students submitted questions in advance, and our leaders, Liam, Nick, and Aaron, worked through as many as they could as a team.Passages: various, spanning Genesis to RevelationWhat Was TaughtNine student questions got a full answer this round, spread across three broad categories.Bible MysteriesA cluster of questions dug into things Scripture only partly explains. Students asked about Noah's Ark, including some of the physical evidence people point to at Mount Ararat, and about Enoch, the rare Old Testament figure who never experienced death. Others asked what Satan actually looks like, and whether time moved differently in the earliest days of Genesis, which opened into why the patriarchs lived so long. In each case, the approach was the same: state clearly what Scripture does and does not say, then separate that from speculation, while still pointing to the bigger spiritual takeaway behind the question.Everyday Life and CharacterOther questions were more practical. Students asked about video games and where to draw the line on content, about how to grow in patience through hard seasons, and about how to handle friendships with people who don't share their faith. These answers leaned on the same core idea: Scripture doesn't always name the specific situation, but it gives clear principles, like weighing whether something is helpful and not just permissible, for working out the answer.Identity and MissionThe last group centered on who students are and what they're here to do. One question dealt with insecurity and finding identity in Christ rather than in comparison or performance. Another asked about the responsibility to share the gospel with others. Both pointed back to the same foundation: security and purpose come from a relationship with Jesus, not from anything students accomplish on their own.A handful of submitted questions, on the kings in Genesis 14, the number of archangels, filing lawsuits, love, and the Law, didn't get answered this round. Worth checking back in on those in a future Q&A.Talk About It at HomeSince this was a Q&A night rather than a single lesson, here are a few openers pulled from tonight's topics to get a conversation going:Which of tonight's questions would you have asked if you could ask the Bible anything?Where do you feel the most insecure right now, and where do you think that insecurity is coming from?How do you decide whether something you're watching or playing is actually good for you, not just "not technically wrong"?Who is someone in your life who might need to hear about Jesus from you specifically?What's something you're waiting on right now that's testing your patience?‍

chunks.title: Landmark Church
chunks.text: Skip to main contentWatch LiveWatch LiveLiveDashboardDashboardDashboardenEnglish (United States)SpanishSearchMenuJune 3, 2026The Gospel of JohnI Have Overcome The WorldAaron CapitoAbout the SeriesAaron continued the group's walk through the Gospel of John, moving toward the story of the cross. This week's passage sits just before the prayer in John 17 the group studied recently. Jesus is still with His disciples, preparing them for what's about to happen.The message opened by comparing how Jesus taught to Yoda from Star Wars: introduced as strange and hard to follow at first, but unmistakably clear the moment things got serious. Jesus had spoken to His disciples in figures of speech up to this point. Now He tells them plainly what's coming.Passages: John 16:25-33What Was TaughtJesus promises a restored relationship with the FatherJesus tells His disciples that the time is coming when He'll stop speaking in figures of speech, expressive language not meant to be taken literally, and speak to them plainly about the Father. He says that in that day, they'll be able to approach the Father directly in His name.The point drawn from this: something was about to change in how people relate to God. Once Jesus died and rose again, the war between a holy God and sinful people would be over, and access to the Father would be restored. That's the reality behind praying "in Jesus's name." Romans 8:34 was brought in here too, where Paul says Christ is seated at the Father's right hand, interceding for us even now. The challenge to students: do you actually live like you can bring your troubles to God, or do you just say you believe that?Understanding isn't the same as trustingWhen Jesus speaks plainly, His disciples respond that now they finally understand and believe. It's a familiar posture: people often want God to reveal Himself clearly and completely before they'll commit to Him. But Jesus doesn't accept their claim at face value. He predicts that within hours, they'll scatter and abandon Him, proving they didn't understand as fully as they thought.Two things were highlighted about Jesus's coming death: it wasn't a sign that God had abandoned Him, and it wasn't a setback. It was the plan all along. The disciples had no real reason to run.Take heart, because Jesus has overcome the worldJesus tells His disciples plainly why He's told them all this: so that they can have peace. He promises they'll have trouble in this world, but tells them to take heart, because He has already overcome the world. The original word behind "take heart" carries the sense of staying courageous and not giving up, even when things are hard.Two movie comparisons were used to illustrate that kind of courage: Marlin in Finding Nemo, who can't control the danger around him but keeps moving forward anyway, and Miles in Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, who doesn't wait until he feels ready before taking the leap. The closing challenge to students: live like Christ has already won, because the trouble we face now doesn't come close to outweighing the joy of following Him.Talk About It at HomeThese are the questions the group discussed:Why do you think people sometimes want God to explain everything immediately instead of trusting Him through the process?When something stressful happens in your life, who is the first person you usually go to? Why do you think we often go to everyone else before we go to God?Why do you think Jesus knew the disciples would fail Him and run away, yet He still loved them and continued teaching them?Is there a situation in your life right now where you need to hear Jesus say, "Take heart"? What makes that situation difficult?A few easier openers if you want to start smaller:What's something you needed courage for recently, even in a small way?Who do you usually call first when something goes wrong? What would it look like to pray first instead?Is there a promise or truth you know in your head but don't always live like you believe?What's one thing that's stressing you out this week?‍

chunks.title: Landmark Church
chunks.text: Skip to main contentWatch LiveWatch LiveLiveDashboardDashboardDashboardenEnglish (United States)SpanishSearchMenuJuly 29, 2026The Gospel of JohnThe High Priestly Prayer Part 2Liam HungateAbout the SeriesStudents are still working through the Gospel of John, moving toward the story of the cross. This week's teaching, led by Liam, continued the study of John 17, the long prayer Jesus prayed with His disciples just hours before His arrest. It picks up where Aaron left off before camp.In the first part of the prayer, Jesus focused on Heaven rather than His own coming suffering, fully committed Himself to God's will, and asked God to protect His disciples' faith after His death. This week's verses continue that same theme: even in His final hours, Jesus's prayer was entirely about others, not Himself.Passages: John 17:13-26What Was TaughtJesus prayed for real joy, not just happinessLiam drew a line between happiness and joy. Happiness rises and falls with your day. Joy is a steady confidence that you are safe in God's hands no matter what your circumstances look like, on the mountaintop or in the valley. Jesus prayed that His disciples would have this kind of full joy even on the worst night of His life, which means He wants that same joy for us too.Jesus prayed for protection, not an easy lifeJesus told His disciples plainly that the world would hate them the way it hated Him. Following Jesus was never promised to be easy. But Liam pointed out what Jesus did not pray: He never asked God to remove His disciples from a hard world. He asked God to protect them while they stayed in it. We're called to be in the world without being shaped by it, and joy was never about avoiding hard things. It's about having something solid underneath you while hard things happen.Jesus prayed for His people to be set apart by truthJesus asked God to sanctify His disciples, meaning to set them apart for His purposes, through the truth of His Word. Liam explained that reading, understanding, and applying Scripture is what protects believers from being shaped by the world around them. Jesus then prayed that His own holiness would benefit His people, not stay contained to Himself, which Liam pointed to as the heart of Christ: willing to give up everything for those who believe in Him.Jesus prayed for unity among all believersAt this point in the prayer, Jesus shifts from praying for the twelve disciples in the room to praying for every believer who would ever come to know Him, including students in the room tonight. He prayed for unity among all of them, modeled on the unity of the Trinity. Liam described what that unity actually looks like: not standing out or seeking attention, but building others up and putting others first. How believers treat each other, at church, at school, in friend groups, is meant to be visible proof to the world of what God's love looks like.Jesus prayed for eternity, and for His presence with us nowJesus prayed that His people would eventually be with Him forever, and that eternity would center on His glory, meaning we won't run out of reasons to be amazed by Him. Even knowing the cross was coming, Jesus still called God righteous, meaning fully good and right. Liam pointed out that Jesus's coming pain didn't change how good God is. Jesus's last request in the prayer was to be present with His people, something Liam said is fulfilled right now through the Holy Spirit living in every believer.To open the message, Liam compared this prayer to a moment from the movie Avengers: Endgame, when Tony Stark, in his final seconds, doesn't say anything about his pain or fear. He simply tells his wife he loves her. Liam's point: in someone's true last moments, whatever comes out reflects what they actually care about most. Jesus's last recorded prayer before His arrest was entirely about us. He prayed for our joy, our protection, our holiness, our unity, and that we would be with Him forever.Talk About It at HomeThese are the questions the group discussed:Jesus said the world would hate His followers. Has that ever actually happened to you, even in a small way, like getting made fun of, left out, or feeling weird for your faith? What happened?Jesus prayed that God would set us apart and make us different from the world through His truth. What's one thing you do every week (a show, an app, a habit, even certain friends) that makes it harder for you to actually look different from everyone else?Jesus prayed specifically for unity among believers. Is there anyone (at school, in a friend group, even in this room) that you've been keeping distance from or have tension with? What's one real step you could take this week toward unity with them?A few easier openers if you want to start smaller:What's the difference between being happy and having a deeper sense of peace, even on a bad day?Has anyone ever seen how you act at church versus how you act at school? Would they look the same?What's one habit or app that shapes how you think more than you'd like it to?Is there someone you could reach out to this week just to check in or make things right?‍

# About this AI assistant

Landmark Church's website offers an AI-powered answer summary above search
results. (Note: the church is always called "Landmark Church" or "Landmark",
never "The Landmark Church".) It answers from the church's website, the church's internal knowledge
base, the ESV Bible, and a short list of trusted ministries approved by
Landmark's leadership (GotQuestions.org and John Piper's content at
DesiringGod.org for quotable material; Enduring Word, Answers in Genesis, and
Logos as link-only recommendations).

It is a starting point, not a substitute for Scripture, the local church, or a
pastor. Anyone with a personal or urgent need should contact the church
directly through the care request form.

chunks.title: AI Search Feature: Changelog & Decisions
chunks.text:
# AI Search Feature: Changelog & Decisions

Internal record of how the Landmark AI answer feature works, why it was built
this way, and every change made to it. Maintained by Claude; updated on each
change and each scheduled feedback review.

## How it works (current architecture)

- Widget (`widget.js`) is embedded via page-level custom code on the Search
  Results page only; it auto-updates from Vercel with no Webflow publish.
- `/api/ask` answers questions from: (1) the crawled website index,
  (2) `content/brain/*.md`, (3) ESV Scripture via Crossway's API, and
  (4) web search restricted to approved ministry domains.
- Copyright rules: GotQuestions quotable ≤200 words with credit; Desiring God
  Piper-only with exact attribution line; Enduring Word / Answers in Genesis /
  Logos link-only. ESV quotes carry the "ESV" notice.
- Crisis questions bypass AI and show the Church Center care form + 988.
- Model: claude-sonnet-5 (env `ANSWER_MODEL` overrides), no extended thinking,
  low effort, answers ≤225 words. Repeated questions served from a shared
  6-hour cache. Low-confidence answers are hidden from visitors (honesty rule).
- Questions log to the "AI Search Questions" Monday board (18420369585);
  visitor feedback logs to "AI Answer Feedback" (18420598077).

## Update policy (agreed with Eric, Jul 2026)

chunks.title: AI Search Feature: Changelog & Decisions
chunks.text:
- Recurring review of the feedback board roughly every 2 weeks: triage items,
  fix bugs / tighten answers / correct info / small in-feature improvements,
  set each item's Triage status, and record changes here.
- Changes that overhaul or materially alter the feature require an email
  summary to creative@thelandmark.church BEFORE pushing, and wait for approval.
- Small fixes ship directly.

## Changelog

### 2026-08-20: Live speaker schedule
- Added a live data source: the "Speaker Schedule" Monday board (18427433958,
  Creative Team workspace; columns Name, Series, Service Date, Service Day).
  When a question is about who is speaking/preaching and when (see
  isSpeakerQuery in `lib/speakers.ts`), the board is fetched live and injected
  as authoritative context with today's date, so "who is preaching this Sunday?"
  stays current as the board is updated. Uses the same MONDAY_API_TOKEN.
- These questions bypass the answer cache (they are date-relative) and skip web
  search. The schedule is internal, so the model is told not to cite a source
  URL for it. Cache key bumped to v12. Approved by Eric (live vs static choice).
- Board id overridable via env MONDAY_SPEAKER_BOARD_ID.

chunks.title: AI Search Feature: Changelog & Decisions
chunks.text:
### 2026-07-02: Initial build
- Three-tier RAG answer engine, Webflow widget, ESV tool, restricted web
  search, crisis escalation, Monday question logging, copyright guardrails.
- Copyright research: verified policies of GotQuestions, Desiring God,
  Enduring Word, Answers in Genesis, ESV API. AiG kept link-only per Eric.

### 2026-07-02: Launch polish
- Lumos-token styling (Gotham, brand-500, radius/shadow matching site cards),
  brand-100 light blue card background for visual distinction.
- No em dashes, no AI-filler style rules; 6-line clamp with See more.
- Speed: Sonnet model, batched ESV fetches, shared answer cache, Monday
  logging moved after response. Cold ~10-15s, repeats ~0.5s.
- Widget scoped to the search results page only (?query= trigger).

### 2026-07-05: Reliability fix
- Root-caused a multi-day outage: the Webflow-registered script pinned an
  integrity hash that drifted from the deployed widget.js. Replaced with a
  plain script tag in the Search page's custom code; widget now updates
  automatically on deploy with nothing to drift.

chunks.title: AI Search Feature: Changelog & Decisions
chunks.text:
### 2026-07-05: Actions, feedback loop
- Action links: up to 2 CTAs per answer linking the specific CMS page;
  thumbnail cards (og:image) for sermons/series/podcasts, secondary outline
  buttons beneath thumbnails, primary buttons otherwise. Homepage links
  resolve to the specific page by title lookup; URLs deduped.
- Answers lengthened to ≤225 words; Collapse/Show toggle (non-persistent)
  replaced Hide; link hovers to dark-700.
- "Give Feedback" inline form on the card → AI Answer Feedback Monday board.
- This changelog created; recurring feedback-review schedule established.

chunks.title: AI Search Feature: Changelog & Decisions
chunks.text:
### 2026-07-14: Speed, streamed answers
- Answers now stream token-by-token so the first words appear in ~1-2s instead
  of waiting the full generation. New `POST /api/ask/stream` (newline-delimited
  JSON events); the widget reads it and types the answer in live, then the
  final "done" event re-renders the authoritative, scrubbed result with
  sources/actions. The widget falls back to the plain `/api/ask` JSON endpoint
  on any streaming error, so the card never fails to appear.
- Caching preserved through streaming via AsyncLocalStorage: cache hits still
  return instantly, misses stream live. The answer schema now lists escalate
  and confidence before answer so the low-confidence "hide" rule is applied
  before any text is shown (no flash-then-remove).
- Web search is now only attached when local retrieval is thin (few matching
  chunks), since it is the biggest source of tail latency and most church-info
  questions are fully covered by the site/brain. Tunable via env
  (WEB_SEARCH_MAX_CHUNKS, WEB_SEARCH_ALWAYS).
- Cache key bumped to v11. Optional follow-up: a cron pinger to keep the
  function warm (skipped for now; depends on the Vercel plan's cron limits).
- Latency findings (measured live): cache hits ~0.3-0.5s. Cold/uncached
  answers stream first text at ~3-7s and finish at ~10-16s (more when a
  theological question triggers web search). Streaming roughly halves the
  perceived wait, but a hard 5-6s total is not reachable on Sonnet: the cost
  is model generation plus serverless variance, not a tunable knob (tested:
  reasoning effort and the json_schema grammar are not the driver; Haiku 4.5
  errors in this pipeline). Getting reliably under ~6s would mean a faster
  model (quality tradeoff) or a warm-instance setup, which is Eric's call.

chunks.title: AI Search Feature: Changelog & Decisions
chunks.text:
### 2026-07-12: Correct Sunday gathering times (8:30am / 10:30am)
- Sunday times were also stale on the site ("9:00am & 11:00am"); correct
  times are 8:30am and 10:30am (Eric). Updated the brain facts file and the
  prompt override. Cache key bumped to v10; index refreshed.

### 2026-07-12: Correct Wednesday gathering time (6:30pm)
- The AI answered "Wednesday at 6:00pm" for the main gathering; the correct
  time is 6:30pm (Eric). Root cause: stale website content, archived sermon
  posts and YouTube livestream descriptions still list "Wednesday at 6:00pm",
  and the 6:00pm youth-ministry times, so the index carries conflicting times.
- Fix: added `service-times-and-facts.md` to the brain as the authoritative
  source for times/locations, and a prompt rule that the BRAIN wins over the
  WEBSITE on concrete facts (times can go stale on old posts). Main Wednesday
  gathering is 6:30pm; 6:00pm belongs to Jr. High (Wed) and Sr. High (Sun)
  youth. Cache key bumped to v9; index refreshed.

### 2026-07-06: Naming convention
- The church is referred to as "Landmark Church" or "Landmark", never
  "The Landmark Church" (Eric). Enforced three ways: prompt style rule,
  server-side scrub of the answer text (crawled page titles still use the
  old form, so the model sees it in context), and a fix in the brain doc.
- Answer cache key bumped to v8 so stale phrasings expire immediately.

chunks.title: AI Search Feature: Changelog & Decisions
chunks.text:
### 2026-07-05: Feedback-driven polish (Eric's review)
- Actions are strictly relevance-gated: empty unless the question is about
  something with its own page; generic homepage links dropped (never
  relabeled/rewritten, fixing a label/URL mismatch); thumbnails limited to
  real content paths (sermons, series, notes, podcast, blog, events, team,

chunks.title: Truth Over Trend (Matthew Maher)
chunks.text:
# Truth Over Trend (Matthew Maher)

Truth Over Trend is Matthew Maher's personal platform. Its website is
https://www.truthovertrend.com/.

When someone asks about Truth Over Trend, or about Matthew Maher's personal
platform, ministry, or website, point them to the site and share the link:
https://www.truthovertrend.com/. It is appropriate to recommend and link it
(for example as a further-study / "go deeper" link).

Truth Over Trend is Matthew Maher's own platform, separate from Landmark
Church's website.
